### MXR-080-0437 — Contrastive projection is not a probability-distribution leaf

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/models/mixture_density.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 463–585
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`ProjectionLeaf.log_density(x,y)` depends on every other row in the current
batch. The same pair changes score when unrelated pairs are added, and every
single-row call returns exactly zero regardless of whether the pair matches.
It therefore cannot be normalized or satisfy the per-observation scorer used
by mixtures/HMMs/EM, despite being wrapped as that distribution type.

Expose a separate batch-contrastive training objective/ranker, not a
probability-distribution leaf.

### MXR-080-0438 — Responsibility-weighted InfoNCE weights the wrong computation

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/models/mixture_density.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 288–326 and 563–573
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The estimator multiplies only each row’s final symmetric InfoNCE score by its
responsibility. But each sample also acts as a negative in every other row;
those cross-row contributions are controlled by other samples’ weights. This
is neither an EM component Q-function nor a coherently weighted contrastive
objective.

Define a separate weighted contrastive loss with explicit anchor/negative
measure semantics.

### MXR-080-0443 — “Dense exact” optimizer state always loses float64 precision

### MXR-080-0444 — CompressedAdam stores moments in unsafe parameter precision

- **Severity:** Critical

- **State:** Source-confirmed

Moments are decompressed into `p.dtype`, so fp16/bf16 parameters accumulate

module. Hyperparameters are not validated, sparse gradients are not rejected,
and the custom Python compression object in `optimizer.state` is not a
portable tensor-only checkpoint.

### MXR-080-0445 — Selective recompute policy is effectively all-or-nothing

### MXR-080-0446 — Merged-block Jacobian correction is detached from training

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/models/coarsening.py`

- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The entire directional-derivative correction is computed under
`torch.no_grad()`. Hybrid fine-tuning of a merged block therefore ignores how
that term depends on input and both component blocks; forward behavior and
training gradients describe different functions.

### MXR-080-0447 — The numerical JVP is not a directional derivative of attention

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/models/coarsening.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 150–168
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The code normalizes `f(x)` and chooses epsilon independently per token. A
self-attention output at one token depends on perturbations to every token, so
using different per-token scales and then multiplying each output by only its
local norm is not `Dg(x)[f(x)]`. The Taylor merge’s core mathematical claim is
false for the very attention blocks it targets.

Use a single scalar perturbation of the full input direction and validate the
approximation against autograd-compatible reference layers.

### MXR-080-0448 — Depth “compression” performs more block work and retains both blocks

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/models/coarsening.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 115–198 and 604–713
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

A merged entry retains both full original blocks. Its forward evaluates
`f(x)`, `g(x)`, `g(x+eps v)`, and `g(x-eps v)` sequentially—roughly four block
branches versus the original two. One low-rank matrix in `block_a` may later be
narrowed, but the advertised depth cut is not a latency/compute or meaningful
parameter reduction.

Report actual parameters, FLOPs, memory, and latency; do not equate one
`ModuleList` entry with compression.

### MXR-080-0449 — Post-hoc low-rank error is excluded from the coarsening budget

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

After depth merges pass the KL budget/trust region, the returned blocks are
further approximated by low-rank projection. That error is deliberately not
propagated into `total_kl`, `within_budget`, or any accept/reject decision.
The returned model can therefore exceed the caller’s declared budget while
reporting `within_budget=True`.

Budget every transformation against the final executable model, with rollback
when the aggregate bound is exceeded.

### MXR-080-0475 — Upper-truncated right-censoring uses the wrong likelihood

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/ppl/survival.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 42–64
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

For a right-censored observation `c` in a finite truncation window `[L,U]`, the
code uses `S(c)/(F(U)-F(L))`. The conditional probability is
`(F(U)-F(c))/(F(U)-F(L))`. A uniform `[0,1]` probe with `c=.75,U=.8` returned
`-1.16315` instead of `log(.05/.8) = -2.77259`.

Implement censoring probabilities relative to both truncation endpoints and
test all censor/truncation combinations analytically.

No shape check couples `time` and `event`; `zip(t, ev)` silently omitted two of
three observations in a direct probe. Arbitrary numeric/string labels are cast
to bool, and truncation bounds or observed locations are not checked against
the window.

Require aligned one-dimensional arrays, exact binary event indicators, finite
times, ordered bounds, and observations consistent with truncation.

### MXR-080-0484 — Admixture can use an unbound local and records a stale objective

### MXR-080-0491 — Split R-hat omits the folded diagnostic needed to detect scale mismatch

### MXR-080-0502 — `predict_mean` is not the posterior mean it claims to be

- **Severity:** Critical

### MXR-080-0510 — Refitting a VMP graph double-counts every observation

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/ppl/vmp.py`
- **Lines at initial revision:** 252–349
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each `Graph.fit` call wires new message closures into persistent node inboxes
without clearing the old ones. A Normal prior plus one observation at 10 had

accepts asserted parent hashes as proof of descent. Serving can mask internal
user errors as compatibility retries.

Use atomic durable writes, immutable authenticated lineage, and one
materialized/replayable fit request.

### MXR-080-0597 — Bayesian streaming cannot cold-start and its forgetting mode discounts the wrong evidence

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Lines at initial revision:** 1581–1685
- **State:** Reproduced

Cold `update(data=...)` calls `_encode` while `self.model is None`, immediately
raising `AttributeError`. Forgetting scales only the incoming batch before
carrying the old posterior, so it discounts new evidence rather than decaying
old evidence. `reset()` leaves the carried posterior estimator in place, so a
new run is not fresh, and NaN schedules pass inequality checks.

statistics/prior, and restore the original estimator on reset.

### MXR-080-0600 — The active-causal benchmark leaks orientation through observational marginals

### MXR-080-0602 — Streaming context keys are repeatedly rotated and the GPU path is device-inconsistent

The cache stores keys after RoPE, then concatenates them with raw keys on the
next call and applies RoPE to the entire concatenation again. Older keys are
therefore rotated repeatedly. RoPE frequencies are created on CPU, so CUDA
positions fail, and non-positive windows trigger empty masks or Python's
`-0` full-slice behavior. Cache layout, absolute positions, devices, even head
dimensions, and positive windows need explicit invariants.

### MXR-080-0608 — Cluster-tail KV compression duplicates unrelated tokens

### MXR-080-0611 — Moment-closure attention counts new observations twice and overlaps near and far memory

### MXR-080-0612 — The advertised mixture Wasserstein barycenter is an order-dependent matching heuristic

### MXR-080-0622 — Summary-tree memory is linear, duplicated, and temporarily incomplete

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/summary_tree.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 28–598
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

All finalized children and parents remain attendable, so state and far
attention grow linearly rather than `O(log N)`, with the same leaves represented
at every level. After 16 evictions, the probe found 15 far nodes whose
represented leaf mass totaled 64. Pending leaves and current-chunk evictions
are temporarily invisible, making outputs chunk-dependent, while far queries
mix RoPE-encoded queries with unrotated keys. Enforce a non-overlapping
frontier and explicit pending state.

### MXR-080-0623 — Tensor-network probabilities silently change the query event

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/tensor_network.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–138
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Short sequences are treated as marginals and extra symbols are ignored without
an explicit event type. A two-site product network returned `0.5` for a
one-symbol “full” probability. Out-of-range evidence produced a conditional
vector `[1, 1]` summing to two, and query variables already in evidence are
overwritten. Complex Born-machine contractions use transpose/square instead of
conjugate transpose/absolute square. Validate event dimensions and complex
semantics.

### MXR-080-0624 — Tensor/pipeline/context parallel utilities do not implement trainable distributed semantics

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/tensor_pipeline_context_parallel.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 28–478
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Tensor-parallel shards are detached tensors, not parameters or modules, so
optimizers cannot update them. Pipeline execution wraps every stage in
`no_grad`, despite trainer/GPipe framing. CPU index tensors break CUDA
sharding, `zip` truncates missing shards, and context parallelism all-gathers
full K/V on each rank while claiming it never materializes the full sequence.
Implement end-to-end gradient, ownership, collective, and memory invariants.

### MXR-080-0625 — Tying discovery mutates models before acceptance and can report false parity

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/tying_discovery.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 25–314
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Resampled scalar profiles can be equal for distinct parameter multisets, so
zero profile distance does not prove permutation equivalence. Proposals may
pair incompatible shapes, while `apply_tie` mutates parameters before the
receipt is accepted, has no rollback, leaves the model in evaluation mode, and
invalidates optimizer references. Relative error returns zero whenever the
baseline norm is zero, even if output changed. Make proposals non-mutating and
parity transactional.

### MXR-080-0626 — Unlearning certification rereads the data it claims was deleted

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/unlearning.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 19–152
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Invalid exclusion IDs are ignored but still listed in the certificate.
Certification recomputes from every raw shard, including excluded data, so it
does not verify deletion after the data is unavailable. It can also certify
one-step deterministic equality for iterative latent estimators it does not
identify or refuse. The JSON/repr fingerprint is not bitwise model state.
Define a threat model and certificate that operates from retained commitments,
not deleted raw records.

### MXR-080-0627 — Gaussian mutual information turns invalid correlation into a plausible result

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/v_information.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–94
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Correlations outside `[-1, 1]` are clipped rather than rejected, so `rho=2`
becomes a large finite mutual-information estimate. Data shapes, holdout
sizes, degrees, and non-finite values are unchecked, and a single held-out
split is described as the best achievable predictive value without
uncertainty. Reject invalid distributions and distinguish an estimator from a
population optimum.

### MXR-080-0628 — Wake/sleep abstraction invents fragments absent from the solutions

### MXR-080-0630 — The typed compiler fabricates exact and monotone contracts from names and defaults

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/compiler.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 31–599
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

An arbitrary estimator defaults to exact closed form, latent sequential/GEM
patterns can be marked exact and monotone-certified, and an unrecognized
objective defaults to MLE-compatible. Invalid declared enums are ignored and
guessed, while any “exact” update automatically receives a monotonicity
certificate without an acceptance proof. The supposedly side-effect-free
compiler calls factories and estimator hooks. Require explicit, validated
contracts and return `UNKNOWN` when evidence is absent.

### MXR-080-0631 — Empty validation evidence passes both acceptance and replay

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/acceptance.py` and `replay.py`

`all()` over zero negative-control receipts marks
`local-negative-controls` passed (`passed=0/0`), and a replay report with zero
steps reports `matched=True`. Bitwise replay can also compare receipts without
requiring state fingerprints. The bounded probes reproduced both outcomes.

empty replay as not run.

### MXR-080-0633 — Boundary sequence identity collides across runs and models

The stream key omits run and model identity, so otherwise identical dependency

### MXR-080-0634 — An “exact” compression contract permits lossy transforms

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/compression.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 22–250
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`contract.exact` still permits low-rank and weighted-sketch compression;
merge-law metadata is incorrectly treated as permission to approximate.
Error-feedback residual is advanced before delivery/commit acknowledgement, so
a dropped message loses the correction. Integer payloads can cast low-rank
factors back to integers. Separate exact serialization from approximation and
commit residual state only after acknowledged application.

### MXR-080-0635 — Active-context bounds can be bypassed with zero-token nodes

### MXR-080-0636 — Context adapters can mutate the live graph outside their declared result

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/context_execution.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 22–199
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Adapters receive the mutable graph itself. A probe added an undeclared node
inside an adapter, returned an empty action result, and still advanced the
graph version; the receipt listed no output. External effects have no
exactly-once/version precondition, graph rollback cannot roll them back, and
receipt construction may fail after graph commit. Pass an immutable snapshot
and apply a validated transaction result atomically.

### MXR-080-0637 — “Frozen” context nodes have mutable, incomplete identity

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/context_ir.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 78–187 and 217–414
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The frozen dataclass contains a mutable metadata dictionary. Mutating the
caller's dictionary changes `content_hash` without a graph version increment.
Conversely, confidence is omitted from the hash, so two same-ID nodes with
different confidence are accepted as idempotent. Verification replacement
also erases prior status rather than retaining an evidence history. Deep-freeze
all identity data and version every evidentiary transition.

### MXR-080-0638 — Required support bundles bypass admission and prompt token accounting

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/context_materializer.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 62–218
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

A required admissible claim adds its entire support bundle without checking
whether each support member was admitted. The probe materialized an unverified
generated node that remained explicitly listed in `excluded`. Rendered
provenance/status headers also consume tokens absent from `node.token_count`,
so the “hard” prompt budget is not hard, and attended tokens are a `min`
label rather than a measured subset. Validate every bundle member and tokenize
the final rendered prompt.

### MXR-080-0639 — Expected-cost scheduling cannot enforce hard action budgets

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `typed_runtime/context_runtime.py` and `context_scheduler.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `context_runtime.py` 20–145; `context_scheduler.py` 20–219
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

Budget admission uses expected costs only; an action may exceed the hard actual
budget and remain committed. Negative expected monetary costs increase value
and evade limits, NaN budget/spend comparisons fail open, and zero-sample gain
evidence is treated as a certain default. Max-iteration termination fabricates
a stop receipt without an actual decision. Reserve worst-case resources and
reject/roll back over-budget execution.

`CostEstimate` and related numeric contracts validate signs with comparisons

### MXR-080-0641 — Distributed exactness and injected-fault receipts overstate what occurred

- **Severity:** High

Distributed receipts copy `contract.exact` into an exactness claim without

stale-version fault at version zero clamps back to zero, so it performs no

determinism/error and require each fault to demonstrate a state transition.

### MXR-080-0642 — Geometry routing misses shared parameters and trusts incomplete evidence

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/geometry.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 25–523
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

PyTorch `named_parameters()` removes duplicates by default, so shared
parameters are never detected and shared-group routing is absent. Evidence
matching ignores `target_name`; missing evidence retains a proposed route
rather than failing closed. Curvature transforms do not consistently reject
indefinite or non-finite factors and cached factors can be stale. Enumerate
aliases explicitly and bind evidence to parameter identity and model version.

### MXR-080-0643 — Graph-memory bounds trust forgeable counts and omit boundary identity

- **Severity:** High

Graph memory trusts a caller-supplied partition token count instead of
recomputing it, so cache bounds can be bypassed. Boundary edges are omitted
from partition hashes, duplicate graph edges are accepted, and prefetch/cache
updates are not atomic. Derive resource counts and identity from canonical
content and make publication transactional.

### MXR-080-0644 — Staleness correction receipts are not bound to the correction applied

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `typed_runtime/hierarchical.py` and `staleness.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `hierarchical.py` 20–166; `staleness.py` 20–229

A `correction_fingerprint` is recorded but never compared with the payload
returned by the correction provider. Stale payloads can then be relabeled at
the current version after only exponential scaling; a zero decay leaves them
unchanged. Recompute and verify correction identity and distinguish a
statistical approximation from an exact rebase.

### MXR-080-0645 — Proposal merging permits duplicate data application and discards contract fields

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/proposal.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 25–393
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The same shard/data contribution can be proposed twice under different
proposal IDs and merged twice. Merge compatibility omits precision, rollback,
error, and other execution-contract fields, while non-finite telemetry passes
validation. Floating addition is called exact without an ordering/error
contract, and integer merges may overflow. Bind proposals to unique data
contribution IDs and compare the full execution contract.

### MXR-080-0646 — Update scheduling spends zero budget and advances fairness before execution

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/scheduler.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 75–349
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

With `budget_fraction=0`, the first eligible node is still selected because
the budget check applies only after `selected` is non-empty. Gain evidence is
not bound to model version and can remain stale indefinitely. Fairness state
advances when work is scheduled, not committed, so failed work resets
starvation and counts as service. Enforce the budget for the first item and
advance clocks from terminal receipts.

### MXR-080-0647 — Structured execution and topology planning report resources they did not enforce

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `structured_execution.py` 20–166; `topology.py` 20–414

`num_workers=0` is silently replaced with a device-derived count, workers may

planner ignores declared decomposition axes and may choose undeclared
partition/merge semantics. Cross-island proposal mode is never used,
unsharded placement skips capacity checks, and model hashes can fall back to
unstable string representations. Plan only declared axes and verify actual

### MXR-080-0648 — Transaction identity and monotonicity gates can be bypassed

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/experimental/typed_runtime/transaction.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 25–477
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The coordinator has no configured run/model identity, so any proposal with a
matching node/version can enter. One surrogate proposal in a batch disables

### MXR-080-0649 — Typed-runtime validation and public inventory certify an incomplete contract

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `typed_runtime/validation.py`, `typed_runtime/__init__.py`, `typed_runtime/local.py`, and `typed_runtime/planner.py`

Validation appears strict only because compiler defaults avoid `UNKNOWN`;
therefore inferred false exactness passes as positive assurance. The package
inventory omits implemented contract types and describes guarantees that the
execution paths do not establish. Local/planner routes inherit compiler

publish a generated stable/experimental capability manifest.

### MXR-080-0650 — Artifact replacement has an unrecovered crash window and no content integrity

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/artifact.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 44–112 and 248–387
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Updating an artifact renames the old directory away before installing the new
one. A process or machine failure between those two renames leaves the
canonical path absent; the randomly named backup is never discovered on
startup. Manifests also contain no digest binding the payload, adapter, and
configuration, so external corruption or a mismatched copied file is not
detected before load. Publish through a recoverable generation pointer or add
startup recovery, and verify a canonical manifest/payload digest.

### MXR-080-0651 — Classifier adapters accept malformed geometry and break device/state contracts

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/model.py` and `mixle/task/capacity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `model.py` 29–209; `capacity.py` 32–75
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Hash dimensions, n-gram orders, label sets, record widths, and embedding-vector
dimensions are not validated. Torch features are always created on CPU, so a
GPU-loaded model fails, and inference calls `eval()` without restoring the
caller's training state. Empty probability batches fail after the logits path
explicitly accepts them. Validate construction invariants, place tensors on
the module device, and restore the prior mode.

### MXR-080-0652 — Impossible structured evidence is converted into a confident ordinary label

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/model.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 232–301
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Broad exception handling converts every failed label score to `-inf`.
`proba_batch()` then replaces an all-impossible row with a uniform
distribution, while `predict_batch()` applies `argmax` directly to the
all-`-inf` row and returns the first label. Unsupported evidence is therefore
silently changed into a normal prediction despite the “exact posterior”
contract. Preserve an explicit impossible/abstain state and distinguish
support errors from internal model failures.

### MXR-080-0653 — LLM adapters silently fabricate labels and discard recoverable JSON

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/llm.py` and `mixle/task/design.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `llm.py` 57–182; `design.py` 120–173
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

An unrecognized or ambiguous free-text classification is mapped to the first
label. Substring matching is order-dependent, and an empty label list crashes.
The JSON scanners count braces inside strings, stop after the first malformed
object, and either return `{}` or abandon later valid JSON. HTTP responses,
sizes, and schemas are trusted by indexing. Return a typed parse failure that
forces escalation, use a real streaming JSON decoder, and validate transport
and response contracts.

### MXR-080-0654 — Function-calling gates reject valid calls and can never serve argless tools

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/toolcall.py`, `mixle/task/plan.py`, and `mixle/task/sft_plan.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `toolcall.py` 25–199; `plan.py` 44–91; `sft_plan.py` 90–153
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Required arguments are checked with truthiness, so valid `0`, `False`, empty
strings, and empty collections are treated as missing. Argless tools are
deliberately given no extractor, but `try_local()` requires membership in the
extractor map, so the probe showed a confident argless `ping` call always
escalating. Duplicate tool names silently overwrite specifications. Validate
presence separately from value semantics and make selection sufficient for a
declared argless tool.

### MXR-080-0655 — Trace ingestion loses executions and the public conversion path is unimplemented

- **Severity:** High

Trace indexes overwrite repeated request strings, malformed files are silently
skipped without a failure ledger, and malformed tool inputs can abort an

### MXR-080-0656 — Classification calibration cannot cover unseen labels and accepts invalid calibration math

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/calibrate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–164
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

A true calibration label absent from the model label set receives probability
zero, but no future prediction set can contain that label, so the stated label
coverage is impossible. Input/label lengths, non-empty data, finite
probabilities, alpha, and quantile ranks are incompletely checked, and JSON
serialization maps both NaN and negative infinity to positive infinity,
hiding corruption. Reject unknown support and enforce finite split-conformal
preconditions before storing a threshold.

### MXR-080-0657 — Generative “conformal” sets have no valid exchangeable label space

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/calibrated_generator.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–172
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Calibration and serving use newly sampled, prompt-specific candidate strings;
candidate identities and even set cardinality change from example to example.
Summing probability assigned to multiple strings accepted by an arbitrary
`is_correct` predicate is not the true-label nonconformity score used by label
conditional conformal prediction. Consequently a singleton carries no stated
`1-alpha` correctness guarantee. Replace this claim with a valid risk-control
construction over a fixed measurable outcome, or report empirical abstention
without coverage language.

### MXR-080-0658 — Router accounting omits every attempted tier before the answer

- **State:** Reproduced

The router increments cost only for the tier that answers. A request that paid
for tiers costing 1 and 2 before the second answered was reported as costing
2 rather than 3. Failed tier calls are also free in the receipt. Costs,
ordering, uniqueness, finiteness, and non-negativity are not enforced, so
reported savings can be fictitious. Record all attempted work and validate the
entire ordered cost model.

### MXR-080-0659 — Harvest resolution selects and certifies a new tier on the same examples

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/router.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 169–311
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`resolve_from_harvest()` trains/calibrates the new tier and decides whether its
escalation drop is acceptable using a split from the same adaptively harvested
set. There is no independent post-selection evaluation, and the accepted
model is immediately inserted. The before rate of one is definitional rather
than a generalization baseline. Reserve untouched traffic or use a valid
sequential evaluation protocol before changing the serving stack.

### MXR-080-0660 — Route economics accepts impossible costs and optimizes calibration on its own evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/economics.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–238
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Negative/non-finite costs, volume, escalation probabilities, and constraints
can flow into break-even and recommendation arithmetic. The local-only route
is withheld except at a zero-escalation constraint even though its semantics
would force ambiguous requests to be guessed. `select_alpha_for_cost()` tries
multiple alphas on one calibration set and returns the cheapest, invalidating
the unadjusted conformal claim. Validate the economic domain and separate
policy selection from coverage certification.

### MXR-080-0661 — Active acquisition trusts invalid probabilities and does not account for all labels purchased

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/acquire.py` and `mixle/task/active.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `acquire.py` 20–191; `active.py` 20–188
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Ensemble probabilities and weights are not checked for shape, normalization,
finiteness, or positivity; NaN acquisition scores can sort to the front, and
the weighted-disagreement path ignores its weights. Active distillation omits
validation-teacher calls from its labeling budget, accepts invalid budgets and
seeds, and fixes the class universe from the initial seed so later labels
cannot be learned. Enforce probability contracts and count every teacher
query in the same budget ledger.

### MXR-080-0662 — Density and disagreement thresholds are calibrated on their fitting data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/density.py`, `mixle/task/disagreement.py`, and `mixle/task/distill.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `density.py` 20–85; `disagreement.py` 20–115; `distill.py` 568–590
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Direct fit paths estimate a density or disagreement model and set its
acceptance threshold on those same examples. The resulting floor is
optimistically biased and does not have the implied held-out false-escalation
behavior. Empty data, invalid alpha, non-finite scores, and teacher-length
mismatches are also not consistently rejected. Require a disjoint calibration
split and record its identity.

### MXR-080-0663 — Reloading an unverified solution silently promotes it

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/solve.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 95–187 and 249–309
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`Solution.save()` permits a non-promoted solution, but `Solution.load()` sets
`promoted=True` unconditionally rather than restoring and checking the saved
verification state. A model explicitly rejected before serialization can
therefore become locally serveable after a restart. Persist immutable
promotion evidence and fail closed unless that exact artifact passed it.

### MXR-080-0664 — Adaptive solution improvement repeatedly spends the same calibration guarantee

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/solve.py`, `mixle/task/regress.py`, `mixle/task/multilabel.py`, and `mixle/task/structured_out.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `solve.py` 189–407; `regress.py` 179–350; `multilabel.py` 157–268; `structured_out.py` 177–256
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Candidate selection, promotion agreement, conformal thresholds, and repeated
`improve()` decisions reuse the same calibration examples. Each adaptive
comparison conditions on the reported evaluation data, so neither the
agreement nor the original coverage level remains an untouched guarantee.
Use nested splits, reusable holdout accounting, or fresh sequential evidence
for every promotion.

### MXR-080-0665 — Regression serving breaks on GPU and calibrates invalid residual sets

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/regress.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–350
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

CPU feature tensors are passed to a potentially GPU-resident network and
outputs are converted with `.numpy()` without first moving to CPU. Empty,
non-finite, or malformed targets and invalid alpha/tolerance/holdout/training
parameters can select negative or unrelated residual ranks and still create a
solution. Validate regression data and quantiles, and make inference
device-safe.

### MXR-080-0666 — Per-label multilabel thresholds do not provide the advertised joint set guarantee

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/multilabel.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–268
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Each label is calibrated independently at alpha, then all decisions are
combined into one output set. Marginal per-label error control does not imply
simultaneous correctness of the whole set at that alpha. The same calibration
slice is also used to report exact-set agreement and choose improvements.
State the marginal contract or calibrate a joint nonconformity score with
independent evaluation.

### MXR-080-0667 — Structured-output solving leaks schemas and lacks joint coverage

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/structured_out.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–256
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The schema is formed from the union of teacher keys, so missing/inconsistent
records later crash per-field teachers. Inputs are keyed by `repr`, collapsing
duplicates, and numeric improvement assumes every harvested key exists.
Independently calibrated fields do not provide the claimed whole-record
coverage. Validate one explicit schema, preserve row identity, and calibrate a
joint structured loss.

### MXR-080-0668 — Generative-text priors can exceed one and training pairs silently truncate

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/generative_text.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–188
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Explicit but unobserved labels receive a pseudo-count of one while observed
counts retain denominator `n`, so the reported priors can sum above one and
log evidence/posteriors cease to be probabilities. Text/label pairs use
`zip`, unknown teacher labels can fail late, and empty/duplicate labels and
invalid hyperparameters are unguarded. Use a normalized prior and strict
aligned support validation.

### MXR-080-0669 — Planner escalation can execute a side-effecting plan twice

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/plan.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 44–104
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Local steps execute incrementally. If a later step fails or becomes uncertain,
the planner escalates to a teacher plan without rolling back earlier effects,
and the fallback can execute the same action again. There is no transaction,
idempotency key, or compensation protocol. Validate the whole plan before
execution and commit it transactionally, or return an explicit partial-state
receipt instead of retrying blindly.

### MXR-080-0670 — Teacher plans bypass the gate and plan agreement ignores semantics

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/plan.py` and `mixle/task/toolcall.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `plan.py` 105–266; `toolcall.py` 89–199
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Fallback teacher output is not checked against tool schemas, required
arguments, maximum length, or executable policy before use. Plan agreement
compares only tool names and required argument strings, ignoring optional
arguments, results, and side effects. Duplicate request maps also overwrite
training traces. Apply the same validation to every origin and define
behavioral equivalence rather than a partial syntactic match.

### MXR-080-0671 — Plan confidence and refinement are measured on their training/selection tasks

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/plan_model.py` and `mixle/task/plan_refine.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `plan_model.py` 20–112; `plan_refine.py` 20–151
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The typicality floor is a quantile of training log-probabilities, not a
held-out OOD calibration. Refinement trains on the same tasks used for its
before/after solve-rate claim and mutates the planner in place even if the
score falls, so a “rejected” refinement still leaves the worse model active.
Use immutable candidates and independent calibration/evaluation tasks.

### MXR-080-0672 — Constrained decoding does not enforce required arguments and mutates model mode

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/constrained.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–183
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The grammar permits `)` before all required arguments are emitted, leaving a
later truthiness check to reject values the grammar supposedly makes
unrepresentable. Both constrained decoding and plan scoring unconditionally
call `train()` in `finally`, even when the supplied model began in evaluation
mode. Preserve the original state and encode required-field completion in the
grammar.

### MXR-080-0673 — Structure refinement can accept a worse model and overfit one holdout

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/refine.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–211
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

A candidate is accepted when its absolute score clears `target`, not when it
improves on the champion. A worse candidate can therefore replace a stronger
baseline. Repeated edits are tried and selected on the same held-out data,
turning its score into a search objective rather than independent evidence.
Require positive champion-relative improvement and fresh or sequentially
valid verification.

### MXR-080-0674 — Orchestration exceeds budgets and emits unreplayable traces

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/orchestrate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–139
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Each budgeted iteration may execute one failed action and then an unchecked
retry, so actual actions can be twice the limit. Retry bypasses confidence
gating, failed actions can leave partial world mutation, and the world receives
the full step while the trace stores only `step["args"]`, omitting action type,
cell, and other fields. Failures after mutation can remain unrecorded. Budget
attempts, reserve resources before execution, and trace the exact committed
action and state transition.

### MXR-080-0675 — Replay equality ignores request, arguments, and seed

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/replay.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–91
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`diff()` compares only tool name and serialized result. Two traces with
different requests, arguments, and seeds but the same result produced an empty
diff. Empty traces also match vacuously. `record_step()` injects `seed`
regardless of whether the callable accepts it. Bind replay identity to the
entire canonical invocation and captured environment/RNG state.

### MXR-080-0676 — Proposal learning trains on failed candidates and cannot honor zero weights

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/propose.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–219
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Candidate ranking ignores the oracle's pass/valid verdict and can select a
failed or dead-end sequence solely by score. Refit clips negative weights but
then gives every candidate at least one replication, so zero-weight evidence
still trains the proposal; all non-positive weights can also collapse the
fit. Validate oracle outcomes first and use an estimator that natively honors
weighted observations.

### MXR-080-0677 — Composed “evidence” adds unrelated score units

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/compose.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–151
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The composition receipt sums arbitrary stage fields named `score` or
`confidence` as if they were commensurate evidence. Its equality check is
constructed from the same sum and is therefore tautological, not validation.
A probability, log score, heuristic confidence, and reward can produce a
plausible total with no statistical meaning. Require a typed evidence algebra
and declared combination rule.

### MXR-080-0678 — Structural invention accepts asserted novelty and NaN scores

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/imagine.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–151
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Any nonempty caller-supplied `new_information` string is treated as proof that
a candidate adds capability. Multiple candidates are selected on one held-out
set, and a NaN held-out score bypasses the rejection comparison. A model can
therefore be labeled as breaking a ceiling without executable novelty or a
finite improvement. Require a machine-checkable capability delta and
independent champion comparison.

### MXR-080-0679 — Generic interaction enforces hard budgets after world mutation

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/environment.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–344
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The loop calls `env.step()` before checking whether returned cost exceeds the
remaining budget. The over-budget action has already changed the world when it
is marked unaccepted. Negative and non-finite costs corrupt remaining budget,
and a zero-cost nonterminal action can run forever because there is no hard
step bound. Reserve worst-case cost before execution and require progress or a
finite action cap.

### MXR-080-0680 — Exploration can loop forever on an unaffordable action

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/explore_world.py`

false and budget stayed four, so `run_episode()` never terminates for such a
policy. Cell/target/budget dimensions are also not validated. List only
affordable actions, mark terminal when no affordable action exists, and cap
episode steps.

### MXR-080-0681 — Probe comparison consumes one-shot seed iterables twice

- **Severity:** High

`head_to_head_probe()` iterates `held_out_seeds` for the non-myopic policy and
then again for the myopic baseline. A generator is exhausted by the first
pass, giving the baseline an empty score of zero and a false head-to-head win.

### MXR-080-0682 — Grid-world learning accepts invalid worlds and nonterminal goal transitions

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/rl.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–214
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

World dimensions, goal/start/obstacle coordinates, episode lengths, and
learning hyperparameters are not validated. Calling `step()` after reaching
the goal can move away because the goal is not absorbing. Invalid or
non-finite learning settings can silently create poisoned Q tables. Validate

### MXR-080-0683 — Maximum-entropy IRL solves a different process than the demonstrations

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/irl.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–255
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Demonstrations stop at the goal, but the transition table lets expected state
visitation leave that goal. Variable starts and trajectory lengths are
collapsed into one start and maximum horizon. The returned policy is computed
before the final reward-weight update, so it is inconsistent with the
returned weights. Model absorbing termination and recompute the final policy
from the committed reward.

### MXR-080-0684 — Outcome-decomposition candidates are compared on different random worlds

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/outcome_decomposer.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–146
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Candidate plans receive different environment seeds, confounding plan quality
with world difficulty. Initial seeds are not derived from the function seed,
and the same candidate/outcome log is adaptively thresholded and refit without
an independent score panel. Evaluate all candidates on common random numbers
and preserve a separate selection audit.

### MXR-080-0685 — Extraction metrics inflate correctness and silently compare prefixes

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/extract.py`, `mixle/task/harness.py`, and `mixle/task/generative_capability.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `extract.py` 20–290; `harness.py` 20–198; `generative_capability.py` 30–132
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

A wrong value for an expected field contributes a false negative but no false
positive, inflating F1. Empty/all-empty comparisons return 1.0, and `zip`
silently truncates mismatched prediction/gold/text lengths. Duplicate
substring alignment always chooses the first occurrence, overlapping spans
overwrite labels, and harness required fields use truthiness. Enforce aligned
lengths and standard micro-F1 accounting, and report ambiguous/truncated
extractions as abstentions.

### MXR-080-0686 — Distillation can call a side-effecting teacher twice and discard better checkpoints

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/distill.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–691
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The batched-teacher probe can fall back to per-item calls after already
invoking the teacher, so one logical labeling pass may execute twice.
Text/label lengths are repeatedly combined with `zip`, agreement can score a
prefix as complete, and early stopping returns the last stalled/worse weights
rather than the best-loss checkpoint. Make teacher dispatch explicit, enforce
cardinality, and snapshot the best validated state.

### MXR-080-0687 — Soft-label distillation admits NaN probability targets

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–177
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

NaNs survive clipping and the `sum <= 0` check, then normalize into NaN
targets. NaN temperature and hard-label weights bypass inequality validation;
label support and tensor shapes are incomplete; and agreement can broadcast
incompatible arrays. Require finite row-stochastic targets and exact shapes
before training.

### MXR-080-0688 — Advanced distillation mutates teachers and permits invalid ensemble probabilities

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/distill_methods.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–968
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Most methods omit finite/range checks for temperature, alpha, weights, epochs,
learning rate, and tensor shapes. An empty teacher ensemble divides by zero;
negative weights are allowed when their total is positive, producing a
non-probability mixture. Teacher modules are switched to evaluation without
restoration, hooks are not exception-safe in every path, and device placement
is inconsistent. Validate each method's mathematical domain and restore all
borrowed state.

### MXR-080-0689 — Sequence distillation trains on prompt reconstruction and fails at zero generation length

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/distill_methods.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 671–851
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The sequence-level loss includes prompt-to-prompt tokens rather than masking
the prompt, so copying a long prompt can dominate the intended continuation
objective. `_greedy_generate()` concatenates an empty list at
`gen_length=0`, and evaluation/training modes are returned inconsistently.
Mask conditioning tokens and validate generation geometry.

### MXR-080-0690 — MLP quantization silently changes arbitrary model architectures

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/quantize.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–292
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`quantize_mlp()` collects every registered `Linear` in module order and
rebuilds them as a sequential ReLU network. Branches, residuals, unused
layers, non-ReLU activations, and shared modules therefore become a different
function without rejection. Non-finite weights poison scales, array
shape/scale consistency is unchecked, and the compiled LNS cache can become
stale after mutation. Restrict conversion to a verified architecture graph
and prove pre/post parity.

### MXR-080-0691 — Checkpoint ladders do not enforce a decreasing family or evaluate the supplied data

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/checkpoint_family_ladder.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–449
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The ladder accepts rungs with increasing parameter counts despite its
decreasing-family contract. `eval_data` is passed to compression but not to
the checkpoint evaluator, so the quality gate can assess a different or
default workload. Empty checks can pass through lower layers, and release
reports retain stale branch/PR history. Bind each rung to one declared
evaluation set and verify monotone resource size.

### MXR-080-0692 — Deployment receipts include rejected rungs but do not produce deployable artifacts

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/deploy_family.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–207
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The deployment pass iterates every family rung, including a quality-rejected
terminal rung. It measures temporary quantized arrays but returns only an
aggregate receipt, not the arrays or a content-addressed deployable artifact.
Dense storage is hardcoded to four bytes per parameter regardless of dtype,
and “cost” is bytes rather than measured inference work. Exclude failed rungs
and publish the exact served payload behind each receipt.

### MXR-080-0693 — Bandit updates admit non-finite rewards and poison all future decisions

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/bandit.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 37–222
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Gaussian Thompson sampling and UCB1 accept NaN/inf rewards; the probe left

`EstimatorBandit` permits non-positive Monte Carlo draws and unchecked
estimator scores, and its random Poisson replicate assignments make the
claimed update commutativity false for an exact replay. Require finite rewards
and state the stochastic ordering contract.

### MXR-080-0694 — Capacity ladders can compare misaligned labels and malformed embedding families

- **Severity:** High

holdouts are not validated. Sequence labels plus `val_texts` but no

### MXR-080-0695 — Multi-fidelity emulation exceeds its hard simulator budget

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/emulate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 129–346
- **State:** Reproduced

Every fidelity receives `n_init` calls before affordability is checked, and
the acquisition loop checks only current spend before taking the next call.
With budget 35, fidelities costing 1 and 10, and `n_init=2`, the receipt

### MXR-080-0696 — Catalog routing treats an uncalibrated prior as an answer gate

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/catalog_router.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 29–86
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

A catalog entry answers merely because its caller-supplied reliability is at
least 0.5 and the optional domain does not disagree. No output is invoked or
verified by this router, and missing domain matches every entry. Costs,

### MXR-080-0697 — Collapse monitoring passes NaN and evidence-free histories

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/collapse.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–95
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Comparisons against NaN are false, so a round with NaN score and diversity was
reported `ok=True`. Empty and one-round histories also certify “no collapse”
without evidence, and negative tolerances invert the intended policy. Require
finite series, non-negative tolerances, and enough comparable rounds; report
insufficient evidence separately from success.

### MXR-080-0698 — LLM model design validates only that a short fit did not immediately crash

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/design.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 43–173
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The “hard correctness gate” runs at most three optimizer iterations on a
possibly empty prefix and checks only finite training log density. It does not
validate schema compatibility, held-out predictive behavior, or that the
fallback estimator itself fits. JSON parsing is brace-naive, and broad
exception fallback erases the failed specification as structured evidence.
Use schema-aware construction and an independent acceptance receipt.

### MXR-080-0699 — Data-mixture optimization does not train on an actual interleaved mixture

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/data_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 49–266
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Each domain's samples are concatenated as one contiguous block rather than
drawn/interleaved from the mixture distribution. The LM can learn block
boundaries and order effects, so optimized weights need not estimate the
claimed corpus mixture. NaN weights pass normalization, duplicate domain names
overwrite evaluation losses, and the same held-out set is reused throughout
adaptive search without a final audit. Sample domain identity per token or
document and reserve independent evaluation.

### MXR-080-0700 — MinHash arithmetic overflows and is not the stated unbiased estimator

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/data_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 269–339
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The affine hash uses signed `int64` multiplication with values near the
`2^61-1` prime. Products overflow before modulus reduction, invalidating the
universal-hash construction and its stated unbiased Jaccard interpretation.
Short/empty documents also collapse to a single synthetic shingle. Use
overflow-safe modular arithmetic and specify empty-document semantics.

### MXR-080-0701 — Frontier-to-native receipts mix cumulative traffic with one evaluation batch

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/frontier_to_native.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 89–224
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Quality is computed on the current `test_data`, but request/escalation counts
and realized cost come from the cascade's lifetime cumulative stats. Prior
traffic contaminates a new receipt. The teacher is called independently for
reference predictions and again on escalations, so stateful teachers can yield
different answers, and empty data creates NaN/division failures. Snapshot
counter deltas and bind all metrics to one immutable evaluation run.

### MXR-080-0702 — Discrepancy invention promotes a different stochastic fit than the one scored

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/discrepancy_invention_loop.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 49–375
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Accepted candidates are fit during proposal scoring, fit again for the
portfolio, and fit again as the winning model. With stochastic fitting, the
gate and adoption do not concern the artifact that earned the held-out score.
The same held-out data drives ceiling detection, candidate selection,
portfolio reweighting, and promotion. Probe simulation can fall back to the
requested action itself for every hypothesis, fabricating agreement. Cache
candidate artifacts and use disjoint evidence by decision stage.

### MXR-080-0703 — Existing knowledge resolves gaps by domain alone without verification

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/knowledge_routing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 90–189
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`_match_existing_item()` checks only `metadata.domain`. A forged item missing
the gap's required properties, provenance, content hash, schema, and verifier
status resolved the gap in the probe. Tool results are likewise wrapped but
not validated against the declared output schema. Require admissible,
content-bound evidence that satisfies the full required schema and acceptance
criteria.

### MXR-080-0704 — Knowledge routing mutates caller memory and overrides a zero budget

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/knowledge_routing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 252–432
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The bundle is shallow-copied, then its original gap dictionaries are mutated
to `resolved`, contrary to the no-mutation contract. `budget` is forced to at
least the number of gaps; a zero-budget probe executed one step and changed
the caller's gap. Only the cheapest candidate is tried, so a failed verifier
or missing executor prevents trying the next compatible tool. Deep-copy
inputs, honor hard budget, and ledger a bounded candidate fallback sequence.

### MXR-080-0705 — Pilot release gates pass NaN and measure MoE before training

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/pilot_ladder.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 142–469
- **State:** Reproduced

NaN final loss and forgetting gap produced `passed=True` with “all criteria
met.” The MoE-vs-dense receipt is computed on the randomly initialized block
before the rung's training loop despite documentation saying it uses the
trained block. Forgetting evaluations consume fresh random batches at every
checkpoint, confounding forgetting with sampling noise. Reject non-finite
health, evaluate fixed panels, and gate the exact trained artifact.

### MXR-080-0706 — Task decomposition labels raw regression as a discovered intermediate structure

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/task_decomposition.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 51–339
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Raw input columns and proposed intermediates share one candidate map, and any
positive raw-input regression is appended to `chosen`. With no intermediate
candidates at all, the probe returned `chosen=['x']` and
`is_decomposed=True`. Name collisions train on an intermediate but prediction
prefers the raw input, while dependency-gain fallback can earn gain with
`edge=None` that prediction simply skips. Model monolithic and decomposed
families explicitly and keep training/serving feature identity identical.

### MXR-080-0707 — SFT planner validation is lossy and calibrated on its own evaluation set

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–405

Serialization has no escaping for separators, duplicate argument keys
overwrite, duplicate requests collapse in dictionaries, teacher plans are
checked only for tool names, and optional arguments are ignored by agreement.
The confidence floor is selected and reported on the same holdout, with the
teacher called repeatedly. Copy fidelity accepts any value appearing as a
substring of the tool name rather than a declared vocabulary. Validate
teacher traces once and use separate calibration and test panels.

### MXR-080-0708 — Recipe tuning reports the adaptively selected validation maximum as held-out agreement

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/tune.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 31–228
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Bayesian optimization repeatedly scores candidates on one validation set and
returns the maximum as `agreement`, without an untouched test estimate.
Malformed recipe spaces, invalid iteration counts, empty sets, and non-finite
cost weights can leave no trial or select invalid scores. The routing variant
separates calibration but still exposes the selection-biased agreement.
Distinguish search objective from independently measured performance.

### MXR-080-0709 — VLM enumeration cannot provide the claimed exact probability order

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/vlm.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 49–176
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Each node exposes only `top_logprobs` (20 by default), so a pruned token can
start a globally higher-probability completed sequence; best-first exactness
requires complete next-token support or a certified residual bound.
Continuations are reconstructed by concatenating token strings and
re-tokenizing server-side, which need not preserve BPE boundaries. Candidate
scores omit EOS, and the empty candidate receives probability one (log score
zero). Remove the exactness claim or require a tokenizer-bound full-support
scorer including termination.

### MXR-080-0710 — Edge footprints undercount deployable artifacts and assume fp32 storage

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/edge.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 53–174
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Torch bytes are hardcoded as four per parameter regardless of actual dtype.
Pure-model bytes serialize only `student.model`, omitting adapter labels,
configuration, metadata, and container overhead required to serve it. The
closed-form op count is a rough structural proxy, not a measurement, yet these
numbers enforce “hard” device budgets. Measure the exact exported serving
artifact and benchmark its actual execution path.

### MXR-080-0711 — Edge search selects on one validation set and accepts corrupt design ledgers

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/edge.py` and `mixle/task/design_prior.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `edge.py` 177–736; `design_prior.py` 30–73

Every screen, promoted full model, winner, and reported Pareto point is chosen
on the same validation labels, with no independent final evaluation.
Validation labels also expand the class vocabulary. Design ledgers accept
non-finite values and inconsistent row widths; deserialization does not check
parallel array lengths; family ranking lets NaN means control sort order.
Validate ledger invariants and separate search evidence from deployment
qualification.

### MXR-080-0712 — Sequential inverse training targets the proposal posterior, not the declared prior posterior

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/inverse.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 110–172 and 356–435
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

After round one, parameters are sampled from the current
`q(theta|y_obs)` and the conditional model is retrained on those pairs without
proposal correction or retained prior simulations. That training distribution
does not identify the original `p(theta|y)`; it identifies a
proposal-conditioned inverse and can progressively narrow away valid modes.
Use a valid SNPE correction/objective and document the posterior target for
every round.

### MXR-080-0713 — The optional inverse “exactness” stage never changes the returned posterior

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/inverse.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 236–269 and 436–471
