- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Importance weights are computed only to report ESS. `InverseModel.posterior()`
continues sampling and scoring the unweighted neural approximation, so
`reweight=True` does not return the described self-normalized importance
posterior or make inference more exact. It is also allowed without `y_obs`.
Return a weighted/resampled posterior bound to the weights, or rename the
option to an ESS diagnostic.

### MXR-080-0714 — Inverse calibration p-values and coverage receipts are invalid for general inputs

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/inverse.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 92–355 and 356–471
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The SBC histogram treats discrete ranks `0..n_samples` as equal continuous
bins, whose rank counts need not be equal, and sums per-dimension chi-square
statistics as independent even when posterior dimensions are correlated.
Coverage pass/fail ignores finite-sample uncertainty. Replication/sample
counts, coverage levels, simulator shapes/finiteness, posterior query width,
and model device/state are not validated. Use a valid randomized-rank SBC
test and uncertainty-aware coverage intervals.

### MXR-080-0715 — Scorecards underprice escalations and define end-to-end accuracy tautologically

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/scorecard.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 86–210
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Blended cost charges student cost only on locally answered requests instead of
on every attempted request. With all calls escalating and costs 1 plus 10, the
receipt reported 10,000 per thousand instead of 11,000. Every escalation is
declared correct by construction, so end-to-end accuracy is not measured
against an external truth, and the teacher is called a second time for timing
(four calls for two examples in the probe). Account for all attempts and
separate teacher agreement from task truth.

### MXR-080-0716 — Capability profiles silently truncate outputs and misclassify abstentions

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/capability.py` and `mixle/task/generative_capability.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `capability.py` 63–159; `generative_capability.py` 30–132
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Agreement, invariance, F1, and schema checks use `zip` without requiring equal
lengths, so a short model response can receive a strong prefix score. Empty
profiles often report zero disagreement or perfect schema/F1 rather than
insufficient evidence. Escalation is recognized only as `None`, while the
package's calibrated models use a separate `ESCALATE` sentinel. Enforce exact
cardinality and one typed abstention representation.

### MXR-080-0717 — `empirical_kl_divergence` computes a different statistic than its public contract

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/evaluation.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 22–64
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The function renormalizes the two models' densities over the observed sample
locations and computes a KL divergence between those normalized location
weights. That is not the documented empirical expectation
`mean(log p1(X) - log p2(X))`; it changes with duplicate sample locations and
answers a different question. An input with no jointly finite density rows
also reaches reductions on an empty array, while positive infinity is admitted
and produces NaN intermediates. Implement the stated empirical estimator (or
rename and formally specify the normalized discrete estimator) and fail
closed on empty or non-finite evidence.

### MXR-080-0718 — The chi-square helper ignores observations on impossible support

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/evaluation.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 89–117
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Bins with zero expected count are removed before the statistic is computed.
Consequently an observation in a bin to which the model assigns zero
probability contributes nothing instead of forcing rejection. Counts,
probabilities, bounds, finiteness, and normalization are also not validated.
Treat positive observed mass at zero expected mass as an infinite statistic
and validate the discrete experiment before issuing a p-value.

### MXR-080-0719 — Evaluation partition helpers can silently lose or misassign observations

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/evaluation.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 120–186
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The k-fold, fixed-size, and proportional partition paths do not consistently
require positive integer sizes, feasible fold counts, or finite nonnegative
proportions that exhaust the sample. Invalid requests can create empty folds,
leave rows at a default assignment, or drop a suffix while still returning a
normal-looking partition. Make conservation of row indices an invariant and
reject every infeasible partition specification.

### MXR-080-0720 — ROC/AUC gives perfect discrimination to tied scores

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/metrics.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 64–145
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The sweep orders positive examples ahead of negative examples within a score
tie instead of processing the tie as one threshold. A direct probe with one
positive, one negative, and both scores equal returned AUC `1.0`; the correct
value is `0.5`. Empty classes and non-finite scores are also not rejected.
Aggregate equal-score blocks before updating the curve and validate that both
classes are present.

### MXR-080-0721 — Classification metrics do not establish a one-to-one label/probability contract

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/metrics.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 18–62
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Duplicate declared labels, observed labels absent from the declared support,
empty inputs, non-finite logits, and incompatible probability widths are not
validated. Duplicate labels can reserve multiple probability columns for one
class, while a missing observed label can be indexed as a different class.
Require unique support, exact array cardinality, finite values, and complete
coverage before computing loss or accuracy.

### MXR-080-0722 — Optional-dependency detection hides broken installations

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/optional_deps.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–118
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Dependency probes catch `ImportError` raised anywhere inside the imported
package and report the package as simply unavailable. A present but broken
installation, including a missing internal dependency or binary-extension
failure expressed as `ImportError`, is therefore silently downgraded to an
optional feature absence. Distinguish “target module not found” from failures
raised while importing a found target and preserve the latter exception.

### MXR-080-0723 — `binomial_rank` accepts malformed experiments and fails on valid edge cases

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/pvalues.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 14–105
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Parallel inputs are combined with truncating `zip`, counts and probabilities
are not validated, and deterministic `p=0`/`p=1` terms are skipped rather than
enforced. For a singleton fair-Bernoulli experiment the unique likelihood
grid has one point and the spacing reduction is empty, so an otherwise valid
case raises. Nonpositive length controls and degenerate precision controls can
also fail or loop. Validate the experiment and handle singleton/discrete
support directly.

### MXR-080-0724 — Serialization registry failure is cached as permanent success

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/serialization.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 149–206
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Registry initialization broadly suppresses import failures and then sets
`_REGISTRY_READY=True`. One transient or internal import failure can therefore
freeze a partial registry for the rest of the process, with no warning or
retry, and concurrent callers are unsynchronized. Build into a temporary
registry, surface unexpected import failures, and publish the ready flag only
after an atomic successful initialization.

### MXR-080-0725 — Registered-object decoding bypasses constructors and class invariants

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/serialization.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 243–448
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The decoder allocates registered classes without invoking their constructors
and writes decoded values directly into `__dict__`. It therefore bypasses
validation and can create states the public class can never construct.
Unbounded nesting and container sizes additionally make the decoder a resource
exhaustion surface. Require a class-owned safe decode hook or constructor path,
validate schemas, and impose explicit depth and size limits.

### MXR-080-0726 — Special functions turn positive infinity and NaN into plausible finite answers

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/special.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 162–206 and 278–321
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`softmax([0, +inf])` returned `[0.5, 0.5]` because every non-finite maximum is
handled as though all logits were negative infinity. Array `digammainv`
initializes NaN positions to zero and can return that finite value rather than
propagating or rejecting the invalid input. Give positive infinity its
well-defined limiting mass, reject/propagate NaN explicitly, and distinguish
it from the all-negative-infinity case.

### MXR-080-0727 — Probability-vector helpers manufacture posteriors from invalid evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/vector.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 124–145 and 347–677
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The weighted log-sum path returned negative infinity for weight zero times
positive-infinite density, and posterior helpers converted positive-infinite,
NaN, or wholly impossible evidence into a uniform posterior. `row_choice`
accepts rows summing below one and assigns all residual probability to the
last category; a row `[0.2, 0.2]` can therefore select category 1 with
probability 0.8. Enforce finite normalized probability inputs and return a
typed impossible-evidence result rather than fabricated uniform belief.

### MXR-080-0728 — Detector discovery can permanently expose a partial, overwritten registry

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/detectors/__init__.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 30–80
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Duplicate detector names overwrite existing registrations, detector kinds are
not constrained, and discovery marks itself complete before importing all
detectors. An import failure leaves the partial registry marked discovered,
so later calls neither retry nor reveal which families are missing. Registry
construction is also unsynchronized. Validate unique typed entries and publish
one complete immutable registry transactionally.

### MXR-080-0729 — Model-selection penalties omit parameters estimated from the same data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/detectors/binomial.py`, `beta_binomial.py`, `pareto.py`, and `generalized_pareto.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** detector scoring and fit paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Binomial-family detectors infer trial count from the sample maximum while BIC
treats it as fixed. Pareto-family detectors similarly pin thresholds to the
sample minimum without charging or profiling that choice. These data-selected
support parameters change likelihood and model complexity, biasing selection
toward those families. Use a valid joint/profile likelihood and include every
selected parameter in the penalty, or require support controls to be supplied
externally.

### MXR-080-0730 — The selected GPD is not the GPD that the factory returns

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/detectors/generalized_pareto.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 24–100
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Scoring and goodness-of-fit refit a maximum-likelihood generalized Pareto,
while the exported factory reconstructs a method-of-moments estimate. The
candidate can therefore win using one distribution and deploy a materially
different one, invalidating the selection receipt. Carry the fitted parameter
object through selection or make the scoring and deployment estimators
identical.

### MXR-080-0731 — Robust validation does not control the estimator that profiling returns

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 91–118, 951–1027, 1444–1491, and 1839–1892
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The estimator is constructed before robust validation and `DatumNode` ignores
the resulting recommendation. Registered detector families are also omitted
from held-out candidate scoring, so a selected registered family can be
overridden by a built-in comparison without its own held-out score, or be
reported while a different estimator is returned. Make one typed selection
result own the fitted candidate, validation evidence, fallback decision, and
returned estimator.

### MXR-080-0732 — Gaussian code length is clipped on a scale where competing families are not

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 334–397
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The Gaussian candidate clips negative differential-entropy/code-length values
to zero, while other continuous-density candidates may retain negative values.
Continuous densities legitimately exceed one, so negative log density is not
invalid; clipping only one family makes cross-family scores incomparable.
Compute every candidate on the same proper predictive scoring rule without
family-specific truncation.

### MXR-080-0733 — Profiling reports uncalibrated fitted-model KS p-values as goodness-of-fit evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 707–744 and 1250–1263
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The probability-integral-transform sample is generated with parameters fit on
the same observations, then evaluated using the ordinary fixed-null KS
distribution. Parameter estimation changes the null distribution, so the
reported p-values are not calibrated and can approve a bad family. Use an
appropriate Lilliefors result or parametric bootstrap, preferably on held-out
data.

### MXR-080-0734 — Profiling and estimator inference disagree about the same mixed/non-finite data

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1030–1305 and 1710–2031
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Generator-valued fields fail because one path calls `len()` while another
materializes; infinities make the profile “mixed object” while the estimator
wraps them as optional numeric values; and mixed strings/integers can become a
categorical estimator while profile evidence omits them. Boolean and integer
keys also collide (`True == 1`) in categorical counts. Normalize once into a
typed immutable observation representation shared by profiling and fitting.

### MXR-080-0735 — Shape heuristics assert unsupported image and embedding semantics

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1085–1305 and 1710–2031
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Matrix shape alone classifies data as images, and vector width at least 16
classifies values as embeddings. Ordinary tabular matrices, sensor arrays, or
time-series windows can therefore be routed to neural image/embedding models
without provenance or semantic evidence. Treat these as hypotheses requiring
explicit modality metadata or validated detection, not authoritative types.

### MXR-080-0736 — Automatic factories accept invalid masses and silently ignore Bayesian requests

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/factories.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** factory construction paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

An empty categorical mass map divides by zero, and negative or non-finite
weights are not consistently rejected. More importantly, the documented
`use_bstats` Bayesian path is silently ignored by several lognormal, gamma,
Student-t, and mixture factories, while DPM controls are accepted without a
coherent validity check. Validate every mass/control and either honor the
Bayesian request or fail explicitly.

### MXR-080-0737 — BIC compares maximized likelihoods with method-of-moments fits

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py` and detector fit helpers
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** candidate scoring and selection paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Gamma and Student-t candidates are evaluated at method-of-moments estimates
while other families use maximum-likelihood fits. The usual BIC approximation
requires the maximized likelihood, so these values are not commensurate and
the winning family can be an artifact of estimator choice. Use comparable
maximum-likelihood or integrated predictive scores for all candidates.

### MXR-080-0738 — Automatic HVis affinity hides real failures by changing the requested method

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/affinity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 573–619
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The `auto` path catches every exception raised while constructing local-factor
geometry and silently falls back to Bhattacharyya affinity. Invalid field
weights, broken model statistics, and implementation errors are therefore
reported as a successful but different visualization. Fall back only for a
typed “capability unavailable” result and surface all invalid-input or
internal failures.

### MXR-080-0739 — HVis turns impossible or invalid model evidence into geometry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/affinity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 13–49, 249–414, and 622–701
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Posterior construction has no explicit all-impossible-evidence contract and
can produce NaN responsibilities. Public affinity entry points do not require
finite, nonnegative, row-stochastic responsibilities, and negative
similarities are clamped to a small positive number rather than rejected.
This can convert a failed statistical model into a plausible graph. Preserve
typed impossible evidence and validate all affinity axioms before embedding.

### MXR-080-0740 — Optional fields discard their within-component coordinates

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/affinity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 196–222
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The optional-field iterator forwards posterior mass but replaces the wrapped
field's local coordinates with `None`. Local or balanced HVis therefore
silently becomes posterior-only for optional values, contrary to the stated
contract that fields carry within-component geometry. Preserve the inner
coordinates together with the optional-state representation.

### MXR-080-0741 — Failed Fisher geometry is erased into valid zero vectors

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/affinity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 421–467
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

NaN/Inf field weights and ridge controls pass the current sign checks, and
Fisher vectors use `nan_to_num(..., nan=0)` to replace failed/non-finite model
statistics with zeros. Distinct invalid observations can consequently become
identical, well-formed geometry. Reject non-finite controls and propagate a
typed unavailable/invalid Fisher result instead of fabricating coordinates.

### MXR-080-0742 — Conditional affinities admit self-probability and claim unreachable perplexities

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/affinity.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1010–1112
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Finite diagonal distances are accepted and can receive conditional
probability, although the algorithm assumes excluded self-neighbors.
Perplexity above `n-1` is accepted as a target even though no such distribution
is reachable. Validate a square finite distance matrix, exclude the diagonal
unconditionally, and require a feasible positive perplexity.

### MXR-080-0743 — HVis health receipts are invalid under ties and small samples

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/front.py` and `mixle/utils/hvis/topology.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `front.py` 173–188; `topology.py` 310–396
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Typicality uses a double `argsort`, assigning different percentiles to tied
values and arbitrary ranks to NaNs. Embedding health permits sample sizes and
neighbor counts that make trustworthiness normalization divide by zero or
leave its mathematical domain. Require finite inputs and feasible dimensions,
and give ties equal ranks using a documented convention.

### MXR-080-0744 — Model-fit “coverage” uses the wrong reference distribution on fitted data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/topology.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 190–307
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The same points are used to estimate center/covariance and to compare their
Mahalanobis distances with nominal chi-square coverage. Fitted distances do
not have that fixed-parameter reference law, so the receipt is optimistically
miscalibrated. The fuzzy-nerve topology path likewise makes topological claims
without establishing good-cover conditions. Use held-out or finite-sample
calibrated diagnostics and label heuristic topology as such.

### MXR-080-0745 — Internal UMAP includes every point as its own nearest neighbor

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/umap_np.py` and `mixle/utils/hvis/neighbors.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `umap_np.py` 51–187; model-neighbor construction
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The k-nearest-neighbor result includes the query point at distance zero, and
that self-edge participates in smooth-kNN radius calibration and the fuzzy
graph diagonal. Standard UMAP excludes self-neighbors; including them changes
local connectivity, sigma, edge weights, and the optimized objective. Remove
self before calibration and handle empty graphs and invalid epoch/sampling
controls explicitly.

### MXR-080-0746 — t-SNE accepts invalid probability matrices and can stop when the objective gets worse

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/tsne.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** exact and Barnes–Hut optimization paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The exact path does not establish that `P` is square, symmetric, finite,
nonnegative, normalized, and zero-diagonal; the Barnes–Hut attraction loop
uses only one triangle, silently mishandling asymmetric input. The convergence
test regards a sufficiently negative “improvement” as convergence, so a large
objective increase can terminate successfully. Validate the probability
model and require nonnegative improvement within tolerance (with a separate
divergence test).

### MXR-080-0747 — t-SNE’s advertised alpha update is not a Newton step

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/tsne.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** alpha optimization and reporting paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The update subtracts objective divided by a first derivative, without a
Hessian and without solving a root equation whose zero represents the desired
optimum. It is labeled Newton optimization despite not implementing Newton's
method. Invalid iteration/printing controls can also cause modulo-zero
failures. Specify the actual scalar objective and use a bounded, validated
line search or root solver with truthful receipts.

### MXR-080-0748 — HVis entry points consume one-shot data and silently change requested algorithms

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/embed.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** public `htsne`/`humap` dispatch paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Affinity resolution can consume a generator before later length/posterior
passes, producing empty or mismatched results. Unknown method names fall
through to exact t-SNE, and Barnes–Hut plus alpha optimization silently ignores
the requested optimization. Materialize once, validate sample cardinality and
controls, and reject every unsupported method/option combination.

### MXR-080-0749 — Streaming HVis refresh is a non-transactional destructive update

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/stream.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** landmark projection, drift, and refresh paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Landmark shapes, responsibilities, controls, and finiteness are not validated,
and no-evidence rows may become uniform. More seriously, refresh mutates the
model and clears accumulated stream statistics before embedding/alignment has
succeeded. A downstream exception leaves a partially replaced model and
irretrievably loses pending evidence; NaN drift can also avoid the trigger.
Build and validate a candidate state, then swap it atomically only after every
stage succeeds.

### MXR-080-0750 — Constraint and direct-map APIs accept goals that cannot define valid geometry

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/goals.py` and `mixle/utils/hvis/direct.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** goal dataclasses and direct placement paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Anchor indices/coordinates, label margins, axis indices/values/weights,
responsibilities, embedding dimensions, spread, and margins lack a complete
shape/finiteness/domain contract. Negative indices can mutate unintended rows
and NaN goals can poison an optimization while still returning coordinates.
Validate every goal at construction and every geometry input before mutation.

### MXR-080-0751 — Distributed HVis folds silently discard mismatched statistics

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/distributed.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** distributed statistic add/fold paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Adding a `FiberStats` pair with only one triple present drops that triple
instead of rejecting incompatible schemas, and `ScoreStats` combines component
lists with truncating `zip`. A map-like mapper is also assumed to preserve row
order although its contract does not guarantee that. Enforce identical typed
schemas and stable row IDs before any distributed fold.

### MXR-080-0752 — Sparse-neighbor construction treats “no evidence” as perfect similarity

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/hvis/neighbors.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** sparse factor and model-neighbor paths
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

When all factor weights are zero, every pair receives log affinity zero and
the routine emits an arbitrary zero-distance neighbor graph. Invalid
neighborhood sizes, block sizes, caps, and factors are not consistently
rejected, and empty model input can crash downstream. Return an explicit
no-evidence result and require a positive finite evidence weight with feasible
graph controls.

### MXR-080-0753 — Fractional parallel dimensions produce two contradictory plans

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/training_contracts.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 64–164
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`ParallelPlan` type annotations are not runtime constraints. Validation and
`axis_sizes` truncate dimensions with `int`, while public attributes retain the
fractional values and are passed to external backends. A probe constructing
`ParallelPlan(tp=1.9)` retained `tp == 1.9` but reported a one-rank mesh and
serialized `tp: 1`. Require exact positive integers at construction and use
one canonical representation everywhere.

### MXR-080-0754 — Training layouts and receipts can certify impossible executions

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/training_contracts.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 213–298
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`ParameterLayout`, `DistributedUpdate`, and `StepReceipt` have no invariant
validation. Duplicate placement axes collapse silently when `as_dict()` calls
`dict(self.placements)`, while negative/non-finite losses, counts, byte totals,
shapes, and steps can be emitted as authoritative receipts. Validate typed
identities, unique axes, finite measurements, and nonnegative cardinalities
before a receipt can exist.

### MXR-080-0755 — Cluster launchers do not prove that launched topology matches the plan

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/training_launchers.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 15–99
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The Lightning launcher accepts explicit `devices` and `num_nodes` whose
product can differ from `plan.world_size`; the Ray launcher accepts resource
requests that can conflict with `use_gpu` or leave the intended rank topology
unrealizable. Neither returns a binding receipt between actual workers and
plan coordinates. Validate launcher topology before startup and require every
worker to attest its assigned coordinate.

### MXR-080-0756 — The balance planner treats unknown memory as unlimited

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/balance.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 88–169
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`memory_bytes=None` becomes zero, and zero makes `fits=True`; missing resource
evidence is therefore converted into a positive memory-fit claim. The model
footprint is also divided uniformly across shard count even though cuts are
balanced by FLOPs and can have very unequal byte footprints, so an individual
cut may exceed its device. Represent unknown fit as unknown and estimate/check
each concrete cut against its assigned device.

### MXR-080-0757 — Balance planning silently rewrites workload size and overstates model-parallel work

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/balance.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 72–169
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Nonpositive `n_data` is coerced to one instead of rejected. For a data-by-model
grid, the indivisible-unit lower bound multiplies the heaviest unit by all
`n_data`, rather than the observations handled by one data-parallel replica,
overstating the busiest worker by the data-parallel factor. Costs and unit
weights also lack finite/nonnegative validation. Preserve the requested
workload and derive each worker's actual assigned work.

### MXR-080-0758 — Tree decomposition misses nested models behind atomic wrappers

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/model_decomposition.py` and `mixle/utils/parallel/model_parallel.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `model_decomposition.py` 148–236; `model_parallel.py` 61–104
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Tree sizing and axis discovery recurse only through `shard_children`, and the
parallel-ID walk descends only when the current node is itself threadable.
Nested distributions behind an atomic/non-shardable wrapper are therefore
omitted from memory totals and can never expose their shardable axes. Root
cycle accounting can also double-count the root because it is not seeded into
the seen set. Traverse the full ownership graph independently of whether each
intermediate node is shardable.

### MXR-080-0759 — “Model parallel” execution does not execute the planned model shards

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/model_parallel.py` and `mixle/utils/parallel/balance.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `model_parallel.py` 48–60, 215–300, and 398–418; `balance.py` 173–191
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`auto_parallel_estimator` discards the selected cuts, devices, and axis and
passes only a worker count to `ModelParallelEstimator`. The executor then runs
an in-process thread pool over a fully resident model; it neither partitions
model memory across devices nor realizes placement. A plan can thus claim a
model fits only because it was sharded while execution still requires the
whole model in one process. Require an executable placement contract or label
this path component-parallel threading, not model sharding.

### MXR-080-0760 — Model-parallel mixture folding fabricates priors for invalid likelihoods

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/model_parallel.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 130–217 and 249–279
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Positive-infinite component likelihoods are handled like negative infinity and
replaced by prior weights; NaNs can pass through, and invalid/all-zero mixture
weights remain undefined. Shapes, finiteness, normalization, and initialization
probability are not established. Preserve the limiting semantics of positive
infinity, return typed impossible evidence for all-negative-infinity rows, and
reject every invalid mixture before folding.

### MXR-080-0761 — Resource discovery admits NaN throughput and duplicate physical devices

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 50–103 and 123–320
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`throughput <= 0` does not reject NaN; a direct probe constructed valid
`Resources` with NaN throughput. Torchrun discovery names devices by
`rank % local_cuda_count`, so multi-node ranks repeat names such as `cuda:0`
without node identity and may be planned as distinct slots on the same local
GPU. Require finite positive throughput, unique global device identities, and
launcher-provided node/local-rank topology.

### MXR-080-0762 — Placement objects can overlap, omit, or lie about rows

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 472–574 and 859–929
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`PlacementShard` and `Placement` do not validate integer ranges, exact
coverage, non-overlap, byte estimates, total rows, or membership in declared
resources. `LocalEncodedData` trusts an externally supplied placement, encodes
only its positive-sized ranges, but sets `size = len(data)`. A malformed plan
can therefore duplicate/drop training observations while reporting the full
count. Make placement validation mandatory at the execution boundary.

### MXR-080-0763 — Planner returns shards even when fixed model state cannot fit

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1418–1558 and 1789–1796
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

When model plus statistic state already exceeds device memory,
`_max_rows_for_device` returns one. Splitting data to one-row shards cannot
reduce that fixed state, yet the resulting placement has no failed/unknown fit
verdict. `model_sharding_plan` does not check memory at all, and its count
adjustment can violate `min_components_per_shard`. Fail closed when fixed
state cannot fit and validate actual per-shard bytes and minimum sizes.

### MXR-080-0764 — Memory planning systematically omits private and deep model state

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1688–1703 and 1827–1864
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The recursive estimator skips every `__dict__` key beginning with `_`, stops at
depth eight, suppresses all fallback errors, and does not count container or
object overhead. Many Python models store parameters or caches in private
fields, so the footprint used for a hard memory decision can be zero or far
below reality. Require explicit backend/model size protocols and make unknown
state visible rather than silently counting it as zero.

### MXR-080-0765 — Calibration suppresses failed devices and reports best-case throughput

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1561–1685
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Any exception during device calibration is swallowed and the old device
record is retained with no failure evidence. Successful repetitions use the
minimum elapsed time, creating a systematically optimistic capacity estimate,
and catalog persistence is non-atomic. A resource set can consequently appear
calibrated even when a device never ran the workload. Record per-device
success/failure and distributions of timings, use a robust estimator, and
persist catalogs atomically.

### MXR-080-0766 — Existing encoded handles silently override an explicit backend request

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 647–706
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

If `data` structurally matches `EncodedFold`, `encoded_data` immediately
returns it and ignores the requested backend, placement, precision, resources,
and worker controls. A caller asking to move an existing handle to another
backend receives the original object without warning. Either reject
conflicting controls or provide an explicit no-op/reuse API whose receipt
states that nothing was changed.

### MXR-080-0767 — Multiprocessing workers can hang the driver forever

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/multiprocessing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 50–117, 183–193, and 251–268
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

All response paths use blocking `conn.recv()` with no poll/deadline. A worker
that remains alive but stalls, or dies without closing the inherited endpoint,
can block setup, fitting, or shutdown indefinitely; even `close()` waits on a
reply before its bounded process join. Use pollable deadlines, verify process
liveness, terminate on timeout, and make shutdown bounded.

### MXR-080-0768 — Torchrun broadcasts full folded state to every rank before fitting on root

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/torchrun.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 150–205
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_gather_object` is implemented with `all_gather_object`, materializing every
rank's payload on every rank. `_fold_value_and_share` then broadcasts the full
combined sufficient statistic to all ranks, although only root uses it for the
M-step, before broadcasting the model again. This defeats root-only memory
scaling and can OOM every worker on the state the design says root alone folds.
Gather only to root and broadcast only the resulting model (or a deliberately
sharded result).

### MXR-080-0769 — Distributed initialization accepts probabilities that select no valid experiment

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`, `mpi.py`, `multiprocessing.py`, `ray_data.py`, `resilient_em.py`, and `torchrun.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `pysp_seq_initialize` implementations
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Initialization probability `p` is not required to be finite and within
`[0,1]`. Negative values select no observations, values above one select all,
and NaN selects none, after which estimators may emit a normal-looking model
from zero effective observations. Validate the common initialization contract
once before dispatch and require a supported nonempty result.

### MXR-080-0770 — Checkpoint replacement can leave a stale success marker over corrupted data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/dcp_checkpoint.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 84–111, 140–180, and 265–298
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Saving to an existing directory preserves its old `_SUCCESS` marker while DCP
overwrites files in that same directory. If the new write fails partway, the
old marker still certifies a mixture of old and partially replaced state as
complete—the comments assert the opposite but only the marker replacement is
atomic, not the checkpoint generation. Write each generation to a fresh
directory, verify it, and atomically publish a pointer/rename.

### MXR-080-0771 — Checkpoint completeness has no content integrity or safe metadata boundary

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/dcp_checkpoint.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 93–111 and 182–232
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The manifest lists sidecar names but includes no sizes/digests, and loading
uses `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` on rank metadata. A truncated,
substituted, or untrusted sidecar is neither authenticated nor safely decoded,
and model/optimizer mutation happens before sidecar validation and scheduler
restore. Validate the complete generation before mutating live state, use a
safe typed metadata format, and include integrity digests.

### MXR-080-0772 — The alternate async checkpoint path has no atomic completion protocol

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/fault_tolerant_training.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 202–263
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The background path writes DCP state and then writes `loader_state.json`
directly into the target directory, with no temporary generation, success
marker, atomic replacement, or integrity manifest. `load_checkpoint` can read
a partial tensor generation, a partial JSON file, or tensor and loader state
from different saves. Consolidate on the transactional DCP checkpoint
implementation rather than maintaining a second incompatible format.

### MXR-080-0773 — Respawning one rank rewinds the entire live training job

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/fault_tolerant_training.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 496–528
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`respawn_rank` loads the checkpoint into the canonical model and optimizer and
replaces every rank's loader state, despite documenting that the job is
otherwise untouched. If surviving ranks have advanced since the checkpoint,
their model update and data positions are rolled back; subsequent steps can
repeat data and discard committed optimization. Restore a replica/rank-local
state without mutating the current canonical generation, or perform a
coordinated whole-job rollback with an explicit generation receipt.

### MXR-080-0774 — Simulated elastic steps ignore rendezvous timeouts and accept invalid worlds

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/fault_tolerant_training.py`

- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`world_size`, loader coordinates, batch dimensions, and advancement are not
validated. `run_step` ignores the boolean returned by `wait_started`; a slow
rank can be treated as ready, then later classified dead by another fixed
timeout, while its thread continues. Arbitrary out-of-world IDs in
`kill_ranks` are also added to dead state. Validate the world and use one
cancelable deadline/state machine for every rank.

### MXR-080-0775 — EM observability overwrites duplicate ranks while double-counting their totals

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/em_observability.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 47–144 and 166–407
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Rank/round records admit negative and non-finite time, byte, and observation
values. Per-round dictionaries silently overwrite duplicate rank records, but
whole-fit totals sum every duplicate, so the same report can show one rank
timing and double-count its work. Require unique `(round, rank)` identities
and validate monotone, finite, nonnegative measurements before aggregation.

### MXR-080-0776 — Rebalancing assigns a zero-duration rank zero work

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/em_observability.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 272–299
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

When some ranks have positive durations and one reports zero, inverse-time
weights assign the zero-time rank weight zero. That is the opposite of the
documented throughput interpretation (or, if zero means invalid/empty, it
requires explicit handling). The all-zero special case also returns weights
summing to one although the documented normalization sums to rank count.
Reject invalid timing or define a consistent censored/empty-rank model.

### MXR-080-0777 — Multi-worker recovery can choose another already-dead worker

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/resilient_em.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 344–365 and 382–463
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

All failed workers are identified first, but they are retired one at a time.
While recovering the first failed worker's shards, `_recover_shard` chooses
from `_conns` excluding only the historical blacklist, so another worker known
failed in the same round remains eligible. Recovery can send work to that dead
process and block or fail instead of selecting a survivor. Remove the entire
failed set from eligibility before any recomputation.

### MXR-080-0778 — Migrated shards invalidate the promised bit-identical canonical fold order

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/resilient_em.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 118–125 and 433–472
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

A worker with multiple migrated shards folds them into one payload. The driver
sorts that aggregate by only its minimum shard ID, so shards cannot be
interleaved with other workers' shards in global shard-ID order. Because
floating-point combine is not associative, this contradicts the module's
bit-identical recovery guarantee and can change estimates after migration.
Return one payload per logical shard or use an exact/order-independent
accumulation representation.

### MXR-080-0779 — The “resilient” backend has no timeout and leaves key operations unrecovered

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/resilient_em.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 303–365 and 482–538
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Every pipe receive is unbounded, so a stalled-but-live worker defeats failure
recovery and shutdown. Random initialization and log-density evaluation do not
use the resilient round at all; worker failure there is not retried,
blacklisted, or recomputed. Add deadlines/heartbeats and apply one recovery
protocol to every public distributed operation.

### MXR-080-0780 — SDC’s claimed zero-false-positive bitwise test is not portable

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/sdc_audit.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–50 and 197–219
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The audit assumes identical IEEE results and identical pickle bytes across
different physical workers. Heterogeneous CPUs/GPUs, BLAS kernels, fused
operations, thread reductions, library versions, and serialization order can
legitimately differ bitwise while representing equivalent sufficient
statistics. The detector can therefore quarantine healthy ranks despite its
zero-false-positive claim. Compare a canonical typed statistic with
operation-aware tolerances/digests and record the determinism envelope that
was actually established.

### MXR-080-0781 — SDC quarantine can destroy the only replicas before migration is safe

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/sdc_audit.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 295–306 and 340–359
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

On one mismatch the code retires both workers sequentially. Shards from the
first suspect may be migrated onto the second suspect before that worker is
retired; with only two workers the second retirement has no destination and
fails after destructive state changes. Quarantine should first compute and
validate a survivor placement (or obtain a third witness), then commit all
migrations atomically.

### MXR-080-0782 — The finite-statistic watchdog misses invalid states after key tying

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/sdc_audit.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 97–131
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The recursive guard excludes complex scalars, sets, dataclass/object fields,
and other numeric containers, and it checks only after `combine`. The later
`key_merge`/`key_replace` transformation can introduce non-finite shared state
without a final check. Define a typed statistic traversal and validate the
fully tied value immediately before it is accepted.

### MXR-080-0783 — Unequal token shards can deadlock distributed neural training

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/torch_neural.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 79–87 and 137–186
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Ranks receive contiguous token slices whose lengths may differ, then each rank
independently iterates all local batches. DDP/FSDP collectives require the same
number and order of backward calls on every rank; a one-batch difference
leaves one rank waiting forever. Establish a globally equal step schedule with
padding/drop semantics and receipt the number of tokens excluded or masked.

### MXR-080-0784 — Gradient accumulation optimizes the wrong objective for unequal batch sizes

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/torch_training.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 225–310
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each batch mean loss is divided by the fixed accumulation-step count. When a
last batch or rank has a different token count, this averages batch means
rather than computing the mean over all accumulated tokens; the receipt,
however, reports a token-weighted loss. Partial correction cannot repair the
relative weighting. Accumulate token-summed losses/gradients and normalize by
the actual global token count at commit.

### MXR-080-0785 — Closing a training session silently performs an optimizer update

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/torch_training.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 312–375
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`close()` calls `finish_accumulation()`, which rescales pending gradients and
steps the optimizer. Resource cleanup therefore mutates the model and
scheduler, and the returned receipt is discarded, so an implicit partial
training step is neither requested nor observable. Make close non-mutating;
require an explicit commit-or-discard decision for pending accumulation.

### MXR-080-0786 — Restart continuity is checked one step late

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/training_health.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 276–365
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The documented call convention marks the first observed step after restart
with `restart=True`. The implementation instead stores that step and labels
only `step + 1` as post-restart. A probe with stable losses followed by a large
loss at the restart step reported ordinary `loss_spike`; the following step
was labeled `restart_discontinuity`. Evaluate the marked observation against
the pre-restart baseline before adding it.

### MXR-080-0787 — Training-health configuration can make monitoring permanently ineffective

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/training_health.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 63–203 and 239–399
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Zero/negative heads and model dimensions, a window shorter than
`min_periods`, non-finite/negative thresholds and peak throughput, nonpositive
step times, duplicate/non-monotone steps, and negative heartbeat thresholds
are not coherently rejected. Several such configurations yield NaN MFU or a
baseline that can never warm up while the report remains valid-looking.
Validate the monitoring experiment at construction and reject invalid samples.

### MXR-080-0788 — A Ray handle starts a runtime that it never releases

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/ray_data.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 60–101 and 154–164
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The handle records `_owns_ray = not ray.is_initialized()` and may call
`ray.init`, but `close()` is an unconditional no-op. Object references are
also retained without explicit release. A supposedly scoped handle can thus
leave worker processes and object-store memory alive for the process lifetime.
Shut down only owned runtimes and release owned object references
idempotently.

### MXR-080-0789 — “Capped” categorical profiling can exceed its cap and change the distribution

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/automatic/profiling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 644–660
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The value-array reconstruction assigns at least one representative to every
key, so when support cardinality exceeds the requested cap the result exceeds
that cap. Rounding and forced minimum replication also reweight the empirical
distribution, which then drives fit and validation as though it were the
original sample. Use weighted sufficient statistics or a bounded,
probability-preserving sampling scheme and receipt any approximation.

### MXR-080-0790 — Option helpers leak resources and silently erase non-invertible mappings

- **Severity:** Medium

`text_file` opens a descriptor without an ownership/close protocol,
`get_inv_map` silently keeps only one key when values collide, and
`least_occurring` accepts negative/non-finite count or percentage controls.
These helpers are public utilities and their normal-looking outputs conceal
lost entries or invalid selection. Use context-managed ownership, reject
non-bijective inversion unless multi-maps are requested, and validate limits.

### MXR-080-0791 — Affinity health reports NaN diagnostics instead of insufficient evidence

- **Severity:** High

Empty or too-small inputs and infeasible perplexity can reach reductions that
emit NaN receipt fields without a failed/insufficient-evidence verdict. A
machine consumer can therefore receive a populated health object whose
numbers are undefined. Establish minimum sample and feasible-neighborhood
contracts and use a typed abstention when health cannot be measured.

### MXR-080-0792 — Spark streaming failures leak broadcasts and cached intermediate data

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1126–1157
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Estimator/model broadcasts and the cached partition result are destroyed only
on the successful tail path. Any worker, collection, deserialization, combine,
or key-merge failure skips cleanup and leaves cluster memory resident. Put
every owned distributed resource behind `try/finally` or a scoped handle and
surface cleanup failure separately from the computation failure.

### MXR-080-0793 — Lightning mini-batch controls are inaccessible through the registered backend

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/lightning_data.py` and `mixle/utils/parallel/planner.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `lightning_data.py` 35–136; `planner.py` 652–706 and 829–832

- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The generic `encoded_data` API and Lightning backend factory do not pass
`batch_size`, shuffle, or seed, so users of the registered backend receive
implicit defaults and cannot specify its defining behavior. Each epoch also
rebuilds a generator at the same seed, repeating the identical shuffle order
rather than a deterministic epoch-specific order. Expose typed backend options
and derive reproducible per-epoch seeds.

### MXR-080-0794 — World-size-changing restore reuses arbitrary old rank-local state

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/parallel/dcp_checkpoint.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 182–232
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

With `allow_world_size_change=True`, a new rank loads sidecar
`rank % saved_world_size`. Multiple new ranks can therefore receive the same
old loader/scheduler metadata even though its data ownership no longer
matches. RNG restoration is skipped, but incompatible rank-local state is
still returned without a rebuild contract. Separate global from rank-local
metadata and require the caller to repartition or explicitly transform local
state before resume.

### MXR-080-0795 — Component-scattered sampling returns uninitialized or missing draws

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/_sampling.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 16–48
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The helper validates neither `size`, component-state length and integrality,
component bounds, nor each sampler's returned batch shape. An out-of-range
component leaves `None` in the list path and unwritten memory in the
`np.empty` array path. The bounded probe returned `[0, None]` for component
state `[0, 2]` with one sampler. Reject an invalid assignment before allocating
output and validate every component draw before scattering it.

### MXR-080-0796 — Backend generation failures are misreported as unsupported engines

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/backend.py` and `mixle/stats/compute/kernel.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `backend.py` 45–57; `kernel.py` 91–102
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`backend_seq_log_density` catches every exception from declaration-generated
scoring and converts it to `BackendScoringError`. `GenericKernel` can then
fall back to a different scorer. Invalid data, shape errors, arithmetic
failures, and bugs inside a declared formula are therefore indistinguishable
from absence of a backend. Capability decline needs a narrow typed exception;
execution errors must retain their original type and fail closed.

### MXR-080-0797 — Encoded-data planning metadata is trusted and can become stale after transfer

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/encoded.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 20–55 and 72–98
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`EncodedData` accepts negative or false counts, arbitrary `nbytes`, an engine
that need not own the payload, and an encoder unrelated to it. `from_data`
computes byte size before engine transfer, so dtype conversion can make the
planner-visible size disagree with resident memory. Validate non-negative
counts, derive metadata from the final payload, and provide an encoder-level
row-count invariant rather than trusting caller assertions.

### MXR-080-0798 — The common sampling API has incompatible size contracts

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sampling_api.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 49–103

The entry point does not validate that `size` is a non-negative integer.
Latent posteriors turn a negative size into an empty successful list, relations
and distribution samplers receive the original value, and non-integral sizes
fail at unrelated depths. Establish one public size contract before dispatch
so all supported model kinds agree on scalar, zero, and invalid requests.

### MXR-080-0799 — Sampling extension registration is duplicate-prone and process-global

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sampling_api.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 35–46 and 86–91
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Registration blindly appends handlers to a mutable global list without
identity, replacement, removal, ordering ownership, or synchronization.
Repeated imports can execute a handler multiple times, and a handler may
mutate state before returning `SAMPLE_UNHANDLED`. Use typed registrations with
stable IDs, reject duplicates, snapshot under a lock for dispatch, and define
whether handlers must be side-effect-free when declining.

### MXR-080-0800 — Decomposition hooks can fail and silently become atomic

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/decomposition.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 42–111
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Any `TypeError` raised inside an instance's `decomposition()` implementation
is swallowed and replaced by an atomic decomposition. The descriptor and
registry also accept non-positive unit counts, incoherent axis/reduction
combinations, invalid engine axes, duplicate role names, and silent
overwrites. A planner can consequently replicate a model that was intended to
shard. Validate descriptors and distinguish signature mismatch from an
exception raised by the hook body.

### MXR-080-0801 — Capability metadata can overclaim execution and hide hook defects

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/capabilities.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 22–54 and 75–118

Capability objects accept empty, duplicate, or unknown engine names and
inconsistent `numpy_only_reason`/kernel states. A class-level
`compute_capabilities` whose body raises `TypeError` is silently ignored, and
registrations overwrite without conflict detection. Since this metadata gates
