### MXR-080-0802 — Numerics receipts call first-order approximations valid upper bounds

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/error_receipts.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–55
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The naive formula uses `(n-1)*eps*sumabs` instead of the rigorous
`gamma_(n-1)` factor and omits rounding in receipt accumulation and partition
combination. The documentation nevertheless calls the result a valid upper
bound and says the receipt fields compose exactly, although `abs_total` is
itself a floating-point sum. Either implement a conservative bound that
includes receipt and combine operations or label this explicitly as a
first-order estimate that cannot certify error.

### MXR-080-0803 — Compensated reductions silently truncate and accept non-finite receipts

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/error_receipts.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 58–127
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Weighted reduction uses `zip`, silently discarding unmatched values or
weights. The accumulator accepts NaN/infinite values and weights, arbitrary
negative counts through direct construction, and incompatible compensated
modes during `combine`; it then emits a receipt without an invalid-state
verdict. Enforce equal cardinality and finite inputs, validate merged modes,
and make an invalid numerical receipt impossible to mistake for a bound.

### MXR-080-0804 — Conditioning receipts sanitize invalid covariance inputs

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/error_receipts.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 130–186
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The helper does not require a finite, non-empty, square, symmetric covariance
or a finite positive degeneracy threshold. It silently symmetrizes any square
matrix, potentially turning a materially nonsymmetric input into an
authoritative eigenspectrum. Validate the covariance contract and report
symmetry error separately from conditioning rather than erasing it.

### MXR-080-0805 — Categorical latent posteriors fabricate residual probability

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/posterior.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 113–150
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Only rank is validated. Negative, NaN, non-normalized, empty-width, and
support-length-mismatched responsibility matrices are admitted. Sampling
unconditionally sets the last CDF entry to one, so a row `[0.2, 0.2]` sampled
the last label about 80% of the time in the bounded probe. Require finite
non-negative row-stochastic probabilities and matching support; do not turn
missing mass into a real latent state.

### MXR-080-0806 — Structured posterior constructors do not establish probability laws

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/posterior.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 153–306
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The Markov posterior validates neither shapes nor finite normalized initial
and transition laws and crashes on empty sequences; impossible messages can
flow into generic softmax fallbacks. The LDA posterior accepts non-positive
Dirichlet parameters, mismatched/non-stochastic `phi`, and non-integral,
negative, or length-mismatched counts. Validate each law at construction and
use an explicit impossible-posterior result instead of fabricated marginals.

### MXR-080-0807 — Torch compatibility paths swallow arbitrary kernel failures

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/torch_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 54–67, 77–95, 117–142, and 239–246
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Four broad `except Exception` blocks convert any Torch scoring, posterior, or
accumulation failure into a legacy CPU computation. A backend arithmetic bug,
device failure, invalid data, or estimator mismatch can therefore return a
different algorithm's result as success. Fall back only on a typed unsupported
capability before execution and preserve the original failure once a selected
kernel starts.

### MXR-080-0808 — Torch compatibility controls are accepted but ignored or rewritten

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/torch_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 144–175 and 203–237
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`fit_map` accepts `w_alpha` but never uses or forwards it. `fit` forces at least
one iteration with `max(1, int(max_its))`, so a zero-iteration request mutates
the model, and fractional or negative iteration controls are silently coerced.
Reject invalid controls, honor zero as a no-op if supported, and either map
`w_alpha` to the weight prior or remove it with an explicit compatibility
error.

### MXR-080-0809 — Exponential-family statistics leave the selected engine

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/exp_family.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 35–65 and 118–125
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Multi-block sufficient statistics are converted through `engine.to_numpy` and
combined with `np.concatenate`, despite the class claiming Torch operation
and autograd friendliness. This detaches tensors, moves device-resident data
to the host, and returns a NumPy array only when a family has multiple
statistic blocks. Use an engine-owned concatenate operation and preserve
device, dtype, and gradient lineage uniformly.

### MXR-080-0810 — “Exact” exponential-family derivatives are unguarded approximations

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/exp_family.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 164–202
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`mean_parameters` calls central finite differences an exact gradient, does not
validate `eps`, and may step outside the natural-parameter domain.
Monte-Carlo fallbacks accept zero/negative sample counts, while Fisher
estimation with fewer than two samples returns undefined covariance without
uncertainty or failure. Expose analytic/autodiff/finite-difference/Monte-Carlo
methods distinctly and validate domain, budget, and numerical error.

### MXR-080-0811 — Product exponential-family maps silently omit components

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/exp_family.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 216–281
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_split` does not verify that an extractor returns exactly one batch per
component, and three methods consume components and parts with truncating
`zip`. A short extraction can therefore compute a lower-dimensional statistic
or density while presenting it as the full product law. Check component
cardinality, equal row counts, and per-block widths before performing any
canonical operation.

### MXR-080-0812 — Gradient prior routing silently pads and discards specifications

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/gradient.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 33–184 and 356–362
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Every structural prior normalizer pads missing entries with `None` and
truncates extra entries. Unknown mapping keys are also generally ignored.
Thus a misspelled, short, or over-complete scientific prior can optimize a
different model without a diagnostic. Require exact structural alignment by
default and make any intentional broadcast or partial prior an explicit
mode with a receipt.

### MXR-080-0813 — Gradient priors admit invalid hyperparameters and shapes

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/gradient.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 187–212, 247–257, 305–327, and 614–625
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Dirichlet concentrations are neither checked positive/finite nor matched to
the logits width; tensor broadcasting can apply the wrong prior. Beta and
Normal-Gamma controls similarly accept invalid alpha, beta, kappa, and
non-finite values, producing NaN objectives or improper priors without an
explicit request. Validate every hyperparameter and require exact labeled or
positional shape agreement before optimization.

### MXR-080-0814 — Density representative APIs accept empty and undefined budgets

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/pdist.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 355–419
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`density_quantile` accepts `n_samples <= 0` and then indexes an empty order.
`density_enumeration` accepts invalid point/sample counts, may return one item
for a negative requested count, and uses object identity when a value cannot
be frozen, so equal representatives are not deduplicated. Non-finite scores
are sorted without an invalid-sample policy. Validate budgets and require a
stable equality/key contract for approximate support representatives.

### MXR-080-0815 — Nucleus enumeration can be non-terminating on invalid targets

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/pdist.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 696–750
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`top_p` does not validate finite `p`, probability bounds, `max_items`, or
enumerated log probabilities. `p=NaN` or `p>1` without a cap can consume an
infinite support forever, while `max_items <= 0` still consumes and returns one
item. Validate controls up front, enforce finite non-positive log masses and a
hard termination policy, and report when a cap prevents reaching the target.

### MXR-080-0816 — Key compatibility validation does not compare the two protocols

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/pdist.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1142–1343
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Estimator and accumulator keys are collected into separate registries and
never compared. Estimator signatures omit private state and array contents,
so materially different priors/settings can appear compatible. NaN keys do
not compare equal, while Boolean and integer keys collide under Python
mapping equality. Canonicalize permitted key types, include all
result-affecting configuration, and cross-check estimator sites against the
accumulators that actually merge them.

### MXR-080-0817 — Sequence encoding and convenience scoring have invalid edge contracts

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sequence.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 32–119 and 210–232
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Zero `chunk_size` divides by zero, negative chunk controls silently collapse
to one chunk, and no conservation check establishes that declared chunk
counts match encoded rows. The raw `log_density` convenience function calls
`np.concatenate([])` for an empty input instead of returning an empty vector.
Validate chunk controls and make empty input a defined backend-independent
case.

### MXR-080-0818 — Local and distributed sequence estimation pass different observation counts

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sequence.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 254–342
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Both paths compute `nobs`, but Spark calls `estimator.estimate(nobs, ...)`
while the local path calls `estimator.estimate(None, ...)`. Estimators that
use observation count can therefore produce backend-dependent models from
the same sufficient statistics. Pass the actual count everywhere and validate
that chunk metadata and weight lengths justify it.

### MXR-080-0819 — Spark sequence initialization indexes serialized bytes as seeds

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sequence.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 382–420
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The driver broadcasts `pickle.dumps(seeds)`, but each worker constructs its
RNG from `seeds_broadcast.value[split_index]` without unpickling. Partitions
therefore receive bytes from the pickle stream, usually small repeated
integers, rather than the generated seed vector. Broadcast the numeric array
directly or deserialize it once per worker and test deterministic,
partition-distinct initialization.

### MXR-080-0820 — Scalar estimation validates keys but never applies parameter tying

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sequence.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 532–606
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`estimate` calls `validate_estimator_keys` but neither its local nor Spark
branch performs `key_merge`/`key_replace` before the M-step. The analogous
sequence-estimation and initialization paths do. A keyed model fitted through
this public API is silently untied. Use the shared merge helper exactly once
after the full accumulator reduction on every backend.

### MXR-080-0821 — Spark sequence drivers leak resources and mutate caller lineage

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/sequence.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 86–97, 144–159, 189–201, 283–328, 382–433, and 568–595
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Several encoder/model/estimator/seed broadcasts are never destroyed, and
cleanup in the fitting paths is not protected by `finally`. Exceptions leak
executor and driver memory. Successful fitting also calls
`enc_data.localCheckpoint()` on caller-owned RDDs as an undocumented side
effect. Scope and release every owned Spark object and leave lineage mutation
to an explicit persistence policy.

### MXR-080-0822 — Mixture fast paths disagree on impossible and non-finite evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/kernel.py`, `mixle/stats/compute/stacked.py`, `mixle/stats/compute/fused_kernels.py`, `mixle/stats/compute/fused_codegen.py`, and `mixle/stats/compute/fused_nested.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `kernel.py` 288–324; `stacked.py` 337–399; `fused_kernels.py` 1293–1330; `fused_codegen.py` 1282–1319 and 1380–1407; `fused_nested.py` 147–207
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

All-impossible rows are variously assigned prior weights or a uniform
posterior, while `+inf` and NaN maxima are sometimes treated as the same case
and overwritten. Scoring may report `-inf` as the evidence while the E-step
still accumulates fabricated component statistics. Define one typed
impossible-evidence policy, preserve a unique `+inf` winner when mathematically
valid, and never let NaN become a posterior.

### MXR-080-0823 — Generated-kernel fallback catches data errors as capability decline

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/kernel.py` and `mixle/stats/compute/stacked.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `kernel.py` 257–288 and 329–395; `stacked.py` 255–289 and 492–520
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Generated accumulation catches any `ValueError` from scoring, posterior
formation, statistic generation, or shape checks and runs the host
accumulator. Stacked factories similarly treat arbitrary `ValueError` as a
reason to select a fallback. Invalid inputs and implementation bugs can
therefore change algorithms instead of failing. Capability negotiation must
finish before execution and use a dedicated decline exception.

### MXR-080-0824 — Local DTensor shard metadata assumes one contiguous chunk

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/stacked.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 51–98 and 584–629
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`local_value` converts all local data but `_local_component_bounds` reads only
the first entry from a private chunk-list API and reports one contiguous
`start/stop`. A rank holding multiple or non-contiguous chunks will label its
concatenated statistics as the first contiguous range, sending component
M-steps to the wrong estimators. Represent explicit global indices/ranges and
validate them against every local statistic tensor.

### MXR-080-0825 — Nested fusion equates model shape with encoding compatibility

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_nested.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 64–134 and 356–385
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Homogeneity compares only recursive type/template shape. Components with the
same shape but parameter-dependent or otherwise unequal encoders are assigned
one shared slot, and `_fill_slots` repeatedly overwrites that slot so the last
component's encoding is used for every component. Require encoder equality or
an explicit shared-encoding capability; otherwise retain per-component
encodings.

### MXR-080-0826 — Fused accumulation silently truncates rows on weight mismatch

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_codegen.py` and `mixle/stats/compute/fused_nested.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `fused_codegen.py` 1357–1473 and 1651–1845; `fused_nested.py` 298–354 and 452–502
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Generated E-step loops take their row count from `weights.shape[0]`, not the
encoded data. No wrapper validates equal lengths or one-dimensional finite
weights. In the bounded probe, a two-row Gaussian encoding with a one-row
weight vector returned statistics for only the first row without error.
Longer weights can drive unchecked Numba reads beyond data arrays. Validate
all dimensions before entering compiled code.

### MXR-080-0827 — Public fused scorers can assign density outside a model's support

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_codegen.py` and `mixle/stats/compute/fused_nested.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `fused_codegen.py` 163–239 and 1044–1119; `fused_nested.py` 147–181
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Several inlined expressions rely on an upstream encoder to validate support
and omit the canonical scorer's support branch. Direct fused scoring of
encoded `-1` under an exponential returned `1.0` while the sequence scorer
returned `-inf`; geometric encodings `0` and `1.5` likewise received finite
scores. Since these are public encoded-data functions, validate their encoded
domain or make a validated-encoding token part of the contract.

### MXR-080-0828 — Fused source caching can retain partial modules or stale extension code

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_codegen.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 75–149, 865–947, and 1122–1233
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The loader inserts a module into `sys.modules` before executing it; on import
failure the broad fallback leaves that partial module installed, so the next
call can fail at `getattr` instead of recompiling. Separately, the plan/cache
signature records template names but not template code or registration
version, while public registration permits duplicates. A changed extension
with the same name can therefore reuse incompatible compiled code. Remove
failed modules and fingerprint validated template semantics in every cache key.

### MXR-080-0829 — Fused marshalling does not validate cross-factor row geometry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_codegen.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1477–1554
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The first eligible factor determines `n_rows`; later data arrays, bridged score
tables, categorical tables, chain indices, and parameter component widths are
not checked against it. Generated Numba loops use unchecked indexing, so a
malformed or incompatible composite encoding can silently read the wrong row
or beyond an array boundary. Validate every data/parameter/table dimension and
index range in Python before compilation or invocation.

### MXR-080-0830 — Legacy compiled mixtures trust replacement model and gamma geometry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_kernels.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1220–1385
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The builder fixes structure and `K` at construction, but scoring and
accumulation accept any later `model` without checking type tree, component
count, dimensions, or encoder compatibility. `weighted_suff_stats` likewise
does not require `gamma.shape == (n, K)`. These arrays enter bounds-unchecked
Numba loops, so short dimensions can produce silent corruption or invalid
memory reads. Bind a structural fingerprint to the encoding and validate all
runtime arrays before dispatch.

### MXR-080-0831 — Compiled-mixture thread pools are never closed

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/fused_kernels.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1258–1291 and 1334–1364
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Growing the requested thread count replaces `_pool` without shutting down the
old executor, and the class exposes no `close` or context-manager lifecycle.
Repeated model construction or thread-count growth can retain worker threads
and their resources indefinitely. Close superseded pools and provide an
idempotent explicit lifecycle.

### MXR-080-0832 — Declaration registration does not make declarations safe to execute

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/declarations.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 30–176 and 1154–1387
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`register_declaration` silently overwrites by type and does not call
`validate_declaration`. Validation itself checks names and callable presence
but not parameter existence, statistic shapes, finite outputs, child cycles,
or consistency among runtime/fixed-base flags. Generated execution can thus
consume an invalid declaration that the registry presents as authoritative.
Validate atomically, reject conflicting registrations, and add executable
shape/domain conformance checks.

### MXR-080-0833 — Generated compilation failures are globally cached as unsupported

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/declarations.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 244–290 and 604–664
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Diagnostics catch every exponential-family failure and silently switch to a
backend hook. Generic Numba construction catches every unexpected exception,
returns `None`, and stores that result in a process-global per-type cache.
A transient dependency or tracing defect therefore permanently removes the
capability for that process and hides its cause. Cache only validated
unsupported outcomes and retain typed diagnostics for real failures.

### MXR-080-0834 — Generated histogram statistics silently round observations

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/compute/declarations.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1489–1508
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_weighted_histogram` applies `np.rint(...).astype(int64)` without checking that
values are finite exact integers or that weights match and are finite.
Fractional sufficient statistics can therefore be reassigned to neighboring
count bins, while NaN/overflow conversion is platform-dependent. Validate the
declared histogram domain and lengths before aggregation.

### MXR-080-0835 — Missing-data helpers erase modeled missingness and estimator identity

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/missing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 65–94
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Rebuilding a `CompositeEstimator` drops its merge `keys`, and unwrapping a
fitted composite rebuilds the product without preserving wrapper identity.
More seriously, `unwrap_marginalized` removes every `OptionalDistribution`,
including one with an explicit nonzero `p` that models informative
missingness. A bounded probe showed that an optional model with `p=0.25` was
silently returned as its Gaussian child. Only wrappers proven to represent
MAR marginalization may be stripped, and all structural metadata must survive.

### MXR-080-0836 — SQUAREM packing revives impossible states and is not lossless

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/parameter_packing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 31–52 and 123–166
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Zero categorical probabilities and zero mixture weights are replaced by
`1e-300` before taking logs and are positive after unpacking. The advertised
lossless round trip therefore changes support and can reactivate an impossible
component. Rebuilders also omit leaf merge keys and other constructor
configuration. A probe round-tripped exact zeros into positive values.
Represent boundary coordinates exactly or declare and enforce a strictly
interior model contract; preserve every behavior-bearing field.

### MXR-080-0837 — SQUAREM accepts structurally different leaves and unsafe coordinates

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/parameter_packing.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 31–52 and 116–181
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Leaf checks compare only Python type, not support, width, or labels, and
`pack()` never verifies that its final vector has the frozen width. A
same-type categorical model with changed support can therefore emit a vector
that `unpack()` interprets against another model. Arbitrary sortable labels
are also sorted directly, so mixed string/integer support raises `TypeError`,
and non-finite theta values can flow into exponentiation and normalization.
Bind packing to a full structural fingerprint and reject non-finite or
wrong-width coordinates.

### MXR-080-0838 — Conjugate input normalization admits incompatible array geometry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 57–76 and 134–148
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The common univariate input helper does not require a one-dimensional data
array or a one-dimensional weight vector; it checks only `w.shape[0]`.
Broadcasting or matrix-valued weights can consequently change dot products
and posterior shapes. Posterior samplers also coerce arbitrary `size` with
`int()` and do not require a non-negative integer. Validate event rank,
exact weight shape, finite non-negative mass, and sampling cardinality at the
public boundary.

### MXR-080-0839 — Conjugate builders update on observations outside their likelihood support

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 260–268, 361–379, 706–714, and 778–934
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Geometric, Poisson, exponential, log-Gaussian, Rayleigh, half-normal, Gamma,
inverse-Gamma, inverse-Gaussian, Pareto, and negative-binomial routes omit
some or all of their support checks. Invalid values are squared, logged,
divided, or treated as counts and can yield a plausible posterior or NaN
hyperparameters. A fractional Poisson observation produced a finite posterior
and evidence, while a negative half-normal observation produced an
authoritative posterior. Each builder must validate the exact likelihood
support before calculating sufficient statistics.

### MXR-080-0840 — Categorical conjugate inference can discard observations and weights

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 385–493
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The generic categorical counter zip-truncates unequal data and weight
sequences and validates neither finite nor non-negative weights. When the
likelihood already has a support map, observations outside it remain in the
temporary counter but are omitted from the posterior count vector. A probe
updated a one-state categorical model with an out-of-support label and
returned the unchanged prior with log evidence zero. Empty integer-categorical
data also eagerly evaluates `x.min()` inside `getattr` and crashes even when
the distribution supplies `min_val`.

### MXR-080-0841 — Conjugate hyperparameters are not consistently required to define proper priors

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 294–379, 499–703, 720–920, and 1000–1067
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Unlike the Beta parser, Gamma-rate, inverse-Gamma, Normal-Inverse-Gamma,
Normal-Inverse-Wishart, diagonal, and von-Mises routes do not consistently
require finite positive hyperparameters, valid dimensions, or positive
definite scale matrices. Invalid priors can reach posterior means, evidence,
and samplers without an improper-prior opt-in. Centralize family-specific
prior validation and prove every returned posterior is proper.

### MXR-080-0842 — Multivariate conjugate inference does not establish matrix validity

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 595–703 and 988–994
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The multivariate builder accepts empty/non-finite data, multidimensional or
mismatched weights, invalid prior mean geometry, non-positive kappa, invalid
degrees of freedom, and non-symmetric or non-positive-definite `psi`. Its
log-determinant helper discards the determinant sign. The diagonal builder
likewise infers shape without checking finite data or agreement with the
likelihood dimension. Validate all matrix geometry and use Cholesky-based SPD
checks before emitting an NIW posterior or evidence.

### MXR-080-0843 — The full-Bayesian posterior-predictive contract returns unmarked plug-ins

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–22, 330–337, 534–544, 760–763, 849–851, 975–977, and 1030–1032
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The module and public entry point promise full-Bayesian posterior results, but
several `posterior_predictive()` methods return a likelihood at a posterior
point estimate instead of integrating over parameters. This affects
exponential/known-shape Gamma, log-Gaussian, scale-family, diagonal-Gaussian,
known-parameter positive families, and von-Mises routes. These distributions
understate posterior uncertainty while sharing the same API as exact
predictives. Return the compound law or expose approximation semantics and
receipts in the type and result.

### MXR-080-0844 — Mixtures of conjugates lack probability and data-replay safeguards

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/conjugate.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1167–1272
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The posterior constructor does not validate non-empty aligned components,
finite simplex weights, or evidence shape. The builder normalizes
wrong-length, negative, zero-sum, and non-finite prior weights without checks;
all-`-inf` evidence becomes NaN. It also passes the same `data` object through
every component, so a one-shot iterator is consumed by the first prior and
later priors see different data. Finally, a failed numeric mean silently
substitutes the MAP component while still calling the result a posterior
mean. Materialize and validate data once and make all probability/geometry
contracts exact.

### MXR-080-0845 — Normal-Gamma parameter-prior classes accept invalid laws

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/normal_gamma.py` and `mixle/stats/bayes/multivariate_normal_gamma.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `normal_gamma.py` 27–150; `multivariate_normal_gamma.py` 38–166
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Both scalar and factorized constructors/setters accept non-finite means,
non-positive shape/rate/precision parameters, unequal vector lengths, and
non-vector arrays. Scorers then accept non-positive precision observations
and rely on broadcasting. Probes constructed a scalar law with negative
precision/shape and zero rate that scored `NaN`, and a multivariate law with
mean width two and precision width one. Validate atomically at construction,
setter, scoring, cross-entropy, and sampling boundaries.

### MXR-080-0846 — Normal-Wishart scoring accepts nonsymmetric precision matrices

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/normal_wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 82–177
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

Constructor validation does not first require vector/matrix ranks and exact
`(d,d)` shape, and `set_parameters` mutates the object before all checks
finish. Runtime scoring checks only a Cholesky factorization, which reads one
triangle and is not a symmetry test. Three nonsymmetric precision matrices
with lower off-diagonal values 1, 10, and 100 all received the same finite log
density in a bounded probe. Require finite exact geometry and symmetry before
factorization, and commit setter state only after complete validation.

### MXR-080-0847 — Symmetric-Dirichlet dimension and batch contracts are incomplete

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/symmetric_dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 39–179
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

`dim` is not required to be a positive integer, so zero, negative, boolean,
and fractional dimensions fail later in entropy or sampling. The sequence
scorer assumes a two-dimensional array and indexes `shape[1]`; one- or
higher-rank encodings fail opaquely or reduce along the wrong axes. Validate
the optional sampling dimension and require exact `(n, d)` batch geometry.

### MXR-080-0848 — Dictionary Dirichlet scoring changes dimension with observation keys

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dict_dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 43–177
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

For fixed dictionary alpha, scoring iterates the observation rather than
requiring its keys to match the parameter support. A missing concentration key
therefore produces a lower-dimensional density with a different normalizer,
while an extra key raises raw `KeyError`. A probe scored `{"a": 1}` under
`{"a": 2, "b": 3}` as log density zero. The constructor also retains the
caller's mutable dictionary by reference, allowing post-validation mutation.
Copy alpha and require exact support identity before scoring or cross-entropy.

### MXR-080-0849 — Scalar dictionary-Dirichlet information methods crash without a dimension

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dict_dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 156–183
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The class permits a scalar concentration with observation-dependent dimension,
but `cross_entropy` between two such objects calls `.keys()` on a float and
`entropy` calls `.values()`. Both raise `AttributeError` in direct probes.
Require an explicit dimension for these operations or raise a typed
unsupported-domain error rather than leaking implementation exceptions.

### MXR-080-0850 — Dirichlet scalar, sequence, and backend scorers disagree at the simplex boundary

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 389–479 and 936–961
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The scalar scorer returns the correct infinite or zero boundary density when a
coordinate is zero and its alpha is below or above one. The encoder instead
clips zero to the smallest positive float, so sequence and backend scorers
return a large finite number. For alpha `(0.5, 0.5)` and observation `(0,1)`,
the scalar result was `+inf` while both vectorized routes returned about
`353.05`. Preserve exact boundary masks and raw-support validation in every
execution path.

### MXR-080-0851 — Dirichlet accumulation treats invalid and zero coordinates as finite data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 579–772 and 936–961
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Scalar accumulation skips zero coordinates in the sum of logs, effectively
using zero rather than `-inf`; sequence accumulation uses the encoder's finite
clip. Neither route establishes a finite row-stochastic simplex, exact
dimension, weight length, or finite non-negative weight. Invalid observations
can therefore drive a finite concentration estimate, and scalar and batch
statistics disagree at boundaries. Validate before accumulation and define an
explicit policy for boundary observations whose ordinary Dirichlet
log-likelihood is infinite.

### MXR-080-0852 — Dirichlet estimation silently repairs malformed statistics and priors

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 802–933
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Estimator controls and serialized statistics are largely unvalidated.
Negative pseudo-counts are clamped to zero, a wrong-width prior statistic is
cyclically repeated or truncated with `np.resize`, non-finite mean logs are
replaced, and invalid/negative counts can still produce an authoritative
distribution. Empty accumulators fail before the nominal no-data fallback.
Reject malformed state and expose solver convergence/repair status instead of
silently fitting a different prior or dataset.

### MXR-080-0853 — Pitman-Yor raw and encoded partition inputs are not validated

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/pitman_yor.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 40–43, 108–136, and 187–257
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Raw labels are coerced to integers before counting, so distinct fractional or
string-like identifiers can be collapsed or rejected despite exchangeability.
The public sequence scorer trusts caller-supplied block-size arrays without
requiring positive integral sizes, and sequence accumulation zip-truncates
weights. Counts and histograms also accept non-finite or negative weights.
Preserve label identity and validate canonical positive-integer partitions
and exact batch geometry.

### MXR-080-0854 — Pitman-Yor estimation trusts invalid bounds and serialized histograms

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/pitman_yor.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 271–355
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`max_alpha` is not required to be finite and positive, and `estimate` accepts
arbitrary counts, histogram indices, and signed/non-finite weights. The fixed
bisection bounds assume a valid monotone likelihood and can return a boundary
value even when corrupted statistics violate that premise. Validate the
histogram invariants, solver bracket, and final optimum, and retain
convergence/boundary diagnostics.

### MXR-080-0855 — Dirichlet-process-mixture construction does not establish a mixture law

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 127–200
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Construction and `set_parameters` do not require a non-empty component list,
matching finite simplex weights, positive finite concentration, `(K,2)`
positive stick parameters, matching component priors, or compatible component
encoders. Short or malformed state reaches log weights, sampling, ELBO, and
component indexing. Validate all state atomically and bind it to a component
structure fingerprint.

### MXR-080-0856 — Dirichlet-process responsibilities fabricate or lose impossible evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 201–305 and 406–445
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Scalar and sequence posterior APIs fall back to prior weights when every
component assigns zero probability, while expected-density and ELBO paths
subtract an all-`-inf` maximum and produce NaN. Accumulators use the same
unguarded normalization. Positive infinity and NaN are inconsistently treated
as impossible. Return a typed impossible-posterior outcome and make all
scoring, posterior, ELBO, and accumulation paths agree.

### MXR-080-0857 — Weighted DPM initialization creates counts from zero-weight rows

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 454–482
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`seq_initialize` first multiplies random assignments by observation weights,
then computes remaining-stick counts as `1 - cumsum(p)`. The constant one is
not weighted, so even a zero-weight row contributes one to every second stick
count. A one-row, two-component probe with weight zero produced component
counts `[0,0]` but Beta counts `[[0,1],[0,1]]`. Compute residual mass from
unweighted assignments and multiply the entire statistic by row weight.

### MXR-080-0858 — DPM prior-tree and concentration-uncertainty terms are incomplete

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 56–83 and 625–742
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Structured prior cross-entropy zip-truncates mismatched trees. The estimator
creates a Gamma hyper-posterior for concentration, but `model_log_density`
omits the Gamma prior/posterior cross-entropy and entropy and instead uses a
point `a` in stick terms. Unsupported prior types are silently discarded.
Consequently the reported ELBO is not the stated variational model objective.
Validate exact prior structure and include or explicitly exclude every
variational factor with accurate approximation semantics.

### MXR-080-0859 — Hierarchical-DP state and setters accept incompatible model geometry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/hierarchical_dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 70–139 and 533–562
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The distribution and estimator do not require non-empty compatible
components, positive finite alpha/gamma, a length-`K` simplex beta, or
row-stochastic `(J,K)` group weights. `set_parameters` zip-truncates component
parameter lists, silently leaving unmatched atoms unchanged. Validate the
entire nested state before mutation and reject partial structural updates.

### MXR-080-0860 — HDP floors zero-probability atoms into possible states

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/hierarchical_dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 221–268, 294–328, and 393–436
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Local scoring and responsibilities replace zero group weights with `1e-300`,
and sampling replaces zero `alpha*beta` concentrations with `1e-8`. An atom
declared globally or locally impossible can therefore receive responsibility
or be sampled. These floors are not merely numerical stabilization because
they change support. Preserve exact zero masks and normalize only over
possible atoms.

### MXR-080-0861 — HDP impossible observations produce NaN responsibilities

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/hierarchical_dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 145–155, 245–269, and 393–433
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Group log density correctly returns `-inf` when an observation has no support,
but posterior and accumulator paths subtract an all-`-inf` row maximum and
normalize NaNs. Those NaNs enter group counts and component sufficient
statistics. Use a shared normalization primitive with an explicit
impossible-evidence result and prohibit updates from undefined
responsibilities.

### MXR-080-0862 — Distributed HDP merging loses group identity and is order-dependent

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/hierarchical_dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 331–506 and 593–651
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Sufficient statistics store group counts as an unlabeled list. `combine`
concatenates in reduction order and uses last-writer-wins for `prev_beta` and
`prev_alpha`; it neither verifies that partitions used the same estimate nor
preserves original group identifiers. The fitted `group_weights` rows are
later aligned positionally to input groups, so distributed reduction order can
assign one group's posterior weights to another. Carry stable group IDs and
require identical model-version metadata during merges.

### MXR-080-0863 — HDP estimation can turn malformed state into an authoritative model

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/bayes/hierarchical_dirichlet_process_mixture.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 564–651
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Estimation accepts ragged, negative, or non-finite group counts, invalid
previous beta/alpha, mismatched atom statistics, and non-positive gamma. It
then floors some terms, divides by unchecked denominators, and returns a model
whose constructor performs no validation. Validate serialized sufficient
statistics and concentration laws, check every posterior row and global
simplex, and fail closed on non-finite digamma/table-count results.

### MXR-080-0864 — Matrix-normal construction accepts nonsymmetric covariance factors

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/matrix_normal.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 37–94
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The constructor checks shapes and whether separate factorization routines
succeed, but never requires finite means or symmetric row/column covariances.
Cholesky routines consume one triangle, so a nonsymmetric matrix can pass and
then be used as a covariance and inverse in scoring. A probe constructed a
row covariance `[[1,.1],[.2,1]]` and obtained a finite density. Require finite
means and exact symmetric positive-definite covariance factors.

### MXR-080-0865 — Matrix-valued APIs do not enforce event and batch geometry

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/inverse_wishart.py`, `mixle/stats/matrix/matrix_normal.py`, and `mixle/stats/matrix/wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `inverse_wishart.py` 75–118 and 196–207; `matrix_normal.py` 80–94 and 244–255; `wishart.py` 101–133 and 370–381
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Scalar scorers, sequence scorers, and encoders do not consistently require
exact `(p,p)`, `(n,p)`, or `(N,...)` geometry and finite values. Wrong-rank or
wrong-dimension inputs reach eigensolvers, broadcasting, or `einsum`, yielding
opaque failures and in some broadcastable cases a score for the wrong event
shape. Carry dimensions in encoders and validate exact event/batch shapes
before numeric kernels.

### MXR-080-0866 — Matrix accumulators accept invalid events and unvalidated weights

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/inverse_wishart.py`, `mixle/stats/matrix/matrix_normal.py`, and `mixle/stats/matrix/wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `inverse_wishart.py` 151–193; `matrix_normal.py` 125–178; `wishart.py` 173–280
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Accumulation does not require finite exact-shaped events or finite
non-negative weights. Wishart accumulation computes positive-definiteness
from one triangle but never checks symmetry; a nonsymmetric observation
therefore produced finite scatter and log-determinant statistics. The
inverse-Wishart estimator later symmetrizes arbitrary scatter, and
matrix-normal moments likewise accept any broadcastable arrays. Invalid data
must be rejected before it can be converted into a valid-looking fitted law.

### MXR-080-0867 — Matrix-normal fitting fails on ordinary low-rank samples without a fit result

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/matrix_normal.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 199–241
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The flip-flop estimator does not establish sample-size/rank conditions,
positive iteration count, finite positive tolerance, invertibility at each
step, or convergence. A single valid `2x2` observation centers to zero scatter
and immediately raises `LinAlgError: Singular matrix`. Zero iterations instead
return identity factors unrelated to the data. Return a typed non-identifiable
or non-converged fit with diagnostics, and regularize only under an explicit
policy.

### MXR-080-0868 — Inverse-Wishart “estimation” uses an undefined moment and fabricates a fallback

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/inverse_wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 10–11 and 172–193
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The estimator uses the identity `E[X]=Psi/(df-p-1)`, which is a
method-of-moments relation rather than the inverse-Wishart likelihood MLE and
does not exist unless `df>p+1`. Yet the distribution permits lower valid
degrees of freedom and exposes the estimator; for that range it silently
returns identity scale regardless of the observations. With `p=2`, `df=2`,
and observed matrix `7I`, the fitted scale was `I`. Name and document the
method accurately, implement the likelihood estimator where intended, and
reject an undefined moment fit.

### MXR-080-0869 — Wishart degrees-of-freedom fitting ignores determinant validity and convergence

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 300–367
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The profile solver accepts invalid dimension, initialization, mean
log-determinant, and scatter log-determinant, returns the last Newton iterate
after a non-finite derivative or exhausted iterations, and records no
convergence state. The estimator discards `slogdet`'s sign before calling it.
Malformed or boundary statistics can therefore become a purported MLE or fail
only in the final constructor. Require SPD scatter, a valid bracket, and a
convergence/optimality certificate.

### MXR-080-0870 — LKJ encoding discards matrix dimension and changes the scored law

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/lkj.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 77–135 and 298–314
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`LKJDataEncoder` validates that each input is some correlation matrix but does
not retain or check its dimension. The sequence scorer receives only a log
determinant and applies the distribution's normalizer. Thus a 3x3 identity
encoded for an `LKJDistribution(dim=2, eta=1)` received finite log density
about `-0.693`, while the scalar scorer correctly returned `-inf`. Bind
encoded data to the configured dimension and preserve a per-row validity
mask.

### MXR-080-0871 — Invalid LKJ observations are converted into a boundary estimate

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/lkj.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 176–295
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The accumulator represents an invalid correlation matrix by poisoning
`sum_log_det` with `-inf`, but the estimator interprets the resulting
non-finite score as evidence that the optimum lies below its search interval
and returns the lower eta bound. A direct invalid-matrix update produced
`(count=1, sum_log_det=-inf)` and a valid-looking `eta=0.05` model. Reject
invalid events and non-finite sufficient statistics rather than mapping them
to a parameter boundary.

### MXR-080-0872 — Mutable caller arrays desynchronize matrix distributions from cached algebra

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/matrix/inverse_wishart.py`, `mixle/stats/matrix/matrix_normal.py`, and `mixle/stats/matrix/wishart.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `inverse_wishart.py` 43–65; `matrix_normal.py` 40–69; `wishart.py` 65–91
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Constructors retain `np.asarray` views of caller-owned mean/covariance/scale
arrays while caching determinants, inverses, and Cholesky factors. Mutation
after validation changes public parameters but not the cached algebra. After
changing a Wishart scale from `I` to `diag(4,1)`, the original object kept its
old log density while a freshly constructed object differed by about 1.01.
Copy immutable parameter state or make all updates transactional through
validated setters.

### MXR-080-0873 — Sphere distributions score observations outside their event space

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/bingham.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/kent.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/von_mises_fisher.py`, and `mixle/stats/directional/watson.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** `bingham.py` 92–114 and 269–280; `kent.py` 105–130 and 311–323; `von_mises_fisher.py` 235–369 and 730–760; `watson.py` 87–109 and 252–263
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Scalar, encoded, and backend scorers do not establish finite, exact-dimensional
unit-vector support. Bingham and Kent encoders silently normalize observations
while their scalar scorers do not; Watson and vMF encoders do not normalize or
validate them at all. A Bingham model scored `[2,0,0]` at about `-9.66`, while
encoding that same input first changed the score to about `-3.66`; vMF likewise
assigned finite density to `[2,0,0]`. Enforce one explicit event contract before
every scoring and accumulation path and make scalar, sequence, and backend
semantics identical.

### MXR-080-0874 — Circular encoded interfaces admit forged trigonometric observations

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/projected_normal.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/von_mises.py`, and `mixle/stats/directional/wrapped_cauchy.py`

The public encoded interfaces accept arbitrary `(cos,sin)` arrays without
requiring equal shape, finite values, or `cos²+sin²=1`. Such inputs can change
density and sufficient statistics in ways no raw angle can produce, while
shape broadcasting can silently alter the batch. Either make encoded objects
opaque and validated at construction or validate their invariants at every
public boundary.

### MXR-080-0875 — Projected-normal “stable” Mills-ratio evaluation overflows

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/projected_normal.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 47–83, 109–128, and 204–207
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The implementation evaluates `erfcx(-a/sqrt(2))` directly. For ordinary finite
parameters such as `mu=(40,0)` at the aligned direction, this overflows and both
scalar and sequence log density return positive infinity. The same expression
enters the latent-radius E-step and can become `inf/inf`. Evaluate the combined
log-density and moment ratios with sign-aware asymptotics or a log-domain
normal-CDF/Mills implementation, and reject any non-finite result.

### MXR-080-0876 — Directional constructors admit non-finite or mutable parameter state

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/bingham.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/kent.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/projected_normal.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/watson.py`, `mixle/stats/directional/wrapped_cauchy.py`, and `mixle/stats/directional/wrapped_normal.py`

Several constructors omit finite-value validation, and the matrix/vector
constructors retain caller-owned arrays while caching derived normalizers.
Projected normal, Watson, wrapped Cauchy, and wrapped normal admitted NaN
parameters; Watson stored a NaN direction; Bingham admitted NaN concentration.
Bingham and Kent parameter arrays can also be mutated after construction,
desynchronizing them from validation and cached constants. Validate all
parameters and copy or freeze every array used to derive cached algebra.

### MXR-080-0877 — Bingham normalization fails in a valid high-concentration regime

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/bingham.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 49–60 and 67–78
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The purportedly stable integral multiplies an exponentially small term by an
overflowing unscaled Bessel `iv`. A valid canonical concentration
`[-10000,0,0]` produced a NaN normalizer after hundreds of invalid
multiplications and a quadrature roundoff warning. Use a scaled/log-domain
Bessel integrand with an integration error contract, and never construct a
distribution when the normalizer is non-finite.

### MXR-080-0878 — Bingham and Kent fitting ignores invalid state and optimizer failure

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/bingham.py` and `mixle/stats/directional/kent.py`

Both accumulator families accept wrong-shaped/off-sphere/non-finite events and
negative or non-finite weights. Their estimators trust serialized count,
moment, and scatter geometry, then ignore the optimizer's success, iteration,
objective-finiteness, and identifiability state. Kent's exponential/logistic
parameterization can itself overflow. Validate sufficient-statistic
provenance and mathematical feasibility and return an explicit failed or
non-identifiable fit instead of treating the last optimizer iterate as an
MLE.

### MXR-080-0879 — Kent accepts an invalid orientation frame

### MXR-080-0880 — Bingham and Kent rejection samplers have no termination contract

### MXR-080-0881 — Uniform vMF density cumulative contradicts its own definition

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stats/directional/von_mises_fisher.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 254–322
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

For `kappa=0`, every point has equal density, so the documented
`P(p(Y) >= p(x))` is exactly one for every supported `x`. The implementation
instead orders equal-density points by `mu·x`: it returned `0` at `mu` and `1`
at `-mu`. Its advertised inverse therefore also invents density ranks that do
not exist. Special-case ties under the probability-ordering definition and
define quantile behavior for non-unique level sets.

### MXR-080-0883 — vMF accumulation rejects documented inputs and silently discards data

Scalar `update` documents a general sequence but performs `x * weight`; a

### MXR-080-0884 — vMF fitting fabricates models from malformed or absent statistics

### MXR-080-0891 — Unknown generic-set elements have contradictory likelihood semantics

### MXR-080-0892 — Bernoulli-set conjugate updates lose configured support

### MXR-080-0893 — Bernoulli inclusion probabilities are mislabeled as a simplex

- **Severity:** High

### MXR-080-0894 — Integer Bernoulli-set construction accepts non-probability laws

### MXR-080-0895 — Integer-set probability flooring destroys normalization

### MXR-080-0900 — The default edit “distribution” is not a normalized joint law

- **Severity:** Critical

### MXR-080-0901 — Edit transition matrices are not validated as stochastic kernels

### MXR-080-0903 — Forced edit transitions are scored as possible by compute backends

### MXR-080-0910 — Generic Chow–Liu construction permits uncovered reachable parent states
