### MXR-080-1347 — The duplicate-body gate misses duplicates in sibling classes

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `scripts/scan_duplicate_bodies.py`;
  `mixle/tests/duplicate_body_scan_test.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** scanner 59–95; negative control 66–85
- **State:** Reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The scanner identifies a function only as `(relative_path, function_name)`;
it omits its enclosing class and source line. Two classes in the same file
with identical same-named methods collapse to one set entry and are not
reported. A bounded planted fixture with `A.run` and `B.run`, each containing
the same seven-statement body, returned an empty group list. Record qualified
scope/line identities and add same-file sibling-class and nested-function
negative controls.

### MXR-080-1348 — Sdist normalization can destroy the only built artifact

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `scripts/normalize_sdist.py`; `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** normalizer 27–43; publish workflow 44–52
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The normalizer replaces the input archive in place with `Path.write_bytes`.
That call truncates the existing sdist before the replacement is durably
written; interruption, disk exhaustion, or a short write can leave a corrupt
artifact and no original. Write and validate a sibling temporary archive,
flush it, and atomically replace the source only after successful
decompression, tar reconstruction, compression, and integrity checks.

### MXR-080-1349 — A zero-work fuzz soak reports success

- **Severity:** Low
- **Surface:** `scripts/fuzz_fused_soak.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 23–46
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`--samples` accepts zero or negative values. The loop then performs no
checks, prints a successful completion with zero failures, and returns zero.
That can create a false soak receipt from a typo or bad automation input.
Reject non-positive sample counts and report the number of completed property
checks in machine-readable output.

### MXR-080-1350 — Example “pass” status proves process exit, not the advertised result

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `docs/example-execution-manifest.rst`; `examples/`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** execution manifest 315–356 and 543–552;
  example entry points throughout
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The release manifest defines `passed` as completing with exit code zero and
does not require an acceptance oracle for the advertised behavior. An AST
inventory found assertions in only 7 of 64 Python examples. For example,
`heterogeneous_correctness_example.py` can print that field recovery is false
and still exit zero, and `cross_modal_fit_receipt.py` unconditionally prints
that edges were recovered without checking the learned parents or predictive
thresholds. Separate “runnable” from “claim verified,” define explicit
machine-readable acceptance criteria, and fail evidence-class examples when
their claimed result is absent.

### MXR-080-1351 — The PEFT receipt does not test adapter movement or held-out improvement

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `examples/peft_lora_grad_leaf.py`;
  `mixle/tests/peft_lora_grad_leaf_smoke_test.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** example 16–20 and 92–120; smoke test 34–55
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The example says only LoRA matrices moved and held-out likelihood improved.
It never snapshots LoRA parameters before fitting: `lora_moved` is merely
their post-fit absolute magnitude, which can be positive at initialization.
It also evaluates `before_ll` and `after_ll` on the same training sequences,
not held-out data. The smoke test repeats both mistakes. Snapshot and compare
every trainable adapter tensor, use a disjoint deterministic evaluation set,
and make the receipt report both changes directly.

### MXR-080-1352 — The PEFT adapter calls a conditional score a normalized sequence density

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `examples/peft_lora_grad_leaf.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 10–14 and 56–75
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The wrapper sums next-token log probabilities only from positions 2 through
the end. It assigns no probability to the first token (nor a start-token
model), so over sequences whose first token varies it represents
`p(x[1:] | x[0])`, not a normalized `p(x[0:])`. Calling it a log density lets
conditional scores enter density composition and model comparison under the
wrong normalization contract. Either condition the observation type
explicitly on the first token or include a valid initial-token distribution.

### MXR-080-1353 — GPU benchmark timings omit device synchronization

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `examples/engine_benchmark_example.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 37–62 and 89–118
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The timer brackets `fn()` with `perf_counter` but never synchronizes CUDA or
MPS before starting or stopping. Torch scoring can return while queued device
kernels are still running, so the GPU intervals and reported NumPy/GPU
speedups can measure dispatch rather than execution. The scoring case is
especially direct because its result is not consumed. Add device-specific
warm-up and synchronization around every measured region, consume results,
and couple timing to numerical parity.

### MXR-080-1354 — The “cross-modal fit receipt” contains no modality inputs or encoders

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `examples/cross_modal_fit_receipt.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–29 and 32–59
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The script labels two independent synthetic Gaussian tuples as image and
signal encoder latents, but it contains no image, signal, modality declaration,
encoder, paired representation objective, or cross-modal alignment. The same
calculation is an ordinary regression over two numeric vectors. It also
asserts edge recovery in prose without verifying the learned parent set or a
predictive threshold. Reclassify it as a synthetic vector-feature tutorial,
or supply real typed modality inputs/encoders and ablations that establish
cross-modal behavior.

### MXR-080-1355 — Release negative controls test toy copies rather than the real gates

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/tests/release_gate_negative_controls_test.py`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** negative controls 18–55 and 81–136;
  checklist 59–71
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The suite reimplements tiny helpers and tests them on literals; it does not
invoke the API-manifest generator, optional-import guard, package metadata
check, benchmark regression policy, or dependency scanner it claims to
control. The disconnect is observable: its undeclared-import helper catches a
planted `sklearn`, while shipped examples actually use undeclared
`scikit-learn` and still pass the release gates; its version helper is never
applied to the checkout. A negative control must plant a defect at the real
gate boundary and prove that production gate fails. The checklist should not
mark negative controls complete until that coupling exists.

### MXR-080-1356 — Optional dependency vulnerabilities are outside the security gate

- **Severity:** High

- **Lines at reviewed revision:** security workflow 22–58; project extras

The only vulnerability audit installs the base package and audits that
environment. Torch, JAX, Spark, Dask, Ray, MPI, data connectors, symbolic
engines, and scientist dependencies are never vulnerability-scanned even
though the release documents and examples advertise those surfaces and the
threat model says optional backends expand supply-chain risk. The extras

vulnerabilities. Audit each supported extra profile (or a mechanically
complete union) and retain separate, exact-artifact SBOMs.

### MXR-080-1357 — The checklist names a static security audit that does not exist

- **Severity:** Medium

  `.github/workflows/security.yml`

The release gate is titled “Dependency and static security audit,” but the
hosted workflow only runs `pip-audit` and SBOM generation. Those inspect
installed dependency advisories/inventory; they do not analyze Mixle source
for unsafe deserialization, command/path injection, weak trust boundaries, or
other code vulnerabilities. Either add an actual scoped static-analysis gate

review separately.

### MXR-080-1358 — The repository secret gate misses common credential forms and all history

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `mixle/tests/repo_hygiene_scan_test.py`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** hygiene scan 29–66 and 83–94; checklist
  127–135
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The scan covers only current tracked lines and five regex families: AWS access
key IDs, one OpenAI-style prefix, classic GitHub PATs, Slack tokens, and
private-key headers. It does not detect the same URL credentials, bearer
tokens, password assignments, or fine-grained provider tokens that Mixle's own
runtime secret detector considers sensitive, and it never scans reachable Git
history where a deleted credential remains public. “Secrets hygiene
complete” therefore exceeds the gate. Use a maintained secret scanner over
the full reachable history plus the release tree, with explicit reviewed
test-fixture allowlists.

### MXR-080-1359 — The publish path asserts reproducibility without testing it

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml`;
  `scripts/normalize_sdist.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** publish workflow 37–56; normalizer 1–14
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The workflow builds each artifact once, normalizes the sdist, and uploads it.
It never performs a second clean build or compares wheel/sdist digests, so a
new source of nondeterminism can silently invalidate the byte-for-byte claim.
Earlier local experiments in a decision log are not a regression gate for the
final builder and dependency set. Build twice in isolated directories under
the same pinned environment and fail before upload unless both artifact
digests match.

### MXR-080-1360 — Optional dependency floors are declared but never tested at those floors

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `pyproject.toml`; `constraints-min.txt`;
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml`; `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`;
  `docs/support-policy.rst`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** project extras 51–120; constraints 1–16;
  tests workflow 105–124; extras workflow 14–63; support policy 43–59
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- this finding names a class of modules rather than a file path, so it cannot be cross-referenced against the commit history mechanically; verify against current source

The minimum-version job constrains only NumPy, SciPy, and mpmath and installs
only `[test,highprec]`. The extras matrix installs each optional profile with
an unconstrained latest resolver. Declared floors for Numba, pandas, Arrow,
SQLAlchemy, MongoDB, array stores, Spark, Dask, Ray, Lightning, Torch,
Transformers, JAX, NumPyro, MPI, UMAP, symbolic engines, and native kernels
therefore have no floor evidence. This contradicts the policy that an optional
surface is claimed only when its dependency stack is installed and tested.
Generate constraints mechanically from every declared extra floor and run
feature-level smoke or contract tests against those exact versions.

### MXR-080-1361 — Dependency ranges permit unreviewed future drift contrary to release policy

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `pyproject.toml`; `docs/support-policy.rst`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** project dependencies 29–120; support policy
  61–80 and 159–166
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Every runtime and optional dependency range is lower-bound-only, including
fast-moving numerical, neural, distributed, storage, and documentation stacks.
The support policy permits that form only with a recorded reason that future
drift is safe or captured resolver evidence plus a tracked risk; the metadata
instead makes the blanket assertion that newer majors are allowed. A 0.8.0
install can therefore resolve to dependency generations that did not exist
when the release was tested, while the old-version policy calls resulting
breakage a reproducibility defect. Record the candidate's resolved graphs and
per-dependency drift decisions, and add compatible upper bounds wherever
future major behavior is not demonstrably safe.

### MXR-080-1362 — Release workflows execute third-party actions through mutable tags

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/security.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, and
  `.github/workflows/post-publish-verify.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** every `uses:` entry in the six workflows
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

All external actions are selected by mutable major or release tags such as
`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v6`, and
`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`. Moving or compromising one of those
tags changes code executed by otherwise unchanged commits; the publisher runs
with PyPI OIDC authority. Exact-source release evidence and reproducible
automation cannot be established from mutable action identities. Pin every
action to a reviewed full commit SHA, retain the human-readable version in a
comment, and update pins through reviewed dependency changes.

### MXR-080-1363 — A manual workflow input is interpolated directly into shell programs

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/post-publish-verify.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 8–13 and 30–40
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The free-form `inputs.version` value is inserted directly into two multiline
shell scripts, including inside double quotes. GitHub expressions are expanded
before the shell parses the resulting program, so quote and command syntax in
the dispatch value can alter the command rather than remain version data.
Although dispatch is permission-controlled, the verifier should not turn a
metadata field into arbitrary runner code. Validate the input as one exact
PEP 440 version, pass it through an environment variable, and quote only the
environment expansion.

### MXR-080-1364 — The public-API drift gate fails open for a dynamic public package

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `scripts/gen_api_manifest.py`;
  `mixle/tests/public_api_manifest_test.py`; `mixle/system/__init__.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** generator 129–153; drift test 49–76 and
  133–157; system package 38–70
- **State:** Source-confirmed and adverse-control reproduced
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`mixle.system` builds `__all__` dynamically, so the generator must import it.
Any import exception is converted to an `unresolved` entry, and
`_partition_drift()` drops every unresolved key from comparison. The separate
“dynamic packages resolve” assertion covers only `mixle`, `mixle.stats`, and
`mixle.utils`, omitting `mixle.system`. A direct adverse-control comparison
between the committed `mixle.system` names and an `unresolved: ImportError`
current entry returned no blocking drift. Derive the dynamic-package set
mechanically and require every one to resolve in the release environment;
missing optional dependencies need an explicit package-level policy, not a
catch-all skip.

### MXR-080-1365 — Serialization type removal is not gated in the environments that run the test

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/tests/schema_manifest_test.py`;
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** schema test 20–58; base/full jobs 57–154;
  optional job 184–235
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The always-run assertion checks only `live - recorded`, so a removed or renamed
registered type passes. The reverse comparison is conditional on Torch being
installed. Fast and full CI install only `[test,highprec]`, while the
Torch-bearing optional job selects only optional/Torch/Numba/JAX-marked tests;
`schema_manifest_test.py` is not in that selection. Thus no defined CI lane
guarantees execution of the stale-type check, even though removal is the
schema change that breaks existing artifacts. Run the exact comparison in a
declared full-schema environment, or make the registry discoverable without
importing optional implementations and require exact equality everywhere.

### MXR-080-1366 — The source distribution is published without an installation test

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml`;
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** publish workflow 29–56; clean-wheel job
  156–182; checklist 48–57
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The publisher builds and uploads both a wheel and sdist, but `twine check`
only validates metadata rendering. The clean-install job builds and installs
only the wheel. No job creates a fresh environment from the normalized
`.tar.gz`, builds it through its declared build-system requirements, imports
it, or exercises its package data. A broken or incomplete source distribution
can therefore be released alongside a good wheel while the artifact gates
remain green. Clean-install each exact artifact independently and run the same
base smoke and package-data assertions before upload.

### MXR-080-1367 — Behavioral tests exercise the editable checkout, not the release wheel

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml`;
  `docs/release-readiness.rst`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** test jobs 20–154; clean-wheel job 156–182;
  readiness policy 45–60; checklist 51–57
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Fast, minimum-version, macOS, and full lanes all install `-e .`; the built
wheel lane performs only import smoke. Consequently the broad behavioral
evidence can pass against files that are absent, stale, or differently
resolved in the wheel. The release policy asks for full candidate testing
against the clean wheel where practical, but no named behavioral subset runs
there. Build once, install the immutable wheel outside the checkout, then run
at least the stable-core, serialization, package-data, and representative-fit
tests with the repository tests supplied separately and source shadowing
explicitly excluded.

### MXR-080-1368 — The release artifact builder is not reproducibly specified

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `pyproject.toml`; `.github/workflows/publish.yml`;
  `scripts/normalize_sdist.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** build-system requirements 1–3; publish
  workflow 29–56; normalizer 21–43
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The build isolation allows any `setuptools>=77` and any `wheel`, while the
workflow upgrades pip and installs unconstrained `build` and `twine`; sdist
normalization additionally depends on the runner's system `gzip`. The exact
same tag rebuilt later can therefore execute a different toolchain and emit
different metadata or archives even with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` fixed. No lock,
builder image digest, tool-version receipt, or artifact-attestation step
captures this environment. Pin or content-address the release build toolchain,
record every builder version, and verify the resulting artifact digests
against the approved candidate before publication.

### MXR-080-1369 — The claimed support matrix receives only one full-test cell

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml`;
  `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`; `docs/support-policy.rst`;
  `release-checklists/README.md`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** tests workflow 57–154 and 184–235; extras
  workflow 14–63; support policy 18–59; checklist method 61–68; 0.8 checklist
  54–56
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The full non-optional suite runs only on Ubuntu/Python 3.12. Python 3.11 and
both advertised macOS cells receive only the fast subset. Optional extras are
resolved only on Ubuntu/Python 3.12, not on either macOS version or the oldest
Python. This does not satisfy the release method's “full suite across the
supported Python/OS matrix” or the support policy's requirement to test the
effective dependency graph behind a claim. Define the actual support tiers per
cell, run full stable-core coverage on each claimed Python/OS combination, and
exercise every claimed optional stack on each platform/version where support
is asserted; otherwise narrow the public matrix explicitly.

### MXR-080-1370 — Security-control changes bypass the security pull-request gate

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/security.yml`;
  `.github/pip-audit-ignore.txt`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** workflow trigger 8–17; waiver file 1–15
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The security workflow's `pull_request.paths` includes only
`pyproject.toml`. A pull request can change the audit workflow itself or add
waivers in `.github/pip-audit-ignore.txt` without running the security job.
That permits the control and its exceptions to be weakened without producing
the check intended to review them; a workflow edit could also remove the
post-merge release-branch trigger that would otherwise catch it. Include the
workflow, waiver file, constraints, manifests/locks, and dependency-bearing
build files in the trigger, and protect those paths with explicit review.

### MXR-080-1371 — Release-only workflows have no pre-merge validation gate

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/post-publish-verify.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`, and
  `.github/workflows/tests.yml`

- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Publish and post-publish verification have no pull-request event, while the
extras matrix is manual/scheduled. The ordinary lint job checks Python only;
it does not parse or semantically validate workflow YAML. A malformed action
input, expression, permission block, or release trigger can therefore merge
without any repository gate exercising or validating the affected workflow.
Add a pull-request workflow-lint gate and safe dry-run/contract tests for
release automation; keep actual publication authority isolated from that
validation path.

### MXR-080-1372 — Independent review protocols are not bound to one release candidate

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/0.8.0-tester-report-template.md`,
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-external-use-case-template.md`,
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-statistical-review.md`, and
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-systems-review.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** tester 17–39; use-case 10–50;
  statistical review 1–12; systems review 1–15
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

None of the four independent-evidence instruments requires the approved full
commit SHA and candidate artifact digest. The tester asks for a version string
and ambiguously says “published artifact” even though its two reports are a
pre-publication RC gate; the external use-case intake has no version,
revision, or artifact identity fields; the systems protocol says clean clone
without pinning a ref; and the statistical protocol records no reviewed
revision. Reports can therefore be completed against different moving trees
or rebuilt artifacts and still clear the named external gates. Issue one
content-addressed candidate, require its SHA-256 and source SHA in every
template, and reject reports whose identities do not match final sign-off.

### MXR-080-1373 — Vulnerability waivers do not enforce their required rationale or review date

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/security.yml`;
  `.github/pip-audit-ignore.txt`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** workflow 39–46; waiver file 1–15
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Policy says every ignored advisory must carry an identifier, rationale, and
review date. The workflow strips comments and passes only the first token of
every nonblank line to `--ignore-vuln`; it performs no schema, rationale,
owner, date, or expiry validation. A bare advisory ID therefore becomes an
indefinite blocking-gate bypass while fully satisfying automation. Store
waivers as validated structured records, reject missing/expired reviews, and
surface the accepted rationale and expiry in the retained security receipt.

### MXR-080-1374 — Versioned documentation can display the builder commit as the source revision

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `docs/conf.py`; `docs/poly.py`;
  `.github/workflows/docs.yml`;
  `mixle/tests/docs_version_aware_test.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** Sphinx commit selection 23–52 and context
  172–178; polyversion build 24–87; docs workflow 49–79; test 35–79
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The multi-version job builds many checked-out refs inside one GitHub Actions
run. Each ref's `conf.py` prefers the run-wide `GITHUB_SHA` over its checkout's
own Git commit, and the workflow never sets `MIXLE_DOCS_COMMIT` to the current
polyversion ref. Once a tag contains this configuration, a later rebuild from
`main` can label that historical page with the newer builder SHA. The test
only proves environment variables take precedence; it never exercises a
multi-ref build or checks that the displayed SHA equals the ref being built.
Pass the selected `GitRef` commit explicitly per child build and assert the
rendered tag page carries that immutable tag commit.

### MXR-080-1375 — The required coordinated family-release manifest has no local gate or identity

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `docs/family-release.rst`; `docs/support-policy.rst`;
  `release-checklists/README.md`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-risks.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** family policy 1–111; support policy 27–59
  and 144–153; checklist README 18–27; 0.8 checklist 103–149; risk R-12
  107–114
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Public policy says Mixle is a package family and that final readiness requires
a coordinated manifest plus co-install evidence for the published Python
siblings. The repository contains no such manifest, no immutable link or
digest naming an external one, and no 0.8.0 checklist row that can block on
it. The risk register instead calls version skew “out of this repo's scope.”
Thus package-local sign-off cannot tell whether `mixle-mlops`, `mixle-pde`,
`mixle-knowledge`, or other advertised companions resolve and run against the
candidate. Either explicitly declare core 0.8.0 a standalone release and mark
each sibling excluded, or bind the checklist to one versioned family manifest
and require its co-install receipts before the coordinated claim is made.

### MXR-080-1376 — The README falsely says every shipped example is download-free

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `README.md`; networked scripts under `examples/`;
  `docs/example-execution-manifest.rst`; `docs/security-and-data.rst`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** README 301–313; manifest 98–113 and
  400–420; security/data policy 60–72
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

The README links the `examples/` directory and says each script samples a
known model, refits it, and performs “no downloads.” Shipped examples fetch
Adult, Banking77, CIFAR-10, sunspots, CLIP, and language-model assets through
`load_dataset`, `urlopen`, and `from_pretrained`; the execution manifest
correctly acknowledges some of that network use. This can surprise users with
large transfers, remote code/data trust boundaries, cache writes, and license
conditions, contrary to the separate policy that examples be offline by
default and disclose external calls. Scope the README statement to the five
actually offline examples shown, and label every networked script, download,
cache destination, revision/digest, and offline failure mode.

### MXR-080-1377 — Public documents disagree on which projects form the package family

which compatibility and publication claims a coordinated release covers.

### MXR-080-1378 — The package-index README sends released users to mutable `main`

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `README.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 1–5, 301–305, 332–346

The README embedded in the wheel/sdist links examples, the test guide, license,
and logo assets from `main`. After 0.8.0 ships, those URLs can show later code,
commands, policy, or even content that does not match the installed artifact.
That defeats the version-aware documentation and exact-reproduction contract.
Use relative package-index-safe links where possible and version/tag-bound URLs
for release-specific examples and source; keep a separately labeled
development link to `main`.

### MXR-080-1379 — Manual dispatch can deploy documentation from any branch

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** triggers 27–34; build/deploy conditions
  49–91
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Both production Pages jobs run whenever the event is `workflow_dispatch`,
without checking the selected ref. A user allowed to dispatch the workflow can
choose an unmerged work branch and replace the public documentation with its
content under the `github-pages` environment. This bypasses the stated
main/release review boundary and can publish misleading or hostile rendered
pages. Restrict deployment to an approved branch or signed release ref,
separate build-only manual dispatch from production promotion, and require
environment approval tied to the immutable source SHA.

### MXR-080-1380 — Test and audit workflows inherit repository token permissions

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`, and
  `.github/workflows/security.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** workflow top levels and all checkout steps
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

These workflows declare no explicit token permissions, so their authority
depends on mutable repository-level defaults. They also use checkout's default
credential persistence before running repository-controlled tests, imports,
build hooks, and dependency installers. A compromised dependency or malicious
same-repository change can therefore receive more repository authority than
the read-only work requires. Set workflow defaults to `contents: read` (or
`permissions: {}` where checkout is unnecessary), grant exceptions only per
job, and disable persisted checkout credentials for non-publishing work.

### MXR-080-1381 — The required TestPyPI rehearsal has no executable path

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml`;
  `release-checklists/README.md`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** publish workflow 18–72; checklist policy
  55–79; 0.8 checklist 140–149
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The release policy requires a TestPyPI dry run before the real PyPI upload and
the 0.8.0 checklist marks TestPyPI as an unresolved external gate. The only
manual publication-workflow path builds and checks artifacts without uploading
them; the only upload job is hard-wired to the production `pypi` environment
and runs only for an already-published GitHub Release. There is no TestPyPI
environment, repository URL, trusted-publisher job, or install-back
verification that the owner can configure and execute. An `EXTERNAL` status
therefore describes missing implementation, not merely missing credentials.
Add a non-production rehearsal job that uploads the exact retained candidate
to TestPyPI, downloads it by immutable identity, verifies both artifact
digests, and runs the clean-install smoke before production publication can be
authorized.

### MXR-080-1382 — Documentation dependencies have two contradictory sources of truth

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `docs/requirements.txt`; `pyproject.toml`;
  `.github/workflows/docs.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** requirements 1–3; docs extra 98–101; docs
  workflow 63–75 and 109–114
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`docs/requirements.txt` requires Sphinx 8, MyST 4, and a dated Furo floor.
The advertised and CI-installed `mixle[docs]` extra instead permits Sphinx 7,
MyST 2, and any Furo release. The production multi-version driver then installs
unconstrained current `sphinx-polyversion` and Jinja separately. Nothing in the
repository references `docs/requirements.txt`, so a maintainer can reasonably
use a tracked requirements file that CI ignores and obtain a materially
different parser/theme stack. Choose one generated, versioned documentation
lock or constraints input and make local instructions, revision checks, and
multi-version deployment consume it.

### MXR-080-1383 — The authoritative checklist does not meet its own evidence standard

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/README.md`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-preflight.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** policy 30–53; checklist 24–150; preflight
  1–38
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The governing policy requires a completed gate to record the exact command,
candidate commit SHA, measured result, and date. The 0.8.0 checklist has 39
rows marked `COMPLETE`; none includes a date, only the ancestry row contains
any commit-like SHA, and most contain neither a command nor a measured result.
The linked preflight supplies a date and aggregate counts but identifies a
merge-base preparation commit rather than the source SHA that produced its
artifacts, while explicitly saying several receipts must be regenerated.
Consequently a later reviewer cannot determine which tree most completed
claims describe, reproduce the command, or tell which ones became stale after
another repair. Represent every gate as a structured receipt bound to one
candidate SHA and artifact digest, validate the required fields mechanically,
and reserve `COMPLETE`/`DONE` for receipts that satisfy that schema.

### MXR-080-1384 — The systems-review protocol credits backends its command never runs

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/0.8.0-systems-review.md`;
  `examples/scaling_example.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** review protocol 25–36; example 1–62
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The independent protocol says `python examples/scaling_example.py` fits the
model with local, multiprocessing, Dask, MPI, and Spark where launchers are
available. The script executes only local and multiprocessing fits. It contains
non-executable comments for MPI and Spark and no Dask path at all; it also
prints rounded parameters without asserting agreement. A reviewer following
the named command can therefore appear to exercise advertised distributed
routes while testing only one local process pool, and even disagreement does
not make the command fail. Provide separate executable, fail-closed commands
and tolerances for every backend allowed to satisfy the review, and require the
report to identify exactly which route actually ran.

### MXR-080-1385 — Publication can ship documents that still call 0.8.0 unreleased

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `CHANGELOG.md`; `docs/changelog.rst`;
  `docs/migrations/0.8.0.md`; `docs/charter.md`;

  18–72

- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The source candidate already declares package version `0.8.0`, but four public
documents still label it “Unreleased,” a development draft, or not a
published-release claim. That is appropriate during preparation; the defect is
that neither the checklist nor the publication workflow names or verifies a
final transition for those markers. A GitHub Release can therefore upload an
sdist whose included changelog still calls that exact version unreleased, and
the deployed manual can retain the same contradiction. Add an explicit
pre-publication metadata/document-state gate that rejects unreleased markers
for the version being published while preserving a new forward-looking
`Unreleased` section.

### MXR-080-1386 — The documentation artifact that is deployed is not the strict build

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/docs.yml`; `docs/poly.py`;
  `docs/release-readiness.rst`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** docs workflow 49–114; polyversion driver
  24–87; readiness documentation 67–104
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The release branch and pull requests run a single-revision Sphinx build with
`-W`, but the separate multi-version job that produces and deploys the public
Pages artifact invokes `sphinx-polyversion` without warnings-as-errors. The
workflow comments explicitly acknowledge that its production build has
historically allowed warnings through. The strict job neither builds the root
templates/version switcher nor verifies the bytes later uploaded by the Pages
job. Thus dependency drift, historical-ref failures, root-template defects, or
multi-version-only warnings can coexist with a green strict source check and a
successful deployment. Make the exact deployable multi-version build
fail-closed, validate its generated root/navigation artifacts, and promote that
already-checked immutable output rather than rebuilding a different artifact.

### MXR-080-1387 — The release build exposes checkout credentials to repository code

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** 18–56
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The release build job declares no least-privilege permissions and checkout
retains its authentication credential. It then executes the tagged repository's
build backend and `scripts/normalize_sdist.py`, plus unconstrained downloaded
build tools. Because publication is not restricted to an approved tag or
candidate by MXR-080-1292, code from any release target selected by an owner can
run with whatever repository authority the mutable default grants before the
artifact reaches the protected publishing job. Give the build job explicit
read-only or empty permissions, disable persisted credentials, and pass only
the content-addressed artifact—not a repository credential—across the
environment boundary.

### MXR-080-1388 — The statistical review protocol does not test statistical correctness

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/0.8.0-statistical-review.md`;
  `docs/stable-surface.rst`; `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** statistical protocol 1–98; stable-surface
  table 7–39; checklist scientific gates 74–81
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The five “adversarial statistical review” questions cover claim wording,
estimands, data leakage, calibration assumptions, approximation labels, and
scientific interpretation. None requires the reviewer to test normalization,
support, scalar/vectorized agreement, sampling/scoring consistency, estimator
recovery, effective weights, missing data, empty/degenerate samples,
non-finite inputs, posterior validity, or serialization equivalence across the
families called stable. Those are precisely the contract classes in which this
audit reproduced hundreds of high-severity defects. A reviewer can satisfy the
protocol without executing a single distribution-level adverse probe. Define a
stratified inventory of every stable family and require independent,
machine-readable adverse results for each applicable invariant before the
statistical review can close.

### MXR-080-1389 — The systems-review acceptance samples too little of the claimed system

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/0.8.0-systems-review.md`;
  `docs/release-readiness.rst`; `docs/support-policy.rst`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** systems protocol 1–75; readiness artifact
  and family gates 26–61 and 105–114; support matrix 27–59
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The systems gate passes after one backend and one benchmark reproduce from a
clean clone. It does not require both wheel and sdist installation, supported
Python/OS cells, declared extras, concurrent writers, interruption at each
checkpoint boundary, corrupted/truncated artifacts, rollback, resource
cleanup, network loss, process failure, or co-installation with the advertised
package family. Multiprocessing alone can satisfy the backend requirement even
though Spark, Dask, Ray, Lightning, MPI, torchrun, and accelerator paths have
different serialization and failure boundaries. Replace the “at least one”
acceptance with a risk-based matrix tied to every supported claim and require
fail-closed negative evidence for persistence, distribution, recovery, and
rollback.

### MXR-080-1390 — Two NO-GO tester reports can satisfy the tester gate

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `release-checklists/0.8.0-tester-report-template.md`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0.md`;
  `release-checklists/0.8.0-rc-stages.md`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** tester template 53–85; checklist 138–150;
  RC stages 65–89
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The tester template allows `GO`, `GO with caveats`, or `NO-GO`, but defines no
acceptance rule after the tester chooses one. The release checklist requires
only two reports, and the RC gate requires “independent review” without saying
that a NO-GO blocks progression or that its findings must be resolved and
retested. Two fully completed reports can therefore both reject the release
while mechanically satisfying the only stated deliverable. Define
machine-checkable dispositions: unresolved NO-GO and release-blocking caveats
must keep the gate open, repairs must be rerun by the same or another
independent tester against the identical candidate identity, and only explicit
accepted reports may feed final sign-off.

### MXR-080-1391 — Dataset-backed optional tests are skipped before their dependencies are installed

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml`;
  `.github/workflows/extras-matrix.yml`;
  `mixle/tests/scientist_test.py`;
  `mixle/tests/quotient_leaf_test.py`;
  `mixle/tests/conftest.py`
- **Lines at reviewed revision:** optional workflow 184–235; extras matrix
  15–63; scientist test 1–24; quotient test 1–43; marker registry 309–315
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The broad optional selection runs after installing Torch, UMAP, and JAX but
before installing `datasets`, `transformers`, or the `scientist` extra.
`scientist_test.py` therefore skips during collection, and
`quotient_leaf_test.py` either lacks `datasets` or converts an unavailable
CIFAR cache into a class-wide skip. The workflow installs `datasets` only
later and reruns two different flagship files, never either skipped module.
The extras matrix installs `mixle[scientist]` but performs only `import mixle`,
which does not import or execute the lazy scientist surface. Thus the assembled
scientist and real quotient-leaf receipts can remain entirely unexecuted while
both optional workflows are green. Install each profile before collecting its
tests, explicitly run the matching modules, and fail an evidence lane when a
required module or dataset was skipped.

### MXR-080-1392 — The habitat repair still coerces or bypasses invalid graph inputs

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/biodiversity.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `b458a453`:** 157–176, 199–248, and 437–479
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The new terminal validator converts every source and sink through `int()` before
checking it, so sources `[0.9]` and sinks `[2.9]` silently become nodes zero and
two and produce conductance `0.5`. `least_cost_corridor` does not call either
new validator: the same fractional endpoints are truncated and a resistance
vector `[-1, -1]` returns a negative path cost of `-1`, invalidating the
Dijkstra argument in its own docstring. `fragmentation_impact` also indexes the
first terminal before validation and casts arbitrary numeric masks—including
NaN or `0.2`—to Boolean disturbance cells. Require exact integer identities,
validate the resistance and terminal domains at every public entry point, and
require a genuinely Boolean/binary footprint rather than truth-value coercion.

### MXR-080-1393 — Habitat connectivity materializes quadratic dense graph matrices

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/biodiversity.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `b458a453`:** 251–357 and 367–414
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The corrected circuit-theory route first builds a dense `n × n` Laplacian and
the retained max-flow route builds a dense `(n+2) × (n+2)` capacity matrix,
although a rook raster has only `O(n)` edges. A modest 100×100 habitat raster
therefore needs about 800 MB for one float64 matrix before sliced copies and
the dense solve; a 1000×1000 raster would request roughly 8 TB. All new tests
use tiny line or square graphs, so the implementation can satisfy them while
being unusable on the nontrivial spatial domains the API models. Construct a
sparse Laplacian/capacity graph, solve only reachable free nodes with a sparse
solver, and gate realistic raster sizes and resource bounds.

### MXR-080-1394 — Finite positive resistances can overflow into invalid conductance

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/biodiversity.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `b458a453`:** 134–154, 251–282, and 334–414
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The validator accepts every finite positive resistance, but `_conductance_edges`
blindly computes its reciprocal. Two cells with resistance `1e-320` overflow
to infinite conductance. The supposedly corrected
`effective_conductance(...)` then returns `NaN`; the max-flow route returns
`inf` while emitting invalid-subtraction warnings. Validate representable
conductance or rescale the network before inversion/solving, reject non-finite
intermediate weights, and require a finite nonnegative result.

### MXR-080-1395 — Large valid abundance counts overflow into a negative sample size

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/coverage.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `b458a453`:** 31–57, 79–99, and 384–429
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_abund` first converts counts through float64 and then to signed int64 without

`[int64.max, 1]` wraps its total to `-9223372036854775808`.
`turing_coverage` reports that negative `n` with authoritative full coverage,
and rarefaction rejects size one as outside `[0, -9223372036854775808]`.

domain, and use a checked/Python-integer total before any floating conversion.

### MXR-080-1396 — Empty coverage samples yield contradictory authoritative estimates

### MXR-080-1398 — Coverage inputs silently lose their declared dimensional meaning

### MXR-080-1399 — The sparse-data shrinkage result violates the estimator protocol

- **Severity:** High

`ParameterEstimator.estimate` promises a

`mixle.inference.estimate` path repeats that return contract. The repaired
`LedoitWolfEstimator` instead returns `LedoitWolfInsufficientData` when the
sample is sparse. A one-observation call through the generic API therefore

object can also be inserted as an emission/component by callers that rely on

understood by the generic estimation and composite-model APIs, or raise a
specific estimation exception; do not make one estimator return a foreign
object under the common distribution return type.

### MXR-080-1400 — Shrinkage batch weights broadcast into false sufficient statistics

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/covariance_shrinkage.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `15b4a565`:** 204–228
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`seq_update` validates weight values but never requires a one-dimensional
weight vector whose length equals the number of observations. For a two-row,
two-dimensional batch and the one-element weight vector `[2]`, NumPy
broadcasts that value across both rows while `count` increases by only
`weights.sum() == 2`. The stored moments correspond to total weight four but
the stored count is two; estimation then reports mean `[2, 2]` for observations
`[0, 0]` and `[2, 2]` and returns a jittered `1e-10 I` covariance. Require an
exact `(n_rows,)` weight shape and a two-dimensional observation matrix before
performing any mutation.

### MXR-080-1401 — Two identical observations still become a fabricated Gaussian

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/covariance_shrinkage.py`;
  `mixle/stats/multivariate/multivariate_gaussian.py`

- **State:** Probed

The repair rejects one observation because its zero covariance contains no
variance information, but accepts two identical observations even though
their covariance is equally zero. `_shrink` returns the zero matrix with
shrinkage zero, after which the Gaussian constructor silently replaces it with
`1e-10 I`. The resulting object is presented as a well-posed
Ledoit–Wolf estimate even though every variance was introduced by numerical
healing and not by the data or the shrinkage target. Detect degenerate
dispersion explicitly and return the same governed insufficient/singular
outcome, or require a caller-specified regularization model whose contribution
is visible in the result.

### MXR-080-1402 — Reference-dose exposure validation is bypassed for posterior draws

### MXR-080-1403 — Reference-dose calculation trusts impossible public BMD states

`BMDResult` is public and mutable but validates none of its invariants.
`rfd_exceedance` checks only that `bmdl` is finite; it does not require

internally consistent state machine and make the downstream calculation

### MXR-080-1407 — Empty or uninformative cohorts become exact null epidemiology results

### MXR-080-1420 — Bounded KDE reflection does not preserve probability mass

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/kde.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `f728dc62`:** 224–313
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The finite-interval correction adds only one reflection across each boundary.
For a Gaussian kernel whose bandwidth is not tiny relative to the interval,
those reflected kernels themselves leak through the opposite boundary, and
the omitted repeated images leave the result unnormalized. A KDE fit to

only `0.1191984`, despite the class presenting it as a density on that support.

per-kernel truncation normalization) and test integrated mass across
bandwidth-to-domain ratios.

### MXR-080-1426 — Variance calibration still returns arbitrary search caps

- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/kriging.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `f728dc62`:** 423–474
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The target and input-domain repair does not check whether the requested
coverage is identifiable or reachable within the hard-coded scale interval.
All-zero residuals already have 100% empirical coverage at every positive
scale, yet the function returns the lower search cap `1e-6`; residuals of
`1e300` cannot be covered within the interval and return the upper cap `1e6`.
Neither boundary is an estimated calibration factor. Check endpoint coverage,
return a typed unidentifiable/out-of-range outcome, and derive or disclose
adaptive bounds rather than presenting exhausted constants as solutions.

### MXR-080-1428 — Smith process covariance can diverge from its cached inverse

Construction validates `sigma` but retains the caller's array by reference and

Scoring/dependence and simulation then describe different processes. Copy and
freeze the covariance and derive all cached state from that owned immutable

### MXR-080-1431 — Max-stable approximation diagnostics can certify NaN evidence

### MXR-080-1432 — Empty and Boolean rankings become authoritative consensus models

- **Severity:** High

- **State:** Probed

The repaired permutation validator considers the empty vector a valid
permutation and treats Boolean arrays as integer item IDs. All four aggregation
APIs accept `np.array([])`; Kemeny returns an empty exact consensus at distance

`[False, True]` is silently reinterpreted as `[0,1]`. Require at least one
ranking over a nonempty common item set and reject Boolean identifiers.

### MXR-080-1439 — The SDM honesty flag still uses half the actual prior curvature

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/sdm.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `f728dc62`:** 377–392 and 511–515
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Fixed -- an MXR-cited commit in this release effort resolves it

The Hessian repair correctly uses `2 * ridge * I` for the penalty
`ridge * beta @ beta`, but the later prior-dominance calculation still defines
`prior_curvature = ridge * p`. It therefore compares data curvature against
only half of the actual regularization curvature and can label a
prior-dominated fit as data-dominated. Compute the honesty diagnostic from the
same exact prior Hessian used for the Laplace covariance and test the
classification on both sides of the boundary.

### MXR-080-1440 — Finite habitat posterior inputs can produce infinite covariance

The overflow-safe exponential keeps each mean finite, but the covariance
multiplies those near-maximum means without a finite-result check. A valid
one-cell model with `beta=[700]`, `beta_cov=[[1]]`, and design `[[1]]`
returns finite mean `1.014e304` and covariance `[[inf]]`, violating the
posterior contract. Use stable scaling/log-domain propagation and fail
explicitly when the requested dense covariance is not representable.

### MXR-080-1441 — Habitat covariance materialization is quadratic in domain size

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/sdm.py`
- **Lines at repair revision `f728dc62`:** 240–244
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Although the shared posterior protocol explicitly permits a
`LinearOperator` at survey scale, `HabitatModel.cov` always materializes a
dense `K × K` matrix. A million-cell habitat grid would require about 8 TB for
one float64 covariance before intermediates, even though the coefficient-space
covariance has only `p × p` state and admits matrix-free products. Return a
linear operator or low-rank factor beyond a bounded small-domain threshold.

### MXR-080-1442 — Real-option maturity boundaries are false for expansion and abandonment

- **Severity:** High

- **Lines at live snapshot `2314d4aa`:** 232–246
- **State:** Probed

The terminal policy is hard-coded to boundary zero for every option kind.
That is only the defer threshold. With an expansion fraction of `0.5` and
cost of `40`, expansion becomes worthwhile at underlying value `80`, not
zero; with salvage value `50`, abandonment is optimal below `50`, not below
zero. The returned option values can be finite while the accompanying
exercise policy tells a controller to act at the wrong state. Derive the
terminal and earlier boundary from each kind's actual exercise comparison,
and distinguish “run the base project” from exercising the expansion.

### MXR-080-1446 — Gaussian EVSI accepts asymmetric covariance and uses two different matrices

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/real_options.py`
- **Lines at live snapshot `2314d4aa`:** 405–433 and 447–486
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The dense-matrix validator checks only finiteness. `_safe_cholesky` then
silently symmetrizes covariance matrices, while `solve` and the Kalman
covariance update use the original asymmetric matrices. An observation
covariance `[[2, 1], [0, 2]]` is accepted and produces a normal EVSI result,
but its simulated observations and conditional update therefore describe
different models. Require covariance symmetry and positive
semidefiniteness/definiteness at the boundary; numerical symmetrization may
only repair roundoff within an explicit tolerance and must be applied
consistently to every calculation.

### MXR-080-1449 — Passive Gaussian diagnostics perturb the estimate's random stream

- **Severity:** Medium
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/real_options.py`
- **Lines at live snapshot `2314d4aa`:** 372–402, 461, and 590
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The Gaussian-shape warning consumes 512 draws from the same caller-owned RNG
that subsequently drives the EVSI estimator. A warning-only diagnostic
therefore changes the estimate, and two posterior implementations with the
same Gaussian mean/covariance can produce different seeded EVSI results solely
because their diagnostic samplers consume randomness differently. Run the
screen from an independently derived generator or screen supplied evidence
without advancing the estimator's stream.

### MXR-080-1450 — Finite real-option inputs can return infinite or NaN prices

discount factor, step size, node values, continuations, and final result, or
use stable scaled/log-domain arithmetic.

### MXR-080-1455 — Cost-model arity detection misclassifies valid callables

- **Severity:** High

- **Lines at live snapshot `2314d4aa`:** 406–428 and 552–555

Arity is inferred from the total number of signature parameters rather than
which positional calls the signature can bind. A valid one-argument model
such as `cost(t, *, adjustment=0)` has two parameters, is called with two

against the supported call forms without invoking the function, and reject
ambiguous interfaces clearly.

### MXR-080-1459 — Propagation accepts asymmetric covariance and changes models by method

- **Severity:** Critical

The covariance repair checks the eigensystem of

accepted input describes different stochastic models depending on `method`.
Reject asymmetry outside an explicit roundoff tolerance and pass one validated
matrix consistently to every propagator.

### MXR-080-1461 — Unscented parameters can produce impossible negative covariance

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/doe/propagate.py`
- **Lines at clean DoE snapshot `48fca304`:** 244–318
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Only finiteness is checked for `beta`. For `f(x)=x²`, mean zero, variance one,
and `beta=-10`, the public transform returns output mean `1` and covariance
`-10`; `beta=-1000` returns covariance `-1000`. The wrapper subsequently
clips a negative diagonal to zero standard deviation, turning impossible
uncertainty into false certainty. Enforce a valid weight/parameter regime and
validate the resulting covariance as finite, symmetric, and PSD rather than
clipping it.

### MXR-080-1467 — Sensitivity silently abandons Sobol sampling on any internal exception

### MXR-080-1468 — Opposite-sign factorial aliases are labeled as sums

### MXR-080-1475 — Finite design bounds can generate infinite experiment points

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/doe/designs.py`; `mixle/doe/factorial.py`

The bounds gate checks finite endpoints but not representable span/midpoint
arithmetic. Bounds `[-1e308,1e308]` produce infinite random and fractional-
factorial points; finite positive endpoints near `1e308` make a one-level
factorial midpoint infinite. Maximin LHS can then end in an optimized-away
assertion because every comparison is NaN. Use overflow-safe affine mapping
or reject bounds whose required coded/unit transformation is not
representable, and validate every generated design before returning it.

### MXR-080-1491 — Repeated oracle timeouts can create unbounded live workers

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/doe/oracle.py`
- **Lines at clean DoE snapshot `48fca304`:** 227–315 and 398–442
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each timed-out call leaves an unkillable daemon thread when the callback
ignores cancellation, and optimization immediately proceeds to create the
next one. There is no outstanding-worker cap, circuit breaker, quarantine, or
resource status. A hanging oracle under a large call budget can exhaust
threads and retain candidates/closures indefinitely. Bound concurrency and
stop or isolate the oracle after repeated non-cooperative timeouts.

### MXR-080-1500 — Joint-posterior sampling silently replaces asymmetric covariance

`_safe_cholesky` unconditionally replaces `sigma` by

structure is not changed. Require symmetry within a quantified roundoff
tolerance; do not silently rewrite model evidence.

### MXR-080-1520 — Ask/tell point matching conflates distinct large-valued points

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/doe/optimizer.py`
- **Lines at clean DoE snapshot `d8d6b0ee`:** 126–135 and 292–315
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Pending identity uses default `np.allclose`, including relative tolerance
`1e-5`. Around `1e9`, points thousands of units apart can therefore match.
When two such points are pending, `tell` may delete the first proposal ID for
the second point and leave the actually reported proposal pending, corrupting
write-once accounting. Use explicit proposal tokens or a tight, scale-aware
serialization tolerance that cannot merge distinct valid designs.

### MXR-080-1521 — Amplification's baseline can repeat the search point exactly

- **Severity:** High

The search and random baseline both restart from the same integer seed. In

baseline's uniform point are exactly equal (seed seven produced
`0.07630829` for both). The claimed independent comparison can therefore
spend two oracle calls on the same candidate. Derive independent RNG streams
and record them in the report.

### MXR-080-1524 — Amplification treats abstentions as numeric statistical and training evidence

### MXR-080-1526 — Keyword arguments bypass compute-engine discovery

### MXR-080-1530 — Automatic precision sampling misses the last observation near its limit

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/engines/precision.py`
- **Lines at clean engine snapshot `e94d2ea6`:** 126–212
- **State:** Probed; residual of MXR-080-0145

The stride uses `int(i * n / sample_size)` for `i=0..sample_size-1`. For 513

tail-only value of `1e9` was missed and `auto_precision` recommended
`float32`. Include both endpoints with a deterministic no-duplicate sampling
scheme.

### MXR-080-1531 — The automatic-precision sample limit does not bound numeric work

- **Severity:** High

### MXR-080-1532 — Numeric-format bit controls silently truncate or accept Booleans

- **Severity:** High

- **Lines at clean engine snapshot `e94d2ea6`:** 82–119, 139–180, and 291–299
- **State:** Probed

`FloatFormat`, `FloatFormat.fp`, and `FixedPointFormat` convert counts with
`int` before validating them. `FloatFormat.fp(True)` constructs a nominal
one-bit format, negative mantissa counts fail later with `negative shift
count`, and `FixedPointFormat(-2, -3)` constructs and maps one to zero.
`_require_positive_int` also accepts `True`, while
`min_float_mantissa_bits(NaN)` raises an incidental conversion error. Enforce
finite, exact, non-Boolean domains before deriving any format state.

### MXR-080-1533 — Fixed-point encoding can erase invalid evidence and publishes a false bound

- **Severity:** Critical

`FixedPointFormat(4, 3).round_trip([NaN])` returned zero after only a NumPy
warning. The advertised `max_abs_error` also excludes saturation:

### MXR-080-1534 — Codebooks retain and mutate caller-owned state

### MXR-080-1535 — Codebook shape, index, and wide-payload contracts are not validated

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/engines/formats.py`
- **Lines at clean engine snapshot `e94d2ea6`:** 196–205 and 235–288
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

A 2-D codebook constructs then fails in `searchsorted`; a scalar codebook
constructs then raises `AxisError`. `dequantize([-1])` silently selects the
last code. For a 300-entry codebook, negative `count` returned an empty result,

with `sense=">="`. `hard_constraints` trusts the label and negates it again.
A requirement of 24 therefore becomes `offsets_created <= 24`, permitting
zero offsets and forbidding offsets above the minimum. The regression test
evaluates the raw coefficients with `<=` while separately asserting the
contradictory `">="` label, so it passes without exercising the actual
integration. Emit one self-consistent representation and test it through the
same assembler and solver path used in production.

### MXR-080-1571 — Biodiversity footprint masks convert malformed evidence into habitat loss

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/biodiversity.py`
- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 496–588
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_lost_equivalents` casts `plan_footprint` directly to Boolean. Numeric
fractions and NaN therefore become disturbed cells: `[0, NaN]` and
`[0.2, 0]` each create one full cell of habitat loss and a corresponding
liability/floor. This is the accounting counterpart of MXR-080-1392's graph
mask defect and remains reachable through both public offset functions.
Require a genuinely Boolean mask of the exact habitat shape before computing
legal or financial quantities.

### MXR-080-1572 — Finite biodiversity economics can overflow their hard requirement

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/biodiversity.py`
- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 496–588
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Every input is checked for finiteness, but neither multiplication nor the
reduction is. Finite suitability, area, ratio, and unit cost near `1e308` can
make `lost_equivalents`, `required_offset`, or the liability infinite. The
constraint function then publishes an infinite bound and the pricing function
publishes an infinite cost despite their claimed validated contracts. Check
representability at each product/reduction and reject any non-finite published
quantity.

### MXR-080-1573 — Liability callbacks can launder invalid plan evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/objective.py`
- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 101–169
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`priced_liabilities` validates emissions and the two callback outputs, but not
the `grade` or `exposure` values passed into those callbacks. A plan with NaN
grade or exposure and callbacks that return zeros produces a completely
finite, normal liability record; invalid source evidence has disappeared.
Moreover, three individually finite costs near `1e308` can overflow `total`
and `grand_total` without a final check. Validate every plan field before
calling opaque code and validate all elementwise and reduced outputs after
assembly.

### MXR-080-1574 — Radon risk accepts an unnamed matrix axis and ignores sampling controls

- **Severity:** High

`radon_wlm_risk` accepts a two-dimensional WLM array and returns a
two-dimensional `RiskQuantity`; its `mean` then flattens both axes while its
interval has no declared sample axis. This reintroduces the ambiguous
route/receptor/time structure rejected by the neighboring cancer-risk API.
The public `n` and `rng` controls are ignored entirely, so negative,
fractional, or Boolean draw counts are accepted without effect. Require one
WLM value per draw, or name and preserve every axis, and remove or implement

### MXR-080-1575 — One-site incidence data produce falsely exact richness

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/coverage.py`
- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 60–76, 230–272, and
  301–330
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The incidence validator permits a single sampling unit even though Chao2 and
ICE estimate unseen richness from replication across units. With two species
observed in the only site, Chao2 sets its finite-sample correction to zero and
returns richness exactly two with zero standard error and a point interval.
ICE similarly substitutes a factor of one. Replicated-incidence estimands are
not identifiable from one site; require enough independent units or return a
typed insufficient-evidence result.

### MXR-080-1576 — Zero-coverage ACE and ICE samples are reported as complete estimates

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/analysis/coverage.py`
- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 275–330
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

For an all-singleton abundance sample, `c_ace == 0`; for an incidence identity
matrix, `c_ice == 0`. The formulas' correction terms are undefined at that
boundary, but both functions return observed richness unchanged as an
ordinary estimate. The least-complete samples therefore receive no unseen
species correction at all. Represent zero estimated coverage as
unidentifiable/unbounded evidence rather than falling back to the observed
count.

### MXR-080-1578 — Shrinkage statistic serialization exposes and restores live arrays

### MXR-080-1579 — Impossible added-risk targets are silently replaced

### MXR-080-1581 — Emissions validators accept values the arithmetic cannot use

Activity and factor validators call `float(value)` only to inspect it, then

### MXR-080-1582 — Emissions footprint arithmetic can publish infinity

### MXR-080-1583 — Emissions provenance cannot identify or replay the emissions model

- **Severity:** High

- **Lines at clean analysis snapshot `a220a609`:** 79–115, 133–137, and
  196–268
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The footprint receipts hash only the activity dictionary. They record the
factor source as the constant string `"caller_supplied"` and omit the factor
values, uncertainty values, requested draw count, and RNG state. Two different
emissions models therefore produce different totals with the same content
hash and indistinguishable provenance; a Monte-Carlo interval cannot be
replayed. Hash/version the complete factor model and record the exact sampling
configuration/state alongside the activity digest.

### MXR-080-1584 — Negative water quantities pass the climate feasibility gate

`climate_terms` treats negative shortfall and negative demand as finite,

### MXR-080-1585 — Record statistics silently truncate at non-finite observations

### MXR-080-1586 — Bounded KDEs accept training observations outside their support

normally and returns a density, even though half its empirical mass is outside
