leak pools/sockets until garbage collection. Provide a cursor-backed bounded
iteration/encoding contract with `try/finally` cleanup, explicit ownership and
replay semantics, and projection validation.

### MXR-080-1667 — Disagreement gates accept partial labels and incompatible masks

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/task/disagreement.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 33–113
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Both disagreement measurement and fitting pair predictions with teacher
labels through unchecked `zip`. Three student predictions and one teacher
label produced an ordinary disagreement mass based solely on that first pair;
an empty label sequence produces a NaN mean, while gate fitting forwards a
short target vector against the full feature matrix. `UnionGate` likewise
does not require one boolean per input: combining masks of lengths one and
three failed inside NumPy reduction rather than at the gate boundary. These
paths can train or report an escalation policy from only a prefix of the
claimed evidence. Materialize once, require equal nonzero cardinalities,
validate every probability/mask shape and finiteness, and return an explicit
invalid-evidence state instead of a scalar metric or fitted gate.

### MXR-080-1668 — Callable introspection confuses unsupported metadata with an incompatible call

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/utils/callables.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 7–45
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`accepts_call()` places both `inspect.signature(fn)` and `signature.bind(...)`
inside one `try`, so a `TypeError` raised while obtaining unsupported
signature metadata is indistinguishable from a genuine bind mismatch. A
callable accepting arbitrary arguments and an `rng` keyword executed normally,
but a standards-compatible `TypeError` from its `__signature__` metadata made
`accepts_call(..., rng=...)` return false. Callers then silently choose reduced
fallback protocols and omit seeds or richer context the function accepts.
Retrieve the signature in a separate guarded step (treat both documented
unsupported-signature exceptions as unknown), then interpret only `bind()`'s
`TypeError` as a proven mismatch.

### MXR-080-1669 — Default text vectorization puts every item in a separately trained coordinate system

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/represent/modality.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 68–104
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

When no embedder is supplied, `vectorize()` fits a new autoencoder on four
copies of the single item being transformed. Consequently separate calls
return coordinates from different learned bases, even though the result is
presented as a common fixed-length vector for graph/correlation workflows. In
a deterministic probe, independently vectorized `"alpha alpha"` and
`"beta beta"` had cosine `+0.8105`; fitting those same items in one shared
corpus space gave cosine `-0.7696`. Neither sign nor magnitude is invariant
across the advertised routes. The docstring's suggestion to pass an embedder
does not make the unsafe default comparable. Require an explicitly fitted,
identified representation space (or a single immutable pretrained default),
attach its identity to every vector, and reject attempts to combine vectors
from different spaces.

### MXR-080-1670 — Missing and non-finite signals become ordinary modality evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/represent/modality.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 42–66 and 88–104
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

`signal_features([], dim=4)` returned the ordinary finite vector
`[0, 0, 0, 0]`, exactly the same representation as a real all-zero signal.
There is no missingness bit or insufficient-evidence state, so absent sensor
data can contribute the same graph/cross-modal evidence as a measured
zero-energy trace. Non-finite samples are also accepted: `[0, NaN]` returned
three NaN features plus padding. Validate positive exact dimensions/window
counts and finite nonempty signals, or return a typed missing-modality result
that downstream fusion must handle explicitly.

### MXR-080-1671 — Unknown sequence symbols are encoded as the first real symbol

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/represent/segment.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 34–53
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`ElementSegmenter` maps every symbol absent from its alphabet to ID zero, but
ID zero is already the first declared real category. With alphabet
`["A", "C"]`, both the valid sequence element `"A"` and unknown `"X"`
encoded as zero. Duplicate alphabet entries also overwrite their index while
remaining in `num_categories`. Out-of-vocabulary residues, characters, or
scientific categories therefore become positive evidence for a different
observed symbol. Require a unique alphabet and a dedicated reserved unknown
state, or reject unknown symbols under an explicit closed-world policy.

### MXR-080-1672 — Growing a heterogeneous encoder detaches its modality tags from the optimizer

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/represent/heterogeneous.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 45–98 and 140–148
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Registering a new modality after the tag embedding has been built replaces
that embedding module with a larger one. Any existing optimizer still owns
the old parameter object. In a probe, the grown tag weight had a nonzero
gradient but was absent from the optimizer's parameter groups and remained
bit-identical after `step()`. The newly registered encoder's own parameters
have the same lifecycle hazard. Dynamic registration thus appears to preserve
learned rows while silently freezing all new/replaced trainable state. Freeze
registration before optimizer construction or expose a transactional growth
operation that migrates optimizer parameter/state entries and returns an
explicit rebind receipt.

### MXR-080-1673 — Vector quantization silently changes its declared geometry and token IDs

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/represent/quantize.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 19–100
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The quantizer never verifies that training/serving vectors have width `dim`,
are finite and nonempty, or that iteration controls describe a completed fit.
`VectorQuantizer(2, 2)` fit a `(2, 3)` input and retained
`dim == 2` beside a `(2, 3)` codebook; a NaN input produced a NaN codebook and
NaN reconstruction error; `iters=0` published initialization centers as a
fitted codec. `dequantize()` casts IDs to `int64` before checking them, so
fractional IDs such as `0.9` and `1.9` silently become ordinary tokens.
Validate exact geometry, finiteness, cardinality, positive exact iterations,
and original token integrality before fitting or decoding; publish immutable
codebook identity and convergence evidence.

### MXR-080-1674 — Zero-demand blends are certified against an undefined grade

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/blending.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 30–163
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The linearized grade constraints multiply every grade deviation by source
tonnage and never require positive demand. For `demand=0`, all grade rows are
vacuously satisfied and `blend_to_spec()` returned cost zero and two zero
tonnages even when every source grade was `0.1`–`0.2` and the requested window
was `0.9`–`1.0`. Yet the documented blended grade is a ratio whose denominator
is zero and is therefore undefined. Shapes, finiteness, ordered windows,
availability and parcel domains are also not validated before solver
construction. Require a finite strictly positive demand and coherent physical
geometry/economics, then recompute and verify the returned blend's actual
tonnage and grade before certification.

### MXR-080-1675 — Causal identification accepts challenged assumptions and prediction-only evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/causal.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 73–211
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

`IdentificationResult(status="identified")` rejects only assumptions marked
`FAILED`; an assumption explicitly marked `CHALLENGED` is allowed. It also
places no restriction on `evidence_kind`. A probe constructed an ordinary
identified result with a challenged exchangeability assumption,
`evidence_kind="prediction"`, and the observational expression `E[Y|X]`.
That record passes a contract whose stated purpose is to prevent causal
overstatement. Define which unresolved assumption states block each
identification status, require evidence semantics compatible with the claimed
identification, and make any unsupported result partial/not-identified rather
than relying on a free-form expression.

### MXR-080-1676 — Causal semantic IDs collide when distinct mapping keys stringify alike

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/causal.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 32–53
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

The canonicalizer converts every mapping key with `str(key)` inside a dict
comprehension. Distinct keys can therefore overwrite before hashing:
`semantic_id({1: "first", "1": "last"})` equaled
`semantic_id({"1": "last"})`, and the canonical payload retained only the
latter value. This defeats a content identity used to bind causal records and
can erase evidence rather than merely serialize it differently. Restrict keys
to one validated canonical type or encode key type and value without
collision, reject non-finite/non-JSON values, and test canonical
injectivity over every admitted structure.

### MXR-080-1677 — A string-valued denied authorization grants access

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability_lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 125–247
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

`AuthorizationDecision.__post_init__()` never converts or rejects its
`outcome` field. Its decision logic compares enum members by identity and then
falls through to `GRANTED`. Constructing the public dataclass with
`outcome="denied"` stored the plain string, reported status `granted`, and
made `allows("run")` return true. The same inconsistency affects revocation
checks and serialization. Normalize every enum at construction before any
comparison, reject unknown types/values, and add denial/revocation tests
through direct construction as well as deserialization.

### MXR-080-1678 — Lifecycle snapshots bypass promotion rules and truncate revisions

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability_lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 292–443
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

The lifecycle constructor likewise retains plain strings instead of enum
members, and its invariant checks do not require a validated/supported
snapshot to have passed evaluation. A direct snapshot with
`maturity="supported"`, `operational="available"`, and
`evaluation="unevaluated"` constructed successfully, bypassing every
transition gate, then failed only when `as_dict()` expected `.value`.
`from_dict()` also applies `int()` before validation; revision `-0.5`
silently became zero. Durable records can therefore be forged or altered by
normal-looking input coercion. Canonicalize all state enums, enforce the
cross-dimensional snapshot invariants independently of transition history,
and validate an exact non-Boolean nonnegative revision before conversion.

### MXR-080-1679 — Demand forecasting advertises conformal coverage on non-exchangeable residuals

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/fulfillment.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 1–137
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`forecast_demand()` describes its returned band as retaining nominal
split-conformal coverage, but its calibration cases are successive horizons
from one held-out time-series tail. Those residuals are dependent, ordered,
and generally non-exchangeable; they are not interchangeable calibration
examples under the assumption the module itself states. The method then
refits a different HMM on the full series and transfers one constant
half-width to all future horizons, without proving residual invariance across
horizon or model refit. An ordinary time-series forecast is therefore
published with a finite-sample guarantee the construction does not establish.
Use a time-series-valid rolling/block conformal procedure with multiple
forecast origins and explicit dependence assumptions, retain horizon-specific
calibration evidence, and label the result empirical/inconclusive when those
preconditions cannot be tested.

### MXR-080-1680 — “Exact” CDF quantization discards and renormalizes both tails

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/ops.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 36–83
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

The CDF route computes masses only between the selected lower and upper
quantiles, then renormalizes that interior mass to one. It neither represents
the excluded tails nor states that the output is the conditional distribution
inside the bracket. Quantizing a uniform distribution with
`lo_q=.25, hi_q=.75, bits=2` returned four masses of `.25`; a clipped
quantization of the original distribution would allocate `.375` to each edge
bin and `.125` to each interior bin. The sampling fallback *does* clip tail
draws into edge bins, so the two advertised implementations target different
distributions. Define one target measure, account for lower/upper tail mass
consistently (or expose explicit conditional truncation), validate all
quantile/bit/sample controls, and receipt approximation error.

### MXR-080-1681 — Rolling precedence scheduling can lose the entire optimal project

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/precedence_scheduling.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 148–293
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Above 400 item-period binaries, `schedule_activities()` silently switches from
the declared maximum-NPV scheduling problem to a myopic rolling horizon. A
50-item, 10-period instance with unit capacity and a 10-item chain (nine
predecessors worth `-1`, terminal item worth `100`) returned no schedule and
NPV zero: the first eight-period window could not reach the terminal reward,
so it refused every prerequisite. Solving the same complete MILP selected the
chain in periods 0–9 with NPV 91. This is not merely approximate by a small
gap; the heuristic can erase every profitable long dependency while returning
an ordinary optimum-shaped result. Require an explicit approximate mode and
optimality bound/receipt, preserve cross-window lookahead (or solve the full
model), and never switch semantics solely from an internal size threshold.

### MXR-080-1682 — Capability dispatch certifies non-callable and evidence-free implementations

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 82–194 and 197–508
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Method-presence facets rely directly on runtime-checkable protocols, which do
not establish callable shape or semantics. An object with `condition = 3`
passed `supports(obj, Conditionable)` and therefore clears `require()` before
the operation fails. `FiniteSupport` separately accepts `True` as a support
size because booleans are integers, and `intersect_capabilities([])` returns
all three preserving facets, allowing a childless combinator to advertise
enumerability, finiteness, and rankability without a support. These are
authoritative routing declarations, not harmless introspection labels.
Require callable protocol members (and any minimum semantic receipt), validate
exact non-Boolean support counts, and make the empty intersection explicitly
unknown/neutral rather than maximally capable.

### MXR-080-1683 — The system registry truncates an external lock-file symlink

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/registry.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 190–325
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`Registry.register()` opens the fixed `.registry.lock` path with mode `"w"`
before applying `flock`, following any existing symlink and truncating its
target. In a temporary registry, a lock symlink to an external file containing
`"DO NOT TOUCH"` was followed during an otherwise successful registration;
the external file became empty. Entry-path containment does not protect this
control file. Create/open lock and index controls without following links
(`O_NOFOLLOW`/descriptor verification), require regular files owned inside
the registry root, and fail closed before any truncating operation.

### MXR-080-1684 — An index-write failure leaves an unrecoverable claimed artifact

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/registry.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 258–353
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The registry publishes the model artifact and retains its exclusive claim
marker before appending/writing the index. Only artifact-save failures remove
the claim. Forcing `_write_index()` to fail left both `e/` and `.e.claim` on
disk with no `index.json`; the registration raised, but retrying that ID is
rejected as already existing and normal reads cannot discover it. Artifact,
claim and index are therefore not one transaction. Stage the complete
generation and index mutation under one recoverable commit protocol, roll
back or journal every post-save failure, and reconcile abandoned generations
on startup.

### MXR-080-1685 — Invalid spend records create budget instead of consuming it

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/spend.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 15–55
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`Spend` has no construction invariants and addition propagates arbitrary
values. `Spend(frontier_calls=-5).total_units()` returned `-5`, while negative
oracle counts and NaN wall time serialized as ordinary receipt fields. Any
hard-ceiling comparison using `total_units()` can therefore gain budget from
work or fail open under non-finite state. Require exact non-Boolean
nonnegative call counts and finite nonnegative measured costs, checked again
after addition/deserialization, and make a receipt impossible to construct
when any ledger dimension is invalid.

### MXR-080-1686 — Meta-improvement runs invalid-cost mutations under a zero budget

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/meta.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 20–93
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Improvement costs, regrets and the overall budget are not validated. Under
`budget=0`, an option costing `-5` executed and reported `spent=-5`; a
NaN-cost option also executed and left `spent=NaN` because the over-budget
comparison was false. More generally, `opt.run()` mutates the live system
before regression is measured, and a detected regression merely stops future
work—it does not restore the rejected change. Require finite nonnegative
economics and unique option identities, reserve measured cost before action,
execute against a rollback-capable candidate snapshot, and commit only an
independently accepted improvement.

### MXR-080-1687 — Normal system ingestion escapes the configured knowledge scope

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 247–287
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The normal belief path calls `assimilate()` without its `scope` argument, so
that function uses `"local"` regardless of `SystemConfig.scope`. Configuring a
system for `"tenant-A"` and ingesting two claims returned two apparently
successful `BeliefItem`s whose scope, and stored substrate scope, were both
`"local"`. The import-fallback path does use `config.scope`, so deployment
behavior changes with optional-module availability. Pass the effective scope
through every ingestion route, make it explicit in the receipt, and assert
that a configured tenant cannot write outside its boundary.

### MXR-080-1688 — A partial system write is reported as no accumulation

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 247–274
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Claims are assimilated one at a time without a transaction. If a later
`put()` raises, `with_fallback()` converts the whole operation to
`status="degraded_no_accumulation", assimilated=False`, even though earlier
claims remain stored. A two-claim probe whose store failed only on its second
put returned that receipt while the first claim was still present. This can
cause an orchestrator to retry and duplicate evidence, or to reason from state
its receipt says does not exist. Validate the complete batch before mutation
and commit atomically, or return exact committed IDs plus a durable
partial-failure/recovery receipt.

### MXR-080-1689 — Invalid teacher outputs become durable answered capabilities

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 111–114 and 133–245
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The teacher boundary does not validate its promised string result. Teachers
returning `None` or a dictionary were charged as successful frontier calls,
reported with `status="answered"`, harvested, promoted by `improve()`, and
served forever from the captured cache. In the `None` case the public return
is indistinguishable from refusal/failure unless every caller also inspects
the receipt. Validate and normalize the provider response at the boundary,
reject empty/non-string/non-finite structured outputs according to the query
schema, and never harvest or certify a value that did not satisfy the answer
contract.

### MXR-080-1690 — The default system quality score accepts contradicted and empty answers

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/scorecard.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 17–19 and 37–80
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The default scorer asks only whether the lowercased expected string is a
substring of the reply. It scored `"Paris is not the answer"` as correct for
expected `"Paris"` and scores every non-`None` reply as correct when the
expected string is empty. The resulting scorecards reported quality and
calibration of `1.0`, so this false-positive metric can approve an explicitly
contradicted answer and guide meta-improvement toward it. Require a
task-specific, versioned scoring contract that validates reference data and
handles negation/semantic equivalence with an abstention or inconclusive
state; do not install substring matching as the authoritative default.

### MXR-080-1691 — “Calibration” is copied accuracy and is ignored by regression detection

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/scorecard.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 20–34, 37–80, and 91–106
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`evaluate()` receives no predictive probabilities or confidence observations
and assigns `calibration=quality`. This is not a calibration statistic: a
deterministic system with no confidence can receive perfect “calibration.”
Even if a caller constructs meaningful scorecards, `detect_regression()` does
not compare their calibration field; a drop from `1.0` to `0.0` returned
`regressed=False`. Remove the false metric until confidence/outcome pairs
support a proper calibration score with uncertainty, then make its validated
policy an explicit regression axis.

### MXR-080-1692 — Scorecard regression comparison fails open on invalid or unrelated evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/scorecard.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 20–34 and 91–106
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`SystemScorecard` and `tolerance` have no invariants, and the comparator does
not verify that both cards cover the same held-out set. A current card with
NaN quality or NaN cost, a NaN tolerance, and even a supposedly perfect
zero-case card compared against a 100-case baseline each returned
`regressed=False`. The documented “same held-out set” precondition is neither
identified nor enforced. Bind cards to an immutable dataset/scorer identity
and revision, validate exact nonnegative counts and finite in-range metrics,
validate a finite nonnegative tolerance, and return invalid/incomparable
rather than treating failed comparisons as acceptance.

### MXR-080-1693 — Fault routing classifies policy and programming failures as recoverable model errors

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/fault.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 39–48 and 60–81
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`with_fallback()` and `route_past()` catch every `Exception` without a
declared recoverability policy. A tier raising `PermissionError("denied")`
was bypassed and the next tier's value returned as a degraded `model_error`;
an internal `TypeError` was likewise turned into an ordinary fallback answer.
This lets authorization/policy failures, invariant violations, resource
failures and provider outages take the same route, masking defects and
potentially bypassing a fail-closed boundary. Require an explicit allowlist of
recoverable typed failures per route, propagate programmer/security/integrity
errors, and preserve structured causal evidence for every attempted tier.

### MXR-080-1694 — Degradation receipts can be constructed in contradictory states

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/fault.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 25–36
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The public frozen `DegradedResult` validates no invariant or mode vocabulary.
`DegradedResult("unsafe", False, "teacher_down", "failure")` constructed and
serialized a receipt that says a non-degraded value has a degradation mode
and failure reason; the inverse (`degraded=True` with no mode/reason) is also
accepted, as are arbitrary mode strings. Enforce the named-mode vocabulary
and the exact relationship among degraded state, mode and reason at
construction/deserialization, so downstream audit code cannot receive a
self-contradictory success record.

### MXR-080-1695 — A registry index can redirect artifact loading outside the registry

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/registry.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 108–143, 150–163, and 310–322
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Path containment and kind validation apply only while registering; index
deserialization trusts both fields. An index record with an external absolute
path and `kind="invented"` loaded successfully through the `TaskModel` branch,
because every kind other than the two special strings is treated as a task
artifact. An instrumented loader received the exact outside path. Treat the
index as untrusted persisted input: validate a closed kind enum, safe entry ID,
canonical contained path and artifact integrity on every read/load, and derive
the path from the registry root plus ID instead of trusting serialized paths.

### MXR-080-1696 — Registry queries expose mutable records that rewrite later routing and loads

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/registry.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 108–143 and 318–341
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`find_for()` returns the same mutable `RegistryEntry` objects stored inside
`Registry._entries`. Mutating a public lookup result's `path` immediately
redirected `_get()` to `"/tmp/redirected"`, and clearing its capabilities
removed it from subsequent matching without any registry mutation API,
validation, persistence or receipt. Nested `profile` data is mutable as well.
Make durable entries immutable, return defensive values, and route/load only
from freshly validated canonical registry state with an explicit update
transaction.

### MXR-080-1697 — Invalid fingerprints can win or abort nearest-model selection

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/system/registry.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 108–143, 188–303, and 324–341
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Registration and deserialization accept arbitrary fingerprint values and
dimensions. With a NaN-bearing entry listed before a valid exact match,
`find_for([0, 0])` selected the NaN entry as nearest; changing one stored
fingerprint to length three made the whole two-dimensional query raise a
broadcasting `ValueError`, hiding the healthy entry. Require one versioned,
finite dimensional fingerprint schema per search domain, reject incompatible
entries independently with evidence, and never let an undefined distance
participate in ordering.

### MXR-080-1698 — Fulfillment routing conflates forecast time steps with physical network nodes

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/fulfillment.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 125–147
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`forecast_demand()` returns one value per future time step, but
`route_distribution()` requires that vector to align one-to-one with
`supply_nodes` and uses its length as the dimension of a spatial min-cost-flow
graph. Thus a horizon of four becomes four plant/depot/customer nodes; there
is no location-by-time demand tensor, inventory state, temporal transport arc
or mapping from a forecasted series to customer nodes. The result may be a
valid flow for an invented graph while not representing the stated supply
dispatch problem. Separate temporal forecast coordinates from spatial
entities and compile an explicit, validated location × time network with
inventory, lead-time and conservation semantics.

### MXR-080-1699 — Supply dispatch ignores every measure of forecast uncertainty

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/fulfillment.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 67–122 and 125–147
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Although the upstream function emphasizes a calibrated predictive band and
retains state probabilities/samples, dispatch reads only `Forecast.mean`.
Two forecasts with the same mean `[0, 10]` but upper bounds `[0, 10]` and
`[1000, 1000]` produced the identical cost-10 flow. The second can represent
catastrophic unmet-demand risk, yet no service level, chance constraint,
shortage penalty, scenario or risk receipt reaches the optimizer. Require an
explicit risk policy and propagate calibrated scenarios/bounds into a
stochastic or robust fulfillment problem; an expected-value dispatch must be
labeled as such and must not imply that the forecast coverage was used.

### MXR-080-1700 — A positive demand-spike intervention reduces demand

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pipeline_twin.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 168–195 and 215–227
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The network convention is positive supply and negative demand, but the
`demand_delta` intervention adds a caller's positive delta to the signed
supply vector. On a two-node network with demand `-10`, a documented positive
spike of `5` changed it to `-5`; delivered throughput fell from 10 to 5 and
the run reported no queue. Demand changes need an unambiguous physical
quantity/sign schema, validation that targets are demand nodes, and
post-intervention receipts showing the effective demand rather than silently
applying the opposite scenario.

### MXR-080-1701 — The digital twin reports lost sales as a queue but never serves the backlog

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pipeline_twin.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 197–272
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each period solves against the same nominal demand, adds that period's
shortfall to `queue_total`, and reports the cumulative value, but never adds
the existing queue to a later period's demand or state. A capacity-five
network facing demand ten returned queue `[5, 10]` and throughput `[5, 5]`;
the second solve still requested only ten rather than the outstanding fifteen.
This is cumulative unmet/lost demand, not a queue, and it cannot model backlog
clearance. Either rename and receipt it as lost sales or carry an explicit
per-node backlog state into conservation for the next period, with aging,
service and terminal treatment defined.

### MXR-080-1702 — Simulation controls are silently rewritten into different experiments

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/pipeline_twin.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 46–69, 124–146, and 197–236
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`run()` validates `int(n_periods)` and then uses that coerced value, so
`run(1.9)` silently simulated one period and Boolean counts are admitted.
Negative arrival noise is treated as the `<= 0` deterministic branch:
`arrival_noise=-5` produced ordinary zero-noise runs rather than an invalid
scale error. The constructor also validates no matrix geometry, node
partition or finiteness before simulation. Require exact non-Boolean positive
period counts, finite nonnegative stochastic scales, square aligned network
state, valid unique node IDs and disjoint declared roles before creating a
simulator.

### MXR-080-1703 — The Scientist's image and text outputs are not a shared cross-modal latent space

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/scientist.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 30–32, 35–80, and 563–572
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`perceive()` returns 512-dimensional CLIP image features, while `read()`
returns 384-dimensional embeddings from an independently trained MiniLM.
There is no projection, paired alignment objective, common schema, modality
tag or bridge between them, despite both methods saying they encode into “the
shared scientific latent space” and `StudiedModel` calling itself
cross-modal. Their arrays cannot even be concatenated along the sample axis
without a shape error. Define a versioned multimodal representation contract
and train/validate an actual shared alignment or keep the spaces explicitly
separate with a learned, evidenced bridge.

### MXR-080-1704 — Learning one document string ingests one knowledge item per character

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/scientist.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 398–411
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`Scientist.learn()` iterates its unconstrained `docs` argument directly.
Passing the ordinary single-document value `"hello world"` reported 11
ingested documents and stored `["h", "e", ..., "d"]` as separate knowledge
items. This destroys document structure and makes later retrieval/provenance
depend on accidental character fragments. Distinguish one text document from
a collection in the public type/schema, materialize a collection once, and
receipt per-document identity and rejection rather than accepting every
iterable as a corpus.

### MXR-080-1705 — A valid empty research proposal crashes conjecture rendering

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/scientist.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 341–378
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`ResearchProposal.best()` explicitly permits no options and returns `None`,
but `Conjecture.render()` unconditionally indexes `proposal.best()["how"]`
whenever a proposal object exists. A conjecture carrying a valid empty
proposal raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Define an
empty-plan rendering/abstention state and validate proposal option schemas so
the human-facing uncertainty record cannot fail precisely when no acquisition
route is available.

### MXR-080-1706 — Distillation retention compares teacher and student under different label semantics

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/scientist.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 236–335
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Teacher accuracy uses NumPy's raw label equality, while student accuracy and
agreement coerce both sides to strings. With teacher and student label `1`
against reference label `"1"`, the returned artifact reported teacher
accuracy `0.0`, student accuracy `1.0`, agreement `1.0`, and retention `0.0`.
String coercion can also collapse genuinely distinct labels. Define one
versioned label vocabulary/equivalence relation and validate every teacher,
student and truth value against it before computing all metrics; make
retention undefined rather than zero when its denominator is not valid.

### MXR-080-1707 — Semantic records accept unsupported schema versions as current contracts

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 48–50 and 137–548
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Every semantic dataclass carries `schema_version`, but no constructor checks it
against `SEMANTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`. `ConstraintSpec(schema_version=
"future/999")` constructed normally, and the same omission spans values,
priors, observations, posterior/predictive/calibration/decision artifacts,
capability extensions and trace events. Unknown records can therefore be
interpreted under the 1.0 rules and receive authoritative identities. Validate
the exact supported version before any field interpretation, dispatch known
migrations explicitly, and preserve unsupported records as unreadable rather
than silently accepting them.

### MXR-080-1708 — Frozen semantic identities change through caller-owned mappings

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 53–89, 243–265, and 398–446
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Frozen dataclasses retain mutable mappings such as prior parameters, summaries
and diagnostics by reference. After constructing a `PriorSpec` from
`{"mu": 0}`, changing the original mapping to `{"mu": 9}` changed the same
object's `identity` from
`29c20eb51d65e725cf7c1a8fb85f5c375ec44e1c071979f344b6f1e622c0f133`
to
`f5ba78ddcff91c04988ee352ff19c3e76a770c3d8b2e071549e959daf1c2bb3d`.
Deep-normalize/copy into immutable canonical values during construction and
make the content digest fixed and self-verifying; a durable semantic record
must not change identity without a new revision.

### MXR-080-1709 — Numeric semantic constraints accept NaN and empty vector values

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 137–169
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`ConstraintSpec(lower=0, upper=1).accepts(float("nan"))` returned `True`
because both ordered comparisons against NaN are false. Passing an empty list
also returned `True` because the validation loop executes zero times. Boolean
and type-incompatible values are not given an explicit scalar-domain policy.
Validate finite values and expected scalar/vector shape before comparisons,
reject vacuous containers unless the schema explicitly permits them, and
return a typed validation result rather than allowing IEEE comparison
behavior to certify admissibility.

### MXR-080-1710 — One posterior can assert two contradictory likelihood models for the same data

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 324–370 and 398–446
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each `ObservationSpec` embeds a likelihood, while `PosteriorArtifact` embeds a
second top-level likelihood. The posterior checks only that the top-level
observation-ID set closes; it never requires the two models to agree. A valid
artifact was constructed whose observation declared Poisson likelihood and
whose posterior declared Normal likelihood for that exact observation. Use
one canonical likelihood identity/reference, verify family, parameters and
discrepancy closure for every observation, and reject contradictory evidence
models before issuing a posterior identity.

### MXR-080-1711 — Derived semantic values may depend on themselves or undeclared values

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 268–321 and 398–446
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Dependencies are checked only for non-emptiness. A derived value `d` with
expression `"d+1"` and dependencies `("d",)` constructed successfully;
duplicate, invalid and unknown dependency IDs likewise have no closure or DAG
check in a posterior. Such a record can be assigned a stable identity even
though it has no well-founded evaluation order. Validate portable unique IDs,
close every reference over the artifact's values, parse/bind the expression
to exactly those references, and reject self-dependencies and cycles.

### MXR-080-1712 — Unit declarations are decorative and permit dimensionally contradictory evidence

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 243–370 and 398–446
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

A free value declared in metres accepted a prior declared in kilograms, and
an observation for a metre-valued quantity accepted unit seconds; both then
entered a valid posterior. Units are only checked for truthiness and are never
parsed, canonicalized or reconciled across the value/prior/observation/
likelihood chain. Use a versioned dimensional-unit system with explicit
conversion, require compatible prior and observation measures, and bind
measurement uncertainty and likelihood parameters to the same dimensional
contract.

### MXR-080-1713 — Declared value shape and dtype are not enforced against the value

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/semantics.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 268–321
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`ValueSpec(shape=(2,), dtype="float64", role="fixed", value=1)` constructed
successfully: a scalar is certified as a two-vector, and `dtype` is an
arbitrary unchecked string. Boolean shape dimensions also pass the integer
test because `bool` subclasses `int`. Canonically coerce and validate the
actual value against an exact supported dtype and non-Boolean shape, apply
constraints elementwise under that schema, and make missing/derived values
carry a separately verifiable shape contract.

### MXR-080-1714 — Invalid calibration fractions silently disable or destroy the requested holdout

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 76–137
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`Model.fit()` coerces `calibrate` but validates no finite fraction domain.
`calibrate=NaN` and negative fractions fail the `> 0` branch and silently fit
all rows with `calibration=None`; values at or above one can reserve all rows
and fit an empty training set. An instrumented eight-row NaN request used all
eight rows, returned normally, and recorded no warning. Require either
`False` or a finite fraction strictly between zero and one, prove both
partitions meet method-specific sample requirements, and receipt the exact
immutable row identities.

### MXR-080-1715 — Certification and calibration failures disappear from the lifecycle record

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 124–136
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Both evidence-producing steps catch every exception and replace the result
with `None`, without status, reason or note. An injected internal certification
failure returned a fitted model with `certificate=None`, `calibration=None`
and empty notes, indistinguishable from a caller who never requested or
supported those checks. Preserve a typed attempted/succeeded/failed/not-
applicable record with the failure class and inputs; a fit may remain usable,
but it must not erase why its promised evidence is absent.

### MXR-080-1716 — An internal JSON serializer defect silently creates an executable pickle artifact

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 254–290
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`_write_model()` catches every exception across registry initialization,
conversion and JSON encoding and interprets it as “model requires pickle.”
Forcing `to_serializable()` to raise an internal `TypeError` produced
`format="pickle"` and `model.pkl` for an otherwise JSON-serializable Gaussian.
This changes the artifact's security and portability contract because of a
programming failure. Fall back only on a narrow, explicit unsupported-type
result after successful registry operation; propagate internal/integrity
errors and require the caller to opt into code-executing serialization.

### MXR-080-1717 — A lifecycle artifact drops its certificate, calibration, frontier and fit record

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 254–336
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Deployment writes only the fitted model plus a manifest containing family,
time, fit, notes and format. Loading restores only the fitted model and notes.
A normal round trip changed a model carrying a certificate, calibration
report, candidate frontier and `{"n": 7}` fit record into one with
`None`, `None`, `None` and `{}` respectively. The artifact therefore preserves
prediction code while discarding the evidence needed to judge it. Serialize
and integrity-bind every lifecycle receipt with explicit schema/migrations,
or state that this is only a bare model export and refuse evidence-bearing
deployment through it.

### MXR-080-1718 — The model-search timeout is not an execution deadline

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 375–494
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`propose(timeout=...)` checks elapsed time only before starting a candidate;
the candidate receives no deadline and may run indefinitely. An instrumented
candidate sleeping 80 ms completed and was scored under a 10 ms timeout; the
call returned after about 90 ms and only skipped the next candidate. NaN
timeouts also pass validation and disable every comparison. Validate a finite
nonnegative duration and enforce a cancellable per-candidate/global deadline,
with late work quarantined and exact timeout evidence retained.

### MXR-080-1719 — Lifecycle deployment is neither transactional nor integrity-verifiable

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 254–336
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Deployment writes the model directly into the final directory and writes the
manifest afterward, with no staging generation, atomic promotion, file
digest, directory fsync, exclusive identity or cleanup of a prior generation.
A crash can expose a model without a manifest; redeployment can mix stale
pickle/JSON files, and later byte changes are undetectable. Loading trusts the
manifest's format and bytes without binding either to the claimed family or
creation record. Stage a complete content-addressed generation, hash and
validate every file, atomically promote it, and reject incomplete, mixed or
tampered artifacts.

### MXR-080-1720 — The advertised two-stage stochastic program has no recourse decisions

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stochastic_opt.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 1–37 and 119–168
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The model contains one shared first-stage binary vector `x` and auxiliary
variables used only to linearize CVaR. Its scenario “recourse value” is merely
the realized payoff of that same `x`; there is no scenario-indexed operational
decision, recourse constraint/cost, information stage or nonanticipativity
link. This is a one-stage sample-average risk-adjusted selection model, not a
two-stage stochastic program. Name and receipt the implemented problem
honestly, or add explicit first-stage commitments and scenario-contingent
second-stage actions with a declared information structure.

### MXR-080-1721 — CVaR planning accepts undefined scenario and economic inputs

- **Severity:** Critical

`cvar_epigraph()` validates rank and alpha but not finite loss coefficients;
`[[NaN]]` produced an ordinary constraint row containing NaN. Planning also
does not require an exact positive non-Boolean scenario count or finite
price, cost, samples, liabilities, cap coefficients and bounds. Cost is
flattened by `.size`, so an accidental matrix can silently become a different
item vector. Validate the full finite aligned scenario/economic schema before
constructing the MILP and report posterior/sample identity, weights and
effective risk controls.

### MXR-080-1722 — Hard exclusions truth-coerce arbitrary data into forbidden items

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stochastic_opt.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 231–261
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The no-mine mask is converted with `dtype=bool`, so strings and non-finite
numbers become policy decisions. A mask containing the string `"False"`
tightened the item's bounds to `(0, 0)`—the opposite of its apparent value.
Cap dictionaries and top-level constraint keys have no closed schema, so
unknown keys can be ignored while malformed values enter solver rows. Require
literal Boolean mask values under a versioned policy artifact, reject unknown
or duplicate controls, validate finite cap geometry, and bind each enforced
row to its authority/provenance.

### MXR-080-1723 — Rounded stochastic decisions retain the CVaR of a different solution

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/stochastic_opt.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 153–168 and 263–276
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The returned extraction is made by rounding solver variables, but CVaR is
copied from the solver's `eta/u` variables without recomputing it for that
rounded selection or verifying feasibility/integrality. An instrumented
solver result with `x=.49` returned `extract=False`, expected value zero, and
CVaR `-.49`; the loss of the returned empty selection has CVaR zero. Recompute
all objective/risk/constraint values from the exact discrete artifact,
validate them against the solver result and tolerances, and reject rather than
certify any inconsistent solution.

### MXR-080-1724 — Capability “integrity digests” accept arbitrary text

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability_lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 125–154
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

`CapabilityIdentity.digest` is described as the integrity digest of a concrete
artifact, but validation checks only that it is nonempty.
`digest="not-a-digest"` constructed and round-tripped normally; version text
is likewise unconstrained. This lets authorization bind to a label that
cannot verify any bytes. Require an algorithm-labelled, fixed-format
cryptographic digest (and a canonical version/identity schema), recompute it
at the artifact boundary, and reject missing integrity for concrete
capabilities.

### MXR-080-1725 — Plain self-asserted JSON becomes an executable authorization grant

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability_lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 157–261 and 343–459
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

An authorization records only an `issued_by` string; it carries no signature,
trust-domain identity, verification result or protected store revision.
Loading a hand-built dictionary with `issued_by="root"`,
`outcome="granted"` and scope `"run"` made `allows("run")` return `True`, and
embedding it in a lifecycle did the same. Anyone able to supply persisted
record content can therefore mint the authority that the object itself
enforces. Bind decisions to authenticated principals and capability digests
with verifiable signatures/MACs and replay protection; `from_dict()` must
produce unverified data until a configured trust policy validates it.

### MXR-080-1726 — Lifecycle snapshots cannot be safely versioned or replay-audited

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/capability_lifecycle.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 125–261 and 343–459
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

Despite claiming JSON-compatible cross-project replay, neither identity,
authorization nor lifecycle records carry a schema version. `evolve()` records
only the resulting dimensions, revision and time—no actor, reason, command,
parent identity, evidence/evaluation reference or transition digest. Different
schema interpretations or forged intermediate histories can yield the same
snapshot with no detectable provenance. Define a versioned append-only
transition event with parent hash, authenticated actor, cause/evidence refs
and canonical state digest, then derive snapshots by validated replay rather
than treating an unauthenticated snapshot as its own audit history.

### MXR-080-1727 — Finite empirical fitting is advertised as an exact KL projection

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/ops.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 126–146
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

`project()` draws a finite Monte Carlo sample and returns one fitted target,
but its documentation says this “is exactly” the forward-KL projection. It has
no sampling-error estimate, optimization/convergence certificate, held-out
check, target-family validation or record of the realized sample count.
`n_samples` is truncated through `int()` and nonpositive/fractional controls
are not rejected. Label the result as an empirical approximate projection,
validate exact budgets and sampler output, and attach Monte Carlo,
optimization and model-misspecification evidence before making a KL claim.

### MXR-080-1728 — A zero-weight product expert still deletes support

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/ops.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 149–223
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

Categorical pooling intersects the positive supports of every expert before
using its weight. An expert with support only `{"a"}` at weight zero and a
second expert with `{"a": .5, "b": .5}` at weight one returned
`{"a": 1.0}`; mathematically the zero exponent contributes the constant one,
so the pool should equal the second expert and retain `"b"`. Define and
validate finite weight semantics, exclude zero-weight experts before support
construction, and handle negative weights/zero probabilities under an
explicit properness contract shared with the Gaussian route.

### MXR-080-1729 — Constructing an empty mixture fails with an incidental division by zero

- **Severity:** High

The public `mixture()` helper computes `1 / len(dists)` before validating that
an expert exists. `mixture([])` raised `ZeroDivisionError` rather than a
capability/schema error, and weight length/type validation is deferred to a
lower layer. Materialize once, require a nonempty aligned expert/weight
collection, validate common event semantics, and raise the façade's declared
contract error at its own boundary.

### MXR-080-1730 — “Predecessors first” may be scheduled simultaneously with their dependents

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/precedence_scheduling.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 99–116 and 186–255
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The cumulative constraint is non-strict at each period boundary, so a
dependent and its predecessor can both enter the same period. With one period,
capacity two, values `[1, 10]` and precedence `(1, 0)`, both were scheduled at
period zero even though the public contract says the predecessor is required
“first”/“before.” A two-node cycle was also accepted and co-scheduled. Define
whether precedence means prior completion or merely same-boundary closure; for
the stated former contract, shift the predecessor cumulative term by one
period and validate/reject cycles in the required DAG.

### MXR-080-1731 — Scheduling accepts invalid calendar, capacity and discount domains

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/precedence_scheduling.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 119–177 and 186–255
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

There is no exact positive period-count, finite value/discount, or
nonnegative integral capacity validation. Capacity `-1` reached the solver and
then raised a message claiming the empty schedule is always feasible;
capacity `.5` silently became effective zero for binary unit jobs. Discount
`-1` produced division by zero for later periods, NaN failed only in the
backend, and positive infinity silently zeroed future value. Validate a
versioned calendar/resource model and finite discount domain before building
variables, with heterogeneous resource consumption represented explicitly
rather than through undocumented coercion.

### MXR-080-1732 — Finite precedence values can overflow big-M and violate closure

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/precedence_scheduling.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 53–96
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Big-M is computed by summing absolute float64 values without an overflow
check. For predecessor value `-1e308`, dependent value `1.5e308`, and
precedence `(1, 0)`, the sum became infinity; residual-flow reconstruction
produced NaN and the returned mask selected only the dependent
`[False, True]`, directly violating closure. Use a scale-safe exact reduction
or validated finite bound that cannot overflow, and post-verify every returned
mask against all precedence edges and its recomputed objective.

### MXR-080-1733 — “Append-only” telemetry history is mutable and silently rewritten

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/telemetry/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 35–52 and 73–147
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

`record()` returns the live mutable `Event`, `events()` returns those same
objects, and flushing rewrites the complete file from their current fields.
Changing a recorded event's kind to `"invented"` and timestamp to NaN rewrote
the prior log as that invalid event; the next reader could not load it.
Features/outcomes/tags are only shallow-copied, so nested caller mutations have
the same effect. This is not append-only audit telemetry. Store immutable
canonical events, append integrity-linked revisions/outcomes rather than
mutating history, and return defensive views.

### MXR-080-1734 — Independent telemetry writers erase each other’s events

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/telemetry/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 55–71 and 128–163
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Each recorder loads one snapshot and later replaces the entire log without a
cross-process lock, generation check or merge. Two instances opened on an
empty path; after the first recorded event A and the second recorded event B,
the file contained only B. A successful flush therefore destroys valid
history written by another process. Use a real append/journal protocol or a
locked compare-and-swap generation with conflict detection, and receipt
durable sequence identities.

### MXR-080-1735 — Telemetry’s fixed temporary path follows and installs external symlinks

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/telemetry/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 133–147
- **State:** Probed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Flush always opens `<log>.tmp` with mode `"w"`. Preplacing that path as a
symlink to an external file caused the external file to be overwritten with
the telemetry row; replacement then moved the symlink itself onto the final
log path, permanently redirecting later writes outside the requested
location. Create a unique temporary regular file through a trusted directory
descriptor with no-follow/exclusive semantics, fsync it and its directory,
and verify the destination before atomic promotion.

### MXR-080-1736 — The dashboard adds incompatible units and accepts invalid costs

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/telemetry/dashboard.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 14–46
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Open -- no commit in this release effort has ever touched this finding's surface file

For each event the fold takes the first present field among `cost`, `latency`
and `spent`, then sums all such values into one `cost_total`. A dollar cost of
1 and latency of 2 become the number 3; if both cost and latency are present,
latency is silently discarded. Boolean, negative, infinite and NaN values are
accepted; one NaN produced an ordinary dashboard with `cost_total=NaN`.
Aggregate only versioned quantities with compatible units and validated finite
domains, expose each metric separately, and report missing/incomparable data.

### MXR-080-1737 — Telemetry persists unrestricted raw content despite its privacy claim

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/telemetry/__init__.py` and `mixle/telemetry/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** package lines 1–9; core lines 35–52 and 73–113
- **State:** Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The package says events are designed to avoid raw user content, but
`features`, `choice`, `outcome` and tags accept and serialize arbitrary caller
objects without schema allowlists, redaction, classification or size limits.
Prompts, answers, credentials and personal data therefore land verbatim in a
long-lived local log through the normal API. Define per-kind schemas with
data-classification and minimization rules, redact/reject sensitive fields
before buffering, and make any explicitly permitted raw payload encrypted,
scoped and retention-governed.

### MXR-080-1738 — String-valued “false” confirms billable pool execution

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 98–137
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The billable gate uses ordinary truthiness rather than requiring literal
Boolean confirmation. Submitting with `confirm="false"` executed a billable
backend and returned its result. This is especially dangerous across JSON,
CLI and form boundaries where Boolean-like strings are common. Require exact
`True` plus a signed, unexpired confirmation token bound to job identity,
backend, quoted maximum cost and immutable input digest; all other values must
remain dry-run/rejected.

### MXR-080-1739 — Realized pool spend can exceed the hard budget without limit

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 23–50 and 98–137
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

Only caller-supplied `est_cost` is compared with `budget`; no reservation,
backend-side ceiling or settlement check constrains actual spend. A job
estimated at `.5` under budget `1` returned `status="done", cost=999` and was
accepted unchanged. Checking after execution would still be too late to
prevent spend. Require a backend-enforced maximum authorization, reserve it
before dispatch, meter actual work, cancel at the ceiling, and reconcile an
authenticated cost receipt.

### MXR-080-1740 — Pool dispatch trusts a result for the wrong job with invalid status economics

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 41–55 and 98–137

`PoolResult` has no invariants and `submit()` returns whatever a backend

and NaN duration for a different budgeted job; the public call accepted it
and `.ok` was true. Validate a closed status enum, exact job/input identity,
finite nonnegative duration/cost, budget settlement and artifact digest/
schema before accepting a backend response.

### MXR-080-1741 — A backend exception escapes the promised result and loses submission evidence

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 58–65 and 98–159
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

The backend protocol promises `submit() -> PoolResult`, but the wrapper does
not isolate backend failures. An injected backend `RuntimeError` propagated
directly; `_emit()` was never reached, so there was no failed-job receipt or
telemetry event. Convert dispatch failures into a structured attempt result
that preserves whether execution may have started and its reconciliation
state, while allowing fatal integrity/policy errors to fail closed explicitly.

### MXR-080-1742 — Retrying the same pool job executes and spends again

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 23–40 and 98–137
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed
- **Fix status (cross-ref, 2026-07-28):** Unverified -- the surface file was changed during this effort, but no commit cites this finding; whether it was addressed has not been checked

There is no idempotency claim, durable job state or result lookup. Submitting
the same `PoolJob(id="same")` twice ran its callable twice and returned
artifacts 1 then 2. A network retry or orchestrator recovery can therefore
duplicate irreversible simulations, training runs, writes or billable work.
Persist an exclusive idempotency key bound to immutable job content and return
the committed prior result—or a typed in-progress conflict—on retry.

### MXR-080-1743 — Telemetry failure is silently erased from an otherwise successful pool result

- **Severity:** High
- **Surface:** `mixle/pool/core.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 136–159
- **State:** Probed/Source-confirmed

`_emit()` catches every exception and discards it. A recorder that always
raised still produced a normal successful `PoolResult` with no field saying
the required audit event was absent. The module's claim that every submission
emits telemetry is therefore untestable at the result boundary. Return a
separate durable audit-delivery status/receipt, queue recoverable telemetry
for retry, and fail closed when policy requires an auditable billable action.

### MXR-080-1744 — Portfolio invariants can be bypassed through aliased public weights

- **Severity:** Critical

- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** 41–77

Construction uses `np.asarray` without copying, and the resulting writable
array remains public. Mutating either the caller's original array or
`portfolio.weights` after successful validation changes the supposedly
invariant belief state. A valid `[0.5, 0.5]` portfolio was changed in place to
`[2, -1]` with `w_open=0`, bypassing every constructor check. Copy weights into
private immutable storage and expose only a read-only snapshot or validated
transition API.

### MXR-080-1745 — Invalid likelihoods are converted into plausible belief and surprise values

- **Severity:** Critical
- **Surface:** `mixle/epistemic/portfolio.py`, `mixle/epistemic/likelihood.py`
- **Lines at clean review snapshot `f477839f`:** `portfolio.py` 85–117 and 186–203; `likelihood.py` 85–94

Neither the callable wrapper nor portfolio operations require a finite,
non-negative likelihood. Two likelihoods of `-1` moved all mass to the
open-world state as though every model merely had zero support.
`surprise_score()` returned `inf`, `-1`, `NaN`, and `0` for likelihoods
`-1`, `-2`, `NaN`, and infinity despite promising a value in `[0,1)`.
Validate each likelihood before any total, normalization, or surprise
